News.title: Paedo who got girl, 15, pregnant is jailed after cops found teen hiding in cupboard as sicko blames ‘stupid immaturity’
News.content:
LOCKED UP Paedo who got girl, 15, pregnant is jailed after cops found teen hiding in cupboard as sicko blames ‘stupid immaturity’

A PAEDOPHILE whose 15-year-old pregnant victim was found by police hiding in a cupboard at his home has been jailed.

Ronan Cambridge, who was 25 at the time, told the officers who arrested him he believed the girl was 17.

They gave him the “benefit of the doubt” but the court heard that he continued to message, meet up and engage in sexual activity with her, despite being told of her real age when he was bailed.

On one occasion, he even told the youngster he needed to bathe in case police wanted to take DNA swabs, Maidstone Crown Court heard.





It was also discovered that the refuse collector was the father of her unborn child.

Cambridge, of Palm Drive, Rochester, later pleaded guilty to meeting a child following sexual grooming, sexual activity with a child, and making indecent images of a child.

At his sentencing hearing on Monday (August 3), prosecutor Daisy Kell-Jones said Cambridge, now 26, was first arrested after police found the girl hiding at his home, having been reported missing.

“He said he thought she was 17 and, with there seeming to be an element of truth to that, he was given the benefit of doubt,” said the prosecutor.

“But he was clearly told she was 15 and was bailed with a condition not to contact her.”

The relationship persisted unabated, however, with “hundreds, if not thousands” of messages exchanged between them across “all sorts” of social media platforms, added Ms Kell-Jones.

They also continued to engage in sexual activity and, on one occasion, he told the girl: “I know you’re 15, but there is something different about you.”

The prosecutor told the court that Cambridge’s messaging demonstrated “an awareness of the illegality” of what was going on.



“He talks about needing to get a bath as he has a feeling police will want to take DNA swabs again,” she explained.

Cambridge, who has no previous convictions, was re-arrested a month later and, despite lying about having no contact with the girl, denying making her pregnant, and refuting giving her an engagement ring, he was again bailed with the same condition of no contact.

Still, Cambridge continued messaging the girl, “telling her he loves her and wants to be there for her” said Ms Kell-Jones.

It was in September last year, notwithstanding his attempts to flee officers by jumping out of a second floor window, that he was apprehended for a third and final time.

On being detained, he said: “I’m trying to save myself because I’m on f***ing bail.”



His phone, found under a mattress in his bedroom, was seized and analysed with explicit photos and videos of the girl on the device.

When interviewed, he accepted the footage had been created while he was on bail.

Harriet Snookes, defending, told the court Cambridge had been told “from the outset” the girl was 17 and shown a birth certificate in support.

But she said he blamed his “stupid immaturity” for maintaining contact once he knew her to be underage.

“He accepts the relationship continued and it shouldn’t have,” she added. “He says this was a stupid error of judgement and knows he shouldn’t have remained in contact with her.



Cambridge, who has been on remand for 11 months, was told by the judge, Recorder Cairns Nelson KC, that he repeatedly “went right through that red light” of knowing her true age and being bailed with a non-contact condition.

“I have to deal with you for your conduct against a 15-year-old child over a three-month period last year,” said Recorder Nelson.

“This wasn’t a one-off lapse of judgement by an immature person. This was a deliberate, sustained, knowing breach of the law.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cambridge was jailed for a total of four years and 10 months, of which he will serve two-thirds, less time already spent in custody.

He was also made subject to an indefinite sexual harm prevention order and sex offender notification requirements.

News.title: Mom, 22, ‘slit throats of her 3 children’ & told husband ‘say goodbye to your kids’ after his desperate bid to save them
News.content:
A MOM is accused of slashing the throats of her three children, killing two of them and leaving the other seriously injured in a horror attack.

Kailey Erhart, 22, from North Dakota, allegedly carried out the stabbing frenzy on August 6 after chasing her husband and the children’s grandmother out of the house in the rampage, according to authorities.



Cops say her three-year-old and five-month-old daughters died from their injuries.

Erhart’s one-year-old son miraculously survived after undergoing extensive surgeries, though his condition is not known.



When officers arrived, the blood-soaked mom was in the kitchen holding the knife to her throat which she then dropped before begging them to kill her, investigators said in an affidavit seen by Valley News Live.

She was detained and taken into custody by the officers who were left traumatized by the “horrific” scene at the house, Mandan Police Chief Jason Ziegler said at a press conference.

read more on crime CHILLING FIND Son 'gunned down parents in murder-suicide' as strange sound heard from home

“A scene like that is something that nobody should ever have to see, and the way [the officers] came through in one of the most horrific times that they’ll probably experience in their life, I’m proud,” he said.

“I want to acknowledge this is an extreme, tragic and heartbreaking incident for the children involved, their families, our community and first responders who arrived on scene.”

They found the three young children unresponsive on the floor in a bedroom, all with wounds to their necks.

The children’s father, who was already in the process of divorcing Erhart, was at home with the kids and their grandmother at the time before she allegedly chased them both out with the knife and locking the door, according to authorities.



The desperate dad told investigators that before he was chased out of the home, he managed to take a firearm off Erhart, allegedly causing the crazed mother to bite and scratch him.

He told cops he took the weapon apart and scattered the pieces in an apparent attempt last-minute to stop harm from coming to the children.

A video found on his phone from before the attack showed her carrying one of the children while holding a pistol at her hip and telling her husband, “Say goodbye to your children,” per the affidavit.

He had previously reported threats to harm herself and the children which saw Erhart placed in a mental health facility within the last 12 to 18 months, per the affidavit.



She had been put on medication and was discharged and allowed to be with her children when the attack took place, the affidavit states, noting that the CPS was aware of the previous threats.

Erhart now faces nine criminal charges including Class AA felony murder, attempted murder, and aggravated assault.



Her bond has been set at $3 million cash due to “the extreme violence in these alleged charges and the threat to the community, victims, and children,” District Judge Marina Spahr said.

The mother is also blocked from contacting surviving victims or family members and has not yet entered a plea.

According to the affidavit, when questioned in police custody, Erhart said she put the children to bed and believed their throats had been cut before then.

She further claimed not to remember what happened but that she had the knife in her hands when cops arrived.

Erhart is due in court for a preliminary hearing and arraignment on October 6.



A GoFundMe page has been set up by the children’s paternal grandmother Melissa to support her son and surviving grandchild.

“He is a father trying to survive something no parent should ever have to face,” she wrote.

“I lost two precious souls in a devastating tragedy… and the pain is more than I can put into words.”

“Right now, our focus has to be on caring for this child and making it through each day while grieving such heartbreaking loss,” she added.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: Oblivious tourists ignore warnings & pose for photos on edge of crumbling & ‘very fragile’ 400ft cliff in UK beauty spot
News.content:
DANGEROUS DROP Oblivious tourists ignore warnings & pose for photos on edge of crumbling & ‘very fragile’ 400ft cliff in UK beauty spot

TOURISTS have been blasted after people were seen posing for photos on the edge of a crumbling cliff with a 400ft drop.

Selfie-loving visitors were standing just inches from the edge of the “fragile” chalk cliffs in Birling Gap, East Sussex.



The cliffs are “very fragile and can collapse without warning” said the National Trust, who manage the popular beauty spot.

This follows a similar warning for nearby viewpoint Seaford Head which is also part of the famed white Seven Sisters cliffs.



Some 600,000 walkers head to the trail with constant sightseeing tours enjoying the dramatic coastline.

However, the soft chalk is riddled with deep tension cracks and huge sections regularly break away and crash onto the beach below.



Janice Dykes, of the National Coastwatch, told the BBC: “It might look like a lovely walk from the top, but they can’t know what is under their feet from the top.”

She added: “Some cracks can be 10m (32.8ft) or 15m (49.2ft) long.”



Visitors are urged to stay at least five metres back from the edge while taking in the views.

Despite that, people were seen venturing dangerously close for photographs.

The local council has urged tourists to take care as the edge is “extremely unstable”.

A spokesperson for East Sussex County Council said: “Every year, thousands of tons of chalk falls from the cliffs.

“Despite warning signs, people often stand near the edge. Chalk cliffs are extremely unstable and can fall at any time.



“People underestimate the risks they are taking.”

The danger has become so severe that even the nearby Seaford Head Golf Course is being forced to change its layout.

Parts of the historic links course sit beside the eroding cliff edge and repeated collapses have left golfers playing dangerously close to the drop.

Early this year the coastguard was called to rescue nine people and a dog from Birling Gap beach after a section of the cliffs collapsed.

The group were left stranded after the stairs down to the beach were damaged by the cliff fall.



Both families and the dog were winched to safety after the collapse in January.

News.title: Daniel Kinahan officially arrested after landing back in Ireland for 1st time in decade on Govt jet from Dubai
News.content:
ALLEGED crime boss Daniel Kinahan has touched down on Irish soil for the first time in over a decade.

The 49-year-old has been arrested on the tarmac at Casement Aerodrome, Baldonnel, and will be brought to the Special Criminal Court.



The Irish Government’s Dassault Falcon 6X departed Dubai World Central International Airport at around 10.20am this morning and landed shortly after 6:30pm.

In a statement after the jet’s landing, gardai confirmed that a man has been arrested and charged in relation to serious organised crime offences.



They said: “The male was arrested in the United Arab Emirates on foot of an arrest warrant issued by the Irish Courts. He was extradited following a judicial process there.



“His extradition was in accordance with the bi-lateral agreement on extradition between Ireland and United Arab Emirates. The extradition was facilitated by the logistical support of the Irish Air Corps.”



Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly said: “This arrest shows our determination, along with our international policing partners including Dubai Police, to target transnational organised crime groups.

“It also shows the value of our relationship with the authorities in the United Arab Emirates, the Ministry of Justice at judicial level, and on a police-to-police basis.

“This relationship has been supported by the Irish Government’s Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration and Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.”

Flying at 45,000 ft, the jet with a registration of IRL290 flew west over Saudi Arabia before turning north towards Ireland.



Armed officers are expected to be on patrol around Dublin’s Criminal Courts of Justice.

Snipers from the Gardai’s Emergency Response Unit have also been deployed in the area as part of the operation.

And members of the ERU and National Drugs and Organised Crime Bureau are expected to be on alert inside.

The building has already been swept for bombs and staff there were instructed to take home their bags to avoid any security scares.



Today, authorities in Ireland and the UAE released a joint statement welcoming Kinahan’s extradition.

Referring to him only as an “Irish national”, the statement said he is “regarded as one of the most high-profile individuals sought for prosecution in connection with transnational organised crime”.



Minister for Justice Jim O’Callaghan said: “I would like to express Ireland’s deep appreciation for the support of the United Arab Emirates in handling the extradition request, and commend the professionalism, efficiency, and diligence demonstrated by the UAE judicial authorities throughout the extradition proceedings.

“This decision is another landmark of judicial cooperation between the two countries and reflects the strength of our partnership to address transnational organised crime.”

Abdullah bin Sultan bin Awad Al Nuaimi, Minister of Justice of the UAE, added that the country was committed to “further strengthening judicial cooperation with Irish authorities”.

Taoiseach Micheal Martin today paid “a very strong tribute” to Gardai, the Garda Commissioner and successive Ministers for Justice for tackling organised crime in a “very effective way”.

Speaking at the Tullamore Show, he did not directly comment on the case, but said Gardai deserved “real credit” for their efforts more generally.



In a statement, Minister of Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee said today is the “culmination of years of determined work” by Gardai and successive Governments.

She paid tribute in particular to the late former Garda Assistant Commissioner John O’Driscoll and former Garda Commissioner Drew Harris for their efforts to tackle organised crime.

Daniel Kinahan was last seen on the Emerald Isle on February 15, 2016, at David Byrne’s funeral.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Byrne was shot dead at the Regency Hotel ten days beforehand in an attack which started the Kinahan-Hutch gang war.

Prior to being handed over to Irish authorities as part of his extradition process, Kinahan had claimed: “I’m looking forward to getting home.”

News.title: Pilot blinded by laser and forced to abort landing flight with 159 passengers on board as police open up probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SKY-HIGH CHAOS Pilot blinded by laser and forced to abort landing flight with 159 passengers on board as police open up probe

A MALAYSIA Airlines flight was forced to abort its landing after a laser beam was shone directly into the cockpit.

Flight MH-184, travelling from Kuala Lumpur to Kolkata, was due to touch down at around 11.20pm on Saturday.



But the pilot was forced to delay the landing after being dazzled by the powerful beam.

The pilot reportedly spotted the bright light while the aircraft was still around eight nautical miles from the runway.



The sudden glare briefly left him disorientated, meaning the plane could not land as planned.

Instead, he was forced to circle in the air until it was safe to make another approach.



The aircraft eventually touched down at around 11.25pm, just five minutes behind schedule.

There were 159 passengers on board at the time, with all passengers and crew confirmed safe.

Kolkata airport bosses have since filed a report with police over the incident.

An investigation is now underway to establish exactly what happened.



Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said the use of laser lights around the airport is prohibited, but warned that such incidents do occur occasionally.

Aviation experts say that lasers aimed at aircraft during take-off and landing can be extremely dangerous.

The intense light can temporarily impair a pilot’s vision, causing severe distraction or effects similar to short-term blindness during the most critical stages of a flight.

It is not the first time aircraft operating in and out of Kolkata airport have been targeted by laser beams.

During the 2025 Durga Puja festivities, laser lights used near the Sreebhumi Sporting Club pandal reportedly raised concerns among pilots.



The laser show was subsequently stopped.

In a separate incident on Sunday, a private training aircraft crashed near Baramati airfield in Maharashtra’s Pune district.

Authorities said the crash happened at around 12.30pm and confirmed there were no casualties.

News.title: Man, 20, charged with murder after fatal stabbing of 32-year-old in Birmingham as detectives make plea to witnesses
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

MURDER CHARGE Man, 20, charged with murder after fatal stabbing of 32-year-old in Birmingham as detectives make plea to witnesses

A 20-YEAR-OLD has been charged with murder after a man was fatally stabbed in Birmingham.

Emergency services were called to an address in Chester Road, Sutton, near Oscott College, shortly after midnight on Saturday, August 8.



Joseph Cargill, 20, of Chester Road, Sutton Coldfield, has been charged with murdering Stephen Clarke, aged 32.

Cops said a man, Mr Clarke, had been “stabbed” and sadly died at the scene.



Officers have continued to investigate the incident on Sunday, August 9, with a CCTV specialist on site at the address to gather footage, accompanied by detectives.

And Cargill has been charged with murder and is set to appear before magistrates in Birmingham on Monday, August 10, morning.

Despite the charge, police are still appealing for witnesses to come forward.

A spokesperson for the West Midlands Police:said “We have charged a man with murder following the death of a man in Birmingham this weekend.



“Joseph Cargill, 20, was charged today after Stephen Clarke, who was 32, was fatally stabbed in Chester Road in the early hours of Saturday morning.

“Cargill was remanded in custody to appear before magistrates in Birmingham tomorrow morning (Monday).”

The statement continued: “Our investigation into the incident continues and we are keen to hear from anyone who was in the area at the time.

“Mr Clarke’s family have requested their privacy be respected at this time.

“If you know anything, get in touch via 101 quoting crime number 20/355036/26.”



The suspect and victim are believed to have been known to each other.



Cops previously said they are no longer looking for anyone else in connection with the man’s death.

News.title: Man fighting for his life after being attacked by ‘gang of 6’ outside takeaway as two teens, 16 & 14, arrested
News.content:
STREET ASSAULT Man fighting for his life after being attacked by ‘gang of 6’ outside takeaway as two teens, 16 & 14, arrested

A MAN has been left fighting for his life after he was allegedly attacked outside a takeaway by a gang of six as two teens are arrested.

The victim, who is in his 30s, remains in a critical condition after he was reportedly assaulted on Park Road in Dingle, Liverpool, just before 10pm.

An electric bike was reportedly used in the assault and has been taken by officers.

A 16-year-old boy from Wavertree has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent.





Police also arrested a 14-year-old boy from Dingle was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent.

A police presence remained at the scene to carry out CCTV and forensic work.

Detective Inspector Gemma Ellerton said: “Although we have arrested two males in connection with the incident, we continue to make enquiries into what took place to ensure those involved are held to account.

“We understand the concern that such an incident will cause, especially given the ages of those involved and the busy area in which this occurred.

“With this I urge people in the area who saw the incident, or suspect a young person you know of having been involved, to please come forward and check any devices which may hold images or footage leading up to the assault.

“Any information no matter how small, may help the investigation.”

The force have urged anyone with information to make themselves known through social media with reference 26000647138.

A spokesperson said: “Just before 10pm it was reported that a group of six males assaulted a man outside a takeaway shop on Park Road and used an electric bike in the attack.



“The victim, a man in his 30s, was taken to hospital where he is in a critical condition.

“Officers attended the scene and arrested two males. The electric bike believed to have been used in the assault has also been seized.

“A 16-year-old male from Wavertree was arrested on suspicion of Section 18 grievous bodily harm with intent.

“A 14-year-old male from Dingle was arrested on suspicion of Section 18 wounding with intent.

“They are both still in police custody for questioning.



“Officers remain in the area to carry out witness, CCTV and forensic work.”

News.title: If you want to stop the boats, show migrants our potholes, planning laws and A&E waiting times, Jeremy Clarkson says
News.content:
JEREMY Clarkson thinks he has the solution to solving the migrant boat crisis – start showing them some of the most hated things about the UK.

The TV presenter, 66, says Britain should try and look closer to home for a quick-fire solution and stop taking on France and the Channel migrants through force and wasted deals.



It might be popular to imagine our warships out in water defending the realm but the star of Clarkson’s Farm believes this just appeals to the Tommy Robinson types.

Writing in his column for The Sunday Times, he said: “You’ve got to make the UK less appealing than where they are now, which is France.”



This, he thinks, shouldn’t be too hard to accomplish.

He added: “Show them our potholes and explain that there are vast areas of the UK with such c**p mobile phone coverage they’d be better off communicating with two empty tins and a piece of string.

“Tell them that because of our planning laws, everyone is forced to operate their business from a shipping container and that children with suspected meningitis are forced to wait five hours in A&E before they can see a doctor.”

He has other ways of how his goal could be achieved, these include showing them just how badly our rivers are polluted and revealing how much tax they’ll have to pay if they either get a job or die.

Another way, Mr Clarkson says would work, would be to highlight the 20mph speed limit on our roads.

Not forgetting a trip to a court in the UK where they can see someone being prosecuted for something they posted on social media.



Finally, he thinks, showing a migrant our farmland so they can see the empty fields and tell them that even then if they still want to come here then, as he puts it, “you can’t have any effing money”.

Previously, Mr Clarkson took aim at young people on benefits who “sat at home all day”.

He said youths on benefits should offer gratitude to the taxpayers who support them.

Going on, Clarkson explains that he would be happy with further tax raids to pay for a growing welfare bill in exchange for heartfelt thank you notes from people claiming benefits.

He suggests giving the email address of a working person to people claiming benefits and ensuring a thank you letter is sent to them.



His tongue-in-cheek suggestion comes as analysis revealed some teens on sickness benefits receive around £100 a week more than others working part-time on minimum wage.

News.title: Coroner calls for NHS 111 changes after woman dies from head injury following 'downplayed' fall
News.content:
Coroner calls for NHS 111 changes after woman dies from head injury following 'downplayed' fall

Christine Clegg, 79, died after an unwitnessed fall, which caused a traumatic brain injury, at Kesteven Grange Care Home in Hull, East Yorkshire with the wrong NHS 111 script used to assess her injuries

View 2 Images A coroner has called for changes to the NHS 111 script after a woman died of a head injury after a fall (STOCK) (Image: PA)

A coroner has called for changes to NHS 111 call scripts following the death of a woman after a "downplayed" fall at a care home.

‌



Christine Clegg, 79, passed away following an unwitnessed fall which resulted in a traumatic brain injury at Kesteven Grange Care Home in Hull, East Yorkshire, in June 2025. Following the conclusion of an inquest into her death earlier this year, assistant coroner Sally Robinson has raised concerns that the NHS 111 script used after the fall meant Mrs Clegg did not receive immediate clinical treatment.

‌



When a carer discovered her on the floor, a call was placed to 111 and a staff member described Mrs Clegg as having "put herself on the floor" and having a "bump" on her head.

‌



View 2 Images Despite having an actively bleeding head injury, Christine was assessed as though she had minor cuts and grazes (STOCK) (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Call handlers follow scripts determined by the information they are given. The caller script for "scratches, grazes or minor wounds" can be applied to head injuries, which resulted in the "wrong script" being used in Mrs Clegg's case.

‌



In a prevention of future deaths report, Ms Robinson wrote: "The situation appears to have (been) downplayed and information passed to the operator which was biased information, suggesting Mrs Clegg had placed herself on the floor when in fact she had fallen from a bed, and which caused the wrong script to be followed by the operator.

"The head injury was actively bleeding and the script which should have been followed was that of head injury, but instead, because of the information given by the care staff, the script which was followed was the scratches, grazes or minor wounds pathway. This resulted in a different outcome to the one the correct pathway was likely to recommend, which was to seek clinician input."

Had the operator utilised the "head, facial or neck injury" script, the outcome would have directed the carers to "speak to a clinician" regardless of the responses given. Instead, the call concluded without any clinical involvement, merely basic first aid guidance, and Mrs Clegg subsequently suffered a traumatic subdural haemorrhage, the coroner noted.

Article continues below

Mrs Clegg's condition worsened over the following days, ultimately resulting in her hospitalisation, where she passed away. The report has been forwarded to Yorkshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust and NHS Pathways, recommending that all head injuries be excluded from the "scratches, grazes and nicks" script.

Ms Robinson wrote: "If injuries above the neck were excluded from the scratches, grazes and nicks pathway then the possibility of basic first aid advice being given is eliminated, as all head injury answered, result in clinician advice being sought."

Kesteven Grange Care Home has been approached for comment.

News.title: Nottinghamshire Fire declare major incident as crews battle two giant woodland fires
News.content:
Nottinghamshire Fire declare major incident as crews battle two giant woodland fires

Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident at 1.30pm on Sunday while 14 crews tackle two separate wildfires near Mansfield,warning that response times to further incidents are likely to be delayed

View 2 Images Almost half of Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue's appliances have been deployed to tackle the two blazes (Image: Nottinghamshire Live / BPM Media)

A fire service has declared a major incident after two substantial blazes in woodland areas have placed enormous pressure on resources during hot and dry weather.

‌



Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident at 1.30pm on Sunday as 14 crews battle two separate fires near Mansfield. A blaze ignited at Strawberry Hill Heath at around 2pm on Saturday, with 12 crews fighting the fire at its peak, Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed.

‌



Eight fire engines remain on site, while six others and a water carrier have been dispatched to combat a second fire that broke out at Sherwood Pines on Sunday.

‌



View 2 Images Around 36,000 square metres of woodland and undergrowth have been destroyed in the Strawberry Hill Heath fire (Image: Nottinghamshire Live / BPM Media)

The fire service stated: "As of 1.30 pm, Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service has declared a major incident. This relates to the cumulative impact of multiple incidents placing significant pressure on operational resources, rather than a single incident in isolation.

"The service is currently operating with very limited resources and reduced pump availability. As a result, response times to any further incidents are likely to be delayed."

‌



The public has been urged to steer clear of the area, while residents affected by smoke have been advised to keep their doors and windows shut. "Still call 999 in an emergency," Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service added.

"We would like to remind people not to light any fires, such as campfires or BBQs, and to take extra care when disposing of cigarettes due to the incredibly dry conditions, as a spark could spread quickly."

Approximately 36,000 square metres of woodland and undergrowth have been ravaged by the blaze at Strawberry Hill Heath, with Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service confirming on Sunday that crews were anticipated to remain on site "for several more hours".

‌



Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service operates 24 fire stations throughout the county with 30 fire engines. This means almost half of their fire appliances are currently deployed at the wildfire locations.

Scorching temperatures continued to intensify on Sunday, with southern and south-eastern regions of England braced for the highest readings. The Met Office warned that heatwave conditions are likely to return next week, with temperatures potentially reaching 36C across parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday.

According to the Fire Severity Index, any wildfires are likely to be exceptionally severe on Sunday across nearly all of eastern and south-east England. "Exceptional" severity represents its highest classification.

Article continues below

The Met Office data incorporates rainfall, temperature and humidity figures, which agencies utilise to evaluate the potential intensity of any fire that breaks out. It does not, however, indicate the likelihood of wildfires starting.

News.title: UK drought warnings explained as Brits could face emergency measures not used in 50 years
News.content:
UK drought warnings explained as Brits could face emergency measures not used in 50 years

Britain's contingency plans for severe drought would see standpipes set up in the street and mains water cut off at certain times of day - a state of emergency last seen in the summer of 1976

View 4 Images Residents in the worst-hit areas were forced to use standpipes (Image: Mirrorpix)

Households could face having their mains water cut off and be forced to use standpipes in the street under Britain's emergency drought plans.

‌



Half of England is currently in an official state of drought, with much of the rest of the country classed as experiencing 'severe dry weather'. More than 20 million people in the UK are meanwhile living in an areas covered hosepipe bans - with forecasters warning that yet another heatwave is on the way this week.

‌



But we're not yet at the highest 'red' level of warning, severe drought, which was last activated in the famous summer of 1976. Memorable scenes saw people relying on standpipes for all of their water, strict water rationing introduced, and taps running dry for much of the day.

‌



View 4 Images The last time a severe drought warning was issued - the famous summer of 1976 (Image: Getty Images)

England transformed into barren Western-like frontier as dramatic photos capture horror extent of drought READ MORE :

‌



British food items at risk due to extreme drought - and what shortages could mean for you READ MORE :

How does Britain's drought warning system work?

The Environment Agency uses four levels of drought warning to communicate levels of risk to the public, which are:

Prolonged dry weather: Water levels are falling, and the public is encouraged to limit water use before official restrictions are needed.

Water levels are falling, and the public is encouraged to limit water use before official restrictions are needed. Drought: There is a shortage of water affecting water supplies, farming, and wildlife. Water companies implement temporary use (hosepipe bans) for households, while environmental teams may also intervene to rescue distressed wildlife, or move water locally to safeguard habitats.

There is a shortage of water affecting water supplies, farming, and wildlife. Water companies implement temporary use (hosepipe bans) for households, while environmental teams may also intervene to rescue distressed wildlife, or move water locally to safeguard habitats. Severe drought: Emergency infrastructure and contingency plans are implemented. Authorities are given the power shut off mains water and to implement 'rota cuts', which sees water turned on and off at different times of the day to manage supply. Communal street standpipes or mobile water tanks may be introduced, forcing residents to queue and carry their daily water rations back to their homes.

Emergency infrastructure and contingency plans are implemented. Authorities are given the power shut off mains water and to implement 'rota cuts', which sees water turned on and off at different times of the day to manage supply. Communal street standpipes or mobile water tanks may be introduced, forcing residents to queue and carry their daily water rations back to their homes. Recovery from drought: Issued after significant rainfall, this sees water restrictions and monitoring continue until reservoirs have fully replenished to safe levels.

View 4 Images Residents of Bideford, Devon using standpipes during the historic severe drought 50 years ago (Image: Popperfoto/Getty Images)

‌



What happens when a severe drought warning is issued?

Severe droughts are the point at which a drought truly becomes a national emergency - and they are rare. The government was last forced to raise the warning to this level in 1976, when an extraordinarily dry summer came at the end of 16 months of below average rainfall.

Along with the disruption to household water supplies, this measure also allows water companies to take more water from rivers and underground aquifers than usual, or reduce the amount they are legally required to release back into rivers from reservoirs. During the historic 1976 severe drought, the crisis became so severe that Prime Minister Harold Wilson appointed a Minister for Drought, Denis Howell, and launched massive public information campaigns urging people to share baths and place bricks in their toilet cisterns to save water.

View 4 Images Hanningfield Reservoir in Essex is one of many in Britain where water levels are currently low (Image: NEIL HALL/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



In some of the worst-hit areas, such southwest England, North Wales and Yorkshire, residents relied entirely on street standpipes for their water supply for several weeks as reservoirs dropped to unprecedented levels.

Should we expect a severe drought warning this summer?

The Environment Agency has not indicated that it is expecting to issue a warning for severe drought, with the most affected areas currently under a drought warning. Meteorologists have observed that unlike previous droughts in the UK, which typically follow several months of low rainfall, this summer has had the hallmarks of a 'flash drought' - where dry weather comes suddenly, and to a more extreme extent.

Article continues below

July was the driest month in southern England since records began nearly 200 years ago.

News.title: Three injured in shooting in Denmark as police arrest man
News.content:
Three injured in shooting in Denmark as police arrest man

Police have arrested a man after three people were injured in a shooting incident in the town of Holbaek in eastern Denmark

View Image Danish police have responded to the incident (file photo) (Image: Henning Bagger/Ritzau Scanpix Fo)

Three people have been injured in a town centre shooting, as police have arrested a man.

‌



The attack took place in the Danish town of Holbæk, local police have said, with several people struck by gunfire. Police received the report around 3:45 pm local time (2:45pm UK time).

‌



According to witnesses, a large group of people had gathered at Agervang in Holbæk and started fighting shortly before Sunday's shooting, Danish media reports.

‌



Shortly afterwards, a small white car arrived, and shots were fired. The car drove away, after which a man tried to drive after it. The man had an accident shortly afterwards and has now been arrested while the police investigate his role. However Deputy Police Inspector Lars Krogsgaard has said police are working on the assumption that he was part of the group that was shot at.

Pictures from the scene show that the police have cordoned off a large area after the shooting. There are also police dogs at the crime scene.

Article continues below

Danish police have described the incident as a "settling of scores". In a statement on X the force said: "Police are currently present at several locations in Holbæk following a shooting where several people have been hit. It is the police's assumption that this is a settling of scores in the criminal environment."

They added: "Police received a report of the shooting around 3:45 p.m. It occurred in the Agervang residential area."

News.title: Samantha Morton on 'special' role, as she's tipped for an Oscar after just 10 mins in The Odyssey
News.content:
She appears for barely ten minutes of a three-hour film, yet Samantha Morton, who began her working life as a magician's assistant, has cast the spell everyone is talking about this summer. The 49-year-old actress has emerged as a surprise contender for next year's Best Supporting Actress Oscar for her turn as the sorceress Circe in Christopher Nolan's hit The Odyssey.

The Nottingham-born actress reads Circe not as the villain of Homer's poem, but as a woman punished by history for what she knew rather than what she did. "I think that women in history have often been vilified, whether you're a midwife, a wise woman," Samantha tells The Arts Hour on the BBC World Service.

"We think about kind of the burning of women at the stake, because they were herbalists, you know, and I don't think Circe is a baddie at all."

Shania Twain turned into £300m country music legend by very unexpected hit READ MORE :

Her interpretation, she says, came straight off the page, and she wanted Circe to be far more than just a villain. She adds: "Villains are always amazing roles, but I did want to make her a little bit more. My interpretation was what I read on the script, which was phenomenal, and it was multi-layered, because we are, as humans; we're not just two-dimensional."

‌



View 6 Images Anne Hathaway, Lupita Nyong'o, Charlize Theron, Zendaya, and Samantha Morton attend the premiere of The Odyssey on July 14, 2026 (Image: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Universal Pictures)

"There's been so many interpretations of this woman, this sorceress, witch. But I think that Chris's [Christopher Nolan’s] interpretation of her felt very contemporary to me, without being disrespectful to the original story poem because, in literature, she's often seen as a bit of a baddie, isn't she?"

Samantha’s co-stars in The Odyssey include Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong'o, Zendaya and Charlize Theron. She has shared sets with even bigger names over the years, but says the company has never once fazed her. She continues: "I've worked with some of those big names before, whether it's Tom Cruise, Johnny Depp, Sean Penn, Philip Seymour Hoffman, Joaquin Phoenix.

"My history is that I can, you know … Nottingham lass can hold her own. I'm not intimidated by anybody really, because if you let those nerves get in the way you can't do your job. So I think the nerves affect your performance as an actor. I don't get nervous on set, I'm just so excited to be there. My heart is going like that because it's a real film camera."

‌



View 6 Images Samantha Morton in The Odyssey, for which she has been tipped for an Oscar (Image: PUBLICITY PICTURE)

The Odyssey was shot on 70mm IMAX cameras, built specially for the production, and the format left her giddy. Samantha, who lives in East Sussex with her partner, filmmaker Harry Holm, says: "Whether you're working on 35mm or, in this case, it was 70mm IMAX, which they built specially for the film, it's just I'm buzzing like a kid in a sweet shop.”

That confidence had been hard won, during a Nottingham childhood of care orders and foster homes that she revisited on a podcast earlier this year. "I was taken into care as a baby," she said. Her parents could not cope, her father was in and out of prison and she moved with him between home and the care system - never settling anywhere for long. By 16, she was living alone in a homeless hostel, and it was there that she wrote her first play.

A drama workshop leader gave her the train fare to London to audition for a television part, and within the week she had the role, an agent and her breakthrough in Band of Gold. "Acting saved my life," she said.

‌



View 6 Images Harry Holm, Theodore Morton, and Samantha Morton (Image: Getty Images for Universal Pictures)

The child who ran away into acting is now among the names Oscar pundits expect to hear when the supporting nominations are read out, with The Odyssey closing on a billion dollars worldwide and her odds shortening by the week.

Nolan has said her performance of Circe stopped the set, and that after one of her takes the crew broke into a great round of applause. The only other time he had seen that, he said, was with Heath Ledger on The Dark Knight, and Ledger won a posthumous Oscar in 2009.

Critics have called her Circe the standout of a film wall to wall with stars, with one writing that she runs away with the whole picture; another that a long overlooked actress had finally been handed a role worthy of her.

‌



View 6 Images Tom Cruise and Samantha Morton in the Minority Report report (Image: CBS via Getty Images)

Her co-star felt it on the day. Matt Damon said she was so locked in that she carried the pair of them with her, and that shooting their scenes together, "we all knew we were watching something special."

She reached back into her teenage training as a magician’s assistant for the sequence in which Circe meets Odysseus's shipwrecked men, a scene built with practical effects rather than computers. Should the Oscar come, Samantha - who has three children, Esme, 26, Edie, 18, and Theodore, 18 - would be in select company.

Anthony Hopkins won Best Actor for just over 16 minutes as Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs. Dame Judi Dench took Best Supporting Actress for around eight minutes as Elizabeth I in Shakespeare in Love and Beatrice Straight won the same prize in 1976 for little more than five minutes in Network.

‌



View 6 Images Sean Penn as Emmet Ray and Samantha Morton as Hattie in Sweet and Lowdown. (Image: Getty Images)

Samantha has been nominated twice before, for Sweet and Lowdown in 2000 and In America in 2004, but the years in between have not always been kind. Morton has said Harvey Weinstein once called her "unf***able", and that turning down the 2000 Miramax film About Adam, which she found sexist, left her frozen out for years afterwards.

When she refused, she said, a casting director warned her that ‘you do not say no to Harvey.’ But the disgraced producer is now serving a long prison sentence for sex crimes. And she has never looked back. "At the end of the day, I'm 49. I do believe I'm a good actor," she said. "There are other good actors out there."

For all the Oscar talk, she said the reward was the work itself, and a place in something built to last. She added: "Being part of something that's bigger than any individual is really important in this day and age, because we're living in the age of the I, the me, the Instagram, the selfie, the ego. And The Odyssey is the opposite of that."

‌



*This interview can be heard in full on The Arts Hour, available on BBC Sounds.

News.title: Postman makes desperate plea over 1 thing people do when answering the door
News.content:
Postman makes desperate plea over 1 thing people do when answering the door

Postal workers and delivery drivers have a sometimes thankless job. And now one postman has revealed something shocking some people do when they answer the door

View Image Where would we be without our postmen and women? (Stock image) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Where would we be without Britain's army of postmen and women? Whether you need something urgently, or you've just been on an online shopping spree, they're there rain or shine - and almost always in shorts.

‌



But now one postman has said some people could be a lot more considerate when the doorbell rings. It's natural to be dressed comfortably in your own home, maybe in pyjamas and a dressing gown.

‌



But postman Reece Petch is pleading with people to make sure they are fully clothed when the doorbell rings. Reece frequently documents his delivery experiences on social media, and has revealed he sometimes sees more than he wants to when the door opens, reports the Express.

‌



Beginning his video, Reece stated: "We need to talk some serious business right now, ok? I made a video a few months ago talking about, I don't really care what you come to the door in.

"A lot of people feel insecure about wearing their pyjamas, or wearing their comfy clothes when they come to the door, and that's really stupid. You should never feel like that."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



However, he clarified, that doesn't grant complete freedom regarding door-answering attire - or, in certain instances, lack thereof. "I'd be lying if I said some people don't come to the door in nothing," he stated.

He added: "There is this woman who, no matter what time of day I deliver to her, she always answers the door in underwear. Even in the winter.

"She's always done it, and I've just never really, like, thought about it, but [I] delivered to her in the afternoon and she's still doing it, only she does it in the morning. And I'm like, you gonna put some trousers on? Some joggers, some pyjamas, anything? Or you just gonna stand there just like, 'woohey!'".

‌



And she's not the only person who gives Reece quite a fright when answering the door. "There is an old guy that we deliver to, and he genuinely just comes to the door just b***-naked, nothing on at all," he revealed. "[There have been] times where he has come to the door in, like, a t-shirt and just nothing below. He literally looked like Winnie the Pooh. But a common occurrence, apparently, on my delivery route."

He concluded his video with an appeal, saying: "If I deliver to you, please don't answer the door naked. Just for everyone's sake."

Is it illegal to answer the door naked?

There is no law in the UK against answering the door naked, or semi-clothed. In fact, In fact, it is legal to be naked anywhere in the UK, even in public.

Article continues below

However, indecent exposure - intentionally exposing your genitals in a way likely to cause alarm or distress - is illegal, explains Tyler Hoffman Solicitors. This can apply even if someone is naked in their own home, as the act may have been seen by someone outside, been committed against someone else in the home, or have been shared online.

The key difference between indecent exposure and public nudity is the intent. If the intent was to be seen and cause alarm or distress, this is likely to qualify as indecent exposure. Accidentally exposing yourself is generally not treated as indecent exposure.

People convicted of indecent exposure can be jailed for up to two years and be placed on the sex offenders register. Fines or community service may also be imposed, along with court orders or restraining orders.

News.title: How weight-loss medication is changing relationships with alcohol
News.content:
There is a growing body of research into the link between weight-loss drugs and alcohol consumption.

The drugs, with brands including Wegovy, Mounjaro and Ozempic, contain semaglutide or tirzepatide, which mimic a natural hormone called GLP-1. This suppresses appetite and keeps people feeling fuller for longer, helping them to lose weight.

Early research suggests that because these drugs affect the reward response in the brain, they can reduce cravings for substances including alcohol and nicotine, says Dr Christian Hendershot of the University of South Carolina.

He published a small-scale study, external in 2025 in which participants with alcohol use disorder craved alcohol less while taking Ozempic. Alcohol use disorder, sometimes referred to as alcoholism, is described by the NHS as drinking in a way that is harmful.

A study, external from the University of Colorado Anschutz published last week also suggested that GLP-1 medications in pill form led to fewer days of heavy drinking in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder.

People taking the drugs told BBC News that alcohol had affected them in different ways: some said their cravings for it had gone, drinking had made them feel nauseous or uncomfortably full, or they had got drunk more quickly. Others said they had not noticed any effect on their relationship with alcohol.

Before she started taking Wegovy, Lisa says she drank between six and eight bottles of wine a week with friends. But she had sometimes worried about whether this was too much and whether it could damage her health.

NHS guidance, external is that people should not drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis, which is about six medium glasses of wine or six pints. Drinking too much in the long term can lead to liver damage, high blood pressure and increased risk of cancer.

Lisa says that since starting on the medication she has more than halved her consumption. At a recent day festival, she drank three glasses of wine over the course of nine hours. Previously, she would have had two bottles plus a couple of vodka mixers, she says.

Alcohol has always been a big part of her social life and when she stopped drinking for a few weeks in the late 2010s, she realised friends had stopped inviting her to social events. It led her to start drinking again.

This time round, Lisa says that she still looks forward to drinking wine, but after having a couple of glasses she simply cannot stomach any more.

"I still feel involved in things because I'm still drinking but drinking a lot less," Lisa says.

For years, Warren Thomas, 45, from Colchester, had enjoyed an occasional beer with his family after work, as well as one or two heavy drinking sessions with his friends each month.

But when he spoke to his friends on weight-loss medication about his plans to start taking Mounjaro, they warned him that it could affect how much he drank.

Warren says he noticed the effect within 24 hours of his first dose in mid-June. "I just don't want to drink," he says. "I've just got no appetite for it."

When he went out for his friend's birthday last month, he felt "light-headed and a little bit giddy" after two beers, he says.

"My tolerance level to drinking is now zero," he says.

There is no formal advice in the British National Formulary, a guide to dispensing medicine used by doctors and pharmacists, about whether people on weight-loss drugs should stop drinking alcohol, says Prof Russell Hearn, a GP and professor of medicine at King's College London.

But he gives careful advice to his patients. "Alcohol has a lot of calories in it and if your goal is to lose weight, drinking less will definitely help you with that alongside changing your diet while you're on a GLP-1," he says.

For people like Lisa and Warren, drinking less alcohol has been a happy bonus. But recent graduate Faye Goodwin, 20, feels that it has hampered her social life.

When Faye drinks she says she gets nauseous very quickly and sometimes throws up or gets bad acid reflux.

Faye, who got in touch with BBC Your Voice, has been taking Mounjaro since she was 18 and does not really know what it is like to drink alcohol without the impact of weight-loss medication. But she says she once took a month off the jabs and was able to drink without experiencing any nausea.

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

Banksy, who emerged from Bristol's graffiti scene in the 1990s and became one of the world's most famous street artists, is known for murals and installations that often appear overnight and attract large crowds.

The latest costs relate to a mural depicting a judge in a wig battering a protester with his gavel, which appeared on the Royal Courts of Justice in London on 8 September 2025.

Banksy claimed the image as his own work, by posting it on his website and Instagram account.

News.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
News.content:
After wildfires caused more damage in France this year than at any time since World War Two, many are left asking a single question: why?

A major driver is that climate is changing as a result of the well-documented way humanity is burning fossil fuels. Temperatures are only rising.

But with records showing that nine out of 10 French wildfires are started by humans, the government in Paris is trying to attribute blame - although it is itself accused of being underprepared for the infernos that have now scorched more than 300,000 acres this summer.

The interior ministry has announced 420 arrests of people alleged to have either started the fires deliberately or by accident. Among them are 166 minors.

In one case, a 23-year-old man has been accused of deliberately starting 10 fires in the space of five days in the south-eastern Var area last month. He faces 15 years in prison and a â¬150,000 (Â£128,000) fine, if convicted.

Many others have been tried and immediately sentenced, such as a man who received a three-year jail sentence for starting three recent fires in the Raon-L'Ãtape forest in the Vosges region.

"Only a few square metres of vegetation went up in smoke," noted L'Est RÃ©publicain, the newspaper that reported the story.

Other prosecutions have been perceived as heavy-handed and unjust. A homeless man and someone with severe autism have reportedly been handed jail terms for throwing cigarette butts.

"I was amazed at the number of arrests, it feels excessive," admits Muriel Gestas, a lawyer who has represented several people accused of arson, including two firefighters. She doubts many will lead to a conviction.

The newspaper Le Monde is also unconvinced. It questions to what extent police have examined these cases, given the short time frame.

The authorities' silence on the details - the specific charges, notably whether they involve intent and how the numbers compare with past seasons - rules out any meaningful comparison with previous years, it argues.

But Bordeaux prosecutor Renaud Gaudeul told Le Monde that a tough approach was justified by current circumstances.

"The conditions for a charge of endangering lives are met for those who throw a cigarette butt or light a barbecue in wooded areas. It only takes a tiny spark for it to start," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

News.title: Man arrested after boat capsizes near Statue of Liberty killing woman and infant
News.content:
The operator of a boat that overturned near the Statue of Liberty, killing a woman and a baby, has been arrested and charged with reckless endangerment, New York police said.

Officials said a large search and rescue operation was launched after the incident near New York Harbour on Saturday night.

A nearby vessel rescued 12 people from the water before police arrived, the US Coast Guard (USCG) said.

New York police divers later found a 27-year-old woman and a five-month-old girl, who were transported to a nearby hospital where they later died.

The names of passengers and the specific cause of the incident have not been released.

Around 22:25 local time (03:25 BST), police received a 911 call reporting an overturned boat in the waters near Liberty Island, which houses the iconic statue.

The rescue involved two Coast Guard boats, four fire department boats, two police boats and a police helicopter, the USCG said. The survivors of the incident are all reported to be in stable condition, the agency added.

The investigation into the incident is ongoing, officials said. The boat's operator, a 46-year-old Manhattan resident, faces 13 counts of reckless endangerment, officials said.

Coast Guard investigators are also determining whether the boat was illegally chartered. An illegal charter is any passenger-for-hire vessel operation that does not have required credentials, safety equipment, and certificate of inspection.

"We are extremely grateful for the heroic, swift actions of our partner agencies and Good Samaritan vessel who assisted in rescuing survivors from the water," said Capt Doreen McCarthy of the USCG.

News.title: More areas of UK likely to move into drought as fifth heatwave builds
News.content:
As the hot and dry weather continues for much of the UK, drought status could be declared in additional parts of England this week.

The Environment Agency (EA) has suggested that "several areas" of England could enter drought status as "public water supplies remain under increasing pressure with continued dry weather and high demand".

For the seventh consecutive week, less than 10mm of rain fell across the country, with east and south-east England seeing less than 1mm of rain, according to data from the agency's latest drought summary.

More than half of England and the whole of Wales are already under drought conditions.

Reservoir levels have continued to fall, with almost all across England below normal and five classed as 'exceptionally low', according to the EA.

Wisley in Surrey has gone more than 50 days without a drop of rain. Southern England is approaching two months without any notable rainfall.

Customers of South West Water were the latest to see a hosepipe ban introduced on Saturday.

There are now more than 20 million people in the UK living in an area where prolonged dry weather combined with heatwaves and high demand for water has led to restrictions on usage.

Update: A previous version of this story said that the UK had recorded 35 days of temperatures exceeding 30C, breaking the previous record. As of 9 August, the UK has equalled the 1995 record, with 34 days of temperatures exceeding 30C.

News.title: Israel accused of weaponising archaeology at ancient West Bank sites
News.content:
Up in the hills above the Roman columns of the ancient site of Sebastia, in the occupied West Bank, are olive fields that have been cultivated for generations by Palestinian families.

One of the landowners, Abu Mudif, says he has received notification that his land is part of a tranche of about 450 acres that the Israeli authorities are taking possession of in order, they say, to protect and develop the site for a major new national park.

Typically, Palestinian landowners receive little or no payment for such land expropriation. And even when it is offered, most refuse it as they see accepting it as giving recognition and legitimacy to the loss of what they see as their patrimony.

It's a vital income for Abu Mudif to lose of course, but it goes deeper than that for him.

News.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
News.content:
"Eyes peeled," comes the order from the front passenger seat.

Obediently, we scan the ends and tops of logs, looking between low scrub and patches of vivid wildflowers for a flash of stripes or a dart of movement.

Eluding us is the numbat, a rare Australian marsupial which could be the love-child of a chipmunk and an anteater.

Numbats were once populous across the bottom half of the continent, but Dryandra Woodland â in the south-western corner of Australia â is one of the few places they remain.

As we slowly roll along bush tracks, researchers explain how this annual trip helps plot the species' survival.

Classified as endangered until this month, numbats have been bouncing back. This team's efforts have seen them scratched off the international red list of threatened species - a rare glimmer of hope in a country facing an extinction emergency.

This part of Australia is the front line of that crisis: a last stand for many species driven to the brink by feral pests, disease, urban development, habitat destruction and climate change.

Winging over our car at one point is the endangered Carnaby's cockatoo. On an island just off the coast is one of the last surviving pockets of the world's rarest marsupial, the Gilbert's potoroo. Diving in the sapphire waters around it is the increasingly scarce Australian sea lion.

News.title: Zendaya saw me on the red carpet and her jaw dropped - I'm still in shock
News.content:
"I can't zip this! Mummm?"

This was 29-year-old Zainab Jiwa, calling out for help squeezing into a corset while filming a "get-ready-with-me" TikTok video. It's a scene many 20-somethings still living at home will relate to.

The difference is, Zainab was on her way to the recent London premiere of The Odyssey, one of the summer's biggest blockbusters.

She was invited there as a guest and says she caught the eye of Hollywood megastar Zendaya, thanks to her custom look: a striking gold gown complete with a hood.

"She just walked past, and she saw me there. Her jaw just dropped, so did mine," Zainab tells me.

"It was just a stare-off for a minute, and she was like, 'Oh my god, amazing, amazing,' and then she just walked off."

"Iâm still in shock,â she adds. âThe thought of her noticing my outfit blew my mind."

The interaction went viral, external with 19m TikTok views. Her phone blew up.

While Zendaya has been ruling the red carpets with high-fashion "method dressing" â where stars match outfits to a film's themes â Zainab is perhaps proving that independent creators like her can give Hollywood a run for its money.

Zainab, who is Muslim and wears a hijab, is also often one of the only people covering her hair at premieres, but she says finding ways to incorporate modest wear is part of the fun.

"Even though you're covered, you can still find a way to be on theme.â

News.title: Andy Burnham to embark on cost of living tour through the UK
News.content:
The prime minister is set to announce "a series of measures to make life easier" for those struggling with the cost of living in the coming days, Downing Street says.

No 10 says Andy Burnham's plans are to "give people some room to breathe". He will also focus on ways of "improving high streets" as he embarks on a tour of the UK.

But the government is facing continued pressure over its early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales â with criticism of the fact that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers will be eligible from next year.

Burnham is also likely to face pressure for more action on the cost of living â although significant interventions are unlikely before October's Budget.

Even then, Chancellor John Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

The prime minister has been on holiday this week, but Downing Street said he would be in "listening mode" in the coming days as he tours the UK's nations and regions and works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

A spokesman for the prime minister said: "He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles â like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off â must be accepted as part of life.

"He doesn't think that's right. That's why he's going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost of living measures to give people some room to breathe."

The spokesman added: "He's also going to be kicking off his summer tour around the country, getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are.

"The prime minister is going to be in listening mode to help inform his 10-year plan to bring back hope and make Britain better off."

There are, though, likely to be continued questions about the forthcoming early release scheme, due to start in October.

One of Burnham's first acts in Downing Street was to order a review which limited the range of people who would be eligible.

But those convicted of manslaughter will still qualify for the scheme â including two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

The prime minister has faced calls from PC Harper's family, former senior police officers and opposition politicians for them to be denied early release.

But he has said he cannot go any further without risking prison capacity. Downing Street said on Saturday night that position remained unchanged, despite reports the prime minister could revisit the case.

News.title: Family 'devastated' as hit-and-run driver who killed boy, 13, to have early prison release
News.content:
The family of a 13-year-old boy killed in a hit-and-run say they are "devastated" after being told the driver who caused his death has had his sentence reduced.

Kaylan Hippsley died three days after being struck by a car driven by Harley Whiteman on Brecon Road in Hirwaun, Rhondda Cynon Taf, on 29 February 2024.

Whiteman was originally sentenced to six years and nine months in prison and banned from driving for eight years and four months but, after Kaylan's family appealed, High Court judges increased the sentence to nine years.

Now, the family has been told Whiteman can be released under licence as early as this autumn as part of the UK government's Sentencing Act early release scheme.

News.title: Holiday 'completely overshadowed' by loss of airport luggage
News.content:
Travellers have described struggling to enjoy their holidays, days after hundreds of people flying out of Birmingham Airport were left without their luggage.

While it seems the issues that first emerged on Friday are yet to be remedied completely, the airport said the "vast majority" of baggage was now travelling as planned with passengers, and it was working to reunite others with their luggage.

Louise Fenton said she and her family had had no communication from the airline, holiday company or the airport after their luggage failed to arrive in Gran Canaria on Friday.

She is travelling with three teenagers, and said her daughter, who is autistic, had "struggled enormously" with replacement clothes, and had "barely slept because she is unable to tolerate the alternatives".

"We are staying in a tourist area where the shops are predominantly beach shops, with very limited clothing options, particularly for someone with sensory sensitivities," the mum explained.

"We still have no luggage and, no meaningful information about where it is."

She added the situation had "completely overshadowed" the holiday.

"We have worked hard and saved for this holiday, and we simply don't deserve to have the entire experience taken over by something that isn't our fault."

Speaking to the BBC on Friday and Saturday, travellers variously described the situation as "absolute chaos" and "carnage".

Other flights affected include ones to Turkey, Cyprus, Glasgow and Rome, covering a number of airlines.

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7 million people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assault led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
News.content:
It has taken almost two years to plan, including building a special temperature-controlled crate for him, and co-ordinating complex paperwork across two countries.

Rhossi normally lives in the sea, but has to travel out of the water â first by helicopter from Anglesey to London, then by cargo flight to Houston, Texas, USA.

It means the journey needs to be completed as quickly as possible, and staff have to be constantly on hand to make sure he does not dry out or dehydrate.

Davidson said: "We have to make sure that the shell is really well lubricated, so we spread Vaseline all over to stop it drying out and flaking off.

"The same for the skin â it's really delicate â and especially the eyes, which both have to be lubricated before he goes into the crate and again just before takeoff, or he will start to peel like someone getting sunburned.

"But I have had to go to the checkout in a chemist's with about eight tubes of KY Jelly and three tubs of Vaseline and explain what's happening when I get strange looks."

News.title: Hot weather reveals hidden history across the South
News.content:
As the south of England continues to enjoy an unusually warm and dry summer, parch marks on lawns across the region have revealed the hidden histories of their location.

Among the sites which have seen the outlines of historic installations exposed by the hot weather are Portchester Castle and Blenheim Palace.

At Blenheim, the footprint of an 18th Century garden - which had once stretched across the width of the entire palace - has revealed itself on a lawn.

Andy Mills, the Unesco World Heritage Site's head gardener, told the BBC it was "absolutely magical" to see the outlines of the historic parterre - 260 years after it was demolished.

Mills explained that the original parterre - which is a French word meaning "on the ground" - had been constructed in 1705, and would have "cost an absolute fortune to install".

"It was a very large extravagant thing to do, but it was a way of showing your wealth and importance and that sort of thing," he said.

News.title: Attempted murder arrest after three hit by car
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and dangerous driving after three pedestrians were hit by a car following reports of a disturbance.

The incident happened on Stokes Croft in Bristol at about 06:30 BST, according to Avon and Somerset Police.

A spokesperson for the force said one of the pedestrians was taken to hospital, but their injuries were not considered to be life-changing or life-threatening. The two others were not seriously injured.

A man police believe to be the car's driver was treated for facial injuries after his arrest.

Thomas Street, Hepburn Road, Stokes Croft and City Road are all closed while police make enquiries, with more officers than usual in the area as investigations continue.

The Best Off Licence in Stokes Croft was also damaged in the incident.

Bristol Supt Matt Ebbs said: "We would like to assure the public we do not believe there to be any wider threat.

"Anybody with concerns is welcome to speak to officers on the ground, but we would also appeal to anybody with CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage which may assist our enquiries to contact us."

News.title: Stray cats showing up at raves, gigs and pubs now have own merchandise
News.content:
Celebs pulling in punters with a club appearance is nothing new. But did they ever have so much fur?

At venues in Coventry at least, the glitterati wear whiskers these days.

It began when two stray cats made city venues their home, becoming social media stars thanks to the incongruous sights of tail and turntable, pint and paw.

While one shows up at gigs and rave nights, the other is a bit more pub than dub. But each now has his own range of merch... and visitors flock for a glimpse of these meeow-vers and shakers.

Murphy was first spotted living beneath a bush before wandering into the car park of The Old Windmill pub in the city centre, "rake thin" and in need of care.

Now a permanent resident, he has become a firm favourite with customers.

"We've had people who've never been in the pub before, but have seen him on social media," said the venue's Peter Dunkley. "They come in and the first question is 'where's Murphy'?"

Across town, Fargo is a well-known figure at Fargo Village, the creative hub after which he is named.

Regularly spotted around the site's shops and bars, he too has become an attraction in his own right, mixing among ravers and drinkers.

Fargo Village staff have set up an Instagram account in an effort to track down his owner, and it has attracted a loyal following of fans eager to keep up with his daily adventures.
