New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez revealed to her followers — and the world — that she was freezing her eggs, sharing a live video on her Instagram story during which she administered a hormone injection to herself ahead of a scheduled Sunday television appearance.

“Usually, I keep my private life quite private, but I have made the decision to start freezing my eggs,” Ocasio-Cortez said in the Saturday night live stream, “and I want to share that with anyone who is — and I want to share this because I was weighing it for a very long time, and I think that, you know, I was saving for it for a very long time, and there just isn’t a ton out there, I feel, and sometimes it can feel very daunting.”

The Democratic congresswoman discussed the preparation involved in the medical procedure and noted that taking her first injection “wasn’t so bad.” She mentioned that she would be administering additional doses in the green room before appearing on ABC’s This Week.

“As women in general, we are not taught about our bodies, we are not prepared for our own lives, whether that is in puberty, whether that is in pregnancy, whether that is in perimenopause, menopause, whether that is in so many different aspects of our lives,” she said.

Reflecting on her public profile and reproductive choices, Ocasio-Cortez explained her rationale for sharing the experience publicly despite the personal nature of the procedure.

New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said on Saturday that she would be freezing her eggs, sharing a live video on Instagram during which she administered a hormone injection to herself ( AFP/Getty )

“In the political context that we're in, in an administration that is dedicated to politicizing women’s bodies and taking our choices away from us and punishing us around decisions to be pregnant or not be pregnant — and, frankly, this administration has made pregnancy more dangerous than probably at any point in the last 30 plus years — we’re gonna take our power back,” she said.

She noted that navigating adulthood while serving in Congress presented unique challenges, particularly regarding reproductive decisions and public scrutiny.

“I got sworn into the House of Representatives when I was 29 years old. I was the youngest woman in American history to get elected to congress,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “There’s also this flip side where you have to then grow up in the public eye in a time that most people usually get to grow more privately, and when you get elected later in life you've made all of your mistakes in private.”

She also highlighted double standards faced by female politicians regarding family planning and age.

“This is just not something that men deal with. Men run for office, or frankly, they interview for jobs and people don't think in the back of their mind, ‘OK this guy's running for office, how old is he? Oh, well is he gonna wanna start a family?’” she said. “This is a choice I am making to feel more in control of my life.”

She acknowledged potential fallout, too.

“I am also aware that there is very strangely a political risk, or even a political tax that could come with sharing this information, and, per usual, that doesn't influence my ultimate decision,” she said.

Ocasio-Cortez has frequently advocated for reproductive healthcare. Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, she told GQ in a 2022 interview that men also had a stake in reproductive freedom.

“For almost every woman that has gotten an abortion, there’s a man who has either been affected or liberated by that abortion too,” she told the publication at the time.

Her decision to document the fertility treatment drew immediate responses on social media.

Democratic strategist Xochitl Hinojosa praised the disclosure on X, writing: “THIS. We don’t talk about women freezing their eggs or what women have to go through to start a family. Thank you @AOC for your bravery.”

Other commentators reacted critically to the video and its framing.

User @thewakeninq wrote on X: “AOC just injected herself on camera, told everyone ‘don’t be weird,’ then acted shocked when the internet lost its mind. It’s not diabetes. It’s not a baby. It’s her freezing eggs so she can maybe have one later… while spending her entire career fighting to make sure other women can end theirs. The cognitive dissonance is Olympic-level. Don’t be weird? Too late.”

During her appearance on ABC’s This Week on Sunday, host Jonathan Karl asked Ocasio-Cortez about her decision to open up on social media.

“In this political environment where this administration is denying reproductive care to women across the country, from abortion rights to the ability to carry out a healthy pregnancy, I think it's important for us as leaders to have these conversations and share these processes, especially for working women across the country and normalize them,” Ocasio-Cortez said on the broadcast.

When Anfield had last hosted Liverpool, as Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson bade farewell and their teammates embarked on their final lap of honour, Arne Slot had remained sat in the dugout. It proved the last sighting of him in Liverpool. Some 11 weeks later, Slot’s successor was a visible presence on the edge of the technical area, Andoni Iraola’s constant clapping encouraging his players at the start of a new era. It began with echoes of the old: a 3-2 defeat to Monaco, with a lead lost at Anfield, and with a goal conceded to a set-piece, had some similarities with Slot’s unravelling, even if the stakes were lower.

Iraola may hope the parallels with last season end when the competitive football starts. As it was, Liverpool outlined why they require Ronald Araujo and how their recruitment is unfinished. They have a left-back – Robertson’s replacement is his former deputy, a returning Kostas Tsimikas making his Anfield comeback – but Salah’s old spot remains unfilled. Lewis Koumas was a locum in the place of a legend on the right flank; the Welsh winger may be destined for a fourth straight loan spell rather than a run in the team.

open image in gallery Andoni Iraola still has work to do in the transfer market, as was evident in his Anfield bow against Monaco ( PA )

His presence was an illustration that Liverpool’s business stalled after the June signing of Victor Munoz. They are yet to achieve their main objective. One ambitious target, Yan Diomande, has already eluded them. Another is out of reach as long as there is a significant difference between Liverpool’s valuation of Bradley Barcola and Paris Saint-Germain’s. There is no point in putting in a bid now when the European champions want well over £100m.

Liverpool have shown a willingness to pay such sums in the past; but their budget is limited now. Their two £100m men from 2025 struck in a way that at least offered optimism they will deliver more this season than last.

Alexander Isak only found the net twice at Anfield in his debut campaign for Liverpool; a friendly goal will not count towards his official tally but was guided in after a pass from Ryan Gravenberch. Isak and Florian Wirtz struck in the same game, which they only did once for Slot. The German got a poacher’s goal, bundling the ball over the line after Cody Gakpo’s header was blocked, even if Isak claimed he got the final touch. If Wirtz alternated between central and wide roles under Slot, Iraola has installed him as his No 10.

open image in gallery Alexander Isak (right) and Florian Wirtz were both on target against Monaco ( Reuters )

There seems a clarity to that and a more vertical brand of football after the passiveness of Slotball irritated Anfield. Distinct differences were apparent in Iraola’s home bow. It was notable that the full-backs were often far more advanced than Gravenberch. That may suit Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez, though the latter did not start against Monaco, more than Slot’s style of football did. Yet it also gives a need for centre-backs who can defend one on one.

And, as Liverpool turned victory into defeat, they underlined why the middle of the defence has been the other focus of their recruitment drive, and why additions are necessary. Araujo is undergoing a medical before he completes his surprise loan from Barcelona. Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni, the youngsters who arrived for a combined fee of almost £100m, are yet to play in pre-season; Joe Gomez is already injured.

Virgil van Dijk, in his first appearance since the World Cup, could be forgiven for rustiness when he tripped Aleksandr Golovin to concede a penalty the Russian converted himself. Wataru Endo, who spent the second half at centre-back, and Frimpong were both partly culpable when Mika Biereth levelled the scores.

open image in gallery Virgil van Dijk made his first appearance of pre-season but conceded a penalty ( PA )

Endo had come on for the great success of Liverpool’s tour of the United States. The giant Ifeanyi Ndukwe excelled again in the first half. The problem is that he is ineligible for competitive games, lacking a work permit, perhaps meaning a loan abroad beckons. In the Austrian and the Senegalese Mor Talla Ndiaye, Liverpool have two precocious 18-year-olds. Their defensive future can look secure. The concerns are about the present.

Araujo will tick some boxes; at 27, he is roughly halfway between Van Dijk and the duo of the 19-year-old Leoni and Jacquet, 21, in age and, unlike Gomez, is fit now. Liverpool need a bridge to the next generation. They hoped it would be Ibrahima Konate, but he wanted a financial package that could have felt a problem if, in a couple of years, he found himself understudying Leoni and Jacquet; or, indeed, Ndukwe.

Konate left without a proper goodbye. Harvey Elliott, who could have been gone for good, returned from his unproductive loan at Aston Villa to the loudest cheer of the afternoon. It may not herald a second coming at Anfield, however: he was the third man used at No 10, after Wirtz and then Dominik Szoboszlai, who had begun in midfield.

open image in gallery Harvey Elliott got the loudest cheer of the afternoon off the bench ( Reuters )

Even as he made 11 substitutions, there were other glimpses into Iraola’s thinking. Rio Ngumoha ended the game on the right flank. He may have to step into Salah’s shoes in more meaningful matches.

An economist took live television interruption to a new level on Saturday when an insect flew into his mouth during a CNN interview about the U.S. economy.

University of Michigan professor Justin Wolfers was analyzing labor market data with CNN anchor Omar Jimenez when Wolfers accidentally swallowed a fly mid-interview. He was describing the U.S. labor market as “The Little Engine That Could” and noted it was “not earning an A+ in anyone’s book, but it does seem remarkably resilient so far.”

He added, “But, all resilient until the day that we’re not,” before he suddenly began coughing and struggling to speak.

Jimenez attempted to keep the segment moving to give Wolfers a moment to recover, asking, “You know, I just wonder, like, as we look ahead, everyone is looking — maybe not everyone — but, folks like yourself are looking at the Fed and trying to figure out, okay, we have these economic indicators, maybe the job market is a little softer, but how do you think the Fed is going to read this, considering they didn’t hike interest rates at the last meeting?”

“Mate, I just swallowed a fly on live television!” Wolfers said after managing to clear his throat.

University of Michigan professor Justin Wolfers was analyzing labor market data with CNN anchor Omar Jimenez when Wolfers accidentally swallowed a fly mid-interview ( CNN )

“I was trying to keep talking while you were coughing, so you could figure it out,” Jimenez responded. “It’s all good!”

Wolfers, an Australian native, joked about the situation on air, claiming that “Aussies love eating flies!” before tying the mishap back to Federal Reserve monetary policy.

“It might actually be a metaphor, because the biggest thing going on at the Fed is Kevin Warsh feels like I do right now,” Wolfers said, pausing to cough. “Kevin Warsh doesn’t like talking about what’s going on, and it makes both of us a little harder to understand and a little harder to interpret. So, you can think of Kevin as having swallowed the fly as well. I might swallow a horse; that will get the fly as well.”

Following the broadcast, Wolfers addressed the incident on X.

“A fly just zipped into my mouth while gabbing on CNN,” Wolfers wrote. “Next question was about the Fed, so I did what Kevin Warsh won't — I swallowed hard and kept talking. I figure folks deserve some clarity about the economy.”

He added: “(Postscript: The fly is dead. And I'm no longer a vegetarian.)”

To understand the 127 Yard Sale, it helps to start on a back road in rural Ohio, where a 12-foot rooster statue towers before a red barn. Alternatively, route to a two-lane stretch in Tennessee, where a vendor’s sign propped inside an open casket promises a “killer deal.”

For nearly 700 miles — stretching along Highway 127 in southern Michigan down to Lookout Mountain Parkway, Alabama — the nation’s longest yard sale winds through open farmland, mountain bluffs and small towns.

This year’s sale runs from Aug. 6 though Aug. 9. Across the four-day route, tables hold a mix of everyday attic clear-outs and true oddities.

Shoppers sift through classic roadside fare like vintage tools, mid-century furniture, milk glass and car parts, mixed with items you would be hard pressed to find anywhere else. Over the years, vendors have set up everything from Victorian wheelchairs and antique farm machinery to full-sized replica dinosaurs and even a vintage embalming table.

“Every year, people ask me, ‘What is it like?’” Josh Randall, the director of media relations for the 127 Yard Sale, told The Independent. “It’s one of those things where, until you experience it yourself, it’s very hard to put into words because it’s on such a massive scale. People think yard sale, they think the Saturday morning kind of thing. But because it’s so big, it’s like you’re going to an event. You're not just going to a yard sale.”

open image in gallery At the 127 Yard Sale, which spans Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Georgia and Alabama, shoppers pick through miles of roadside treasures, hunting down everything from vintage chairs and mid-century furniture to full-sized replica dinosaurs ( 127 Yard Sale )

open image in gallery Map of the 127 Yard Sale route from Addison, Michigan, to Gadsden, Alabama ( 127 Yard Sale )

The event’s origins trace back to 1987, when Mike Walker, then county executive of Fentress County in Jamestown, Tennessee, hatched a plan to lure vacationers off major interstates. The goal was to redirect tourist traffic onto two-lane back roads, giving small rural communities along Highway 127 a chance to show off their local businesses, parks and regional culture.

The local experiment quickly caught on. Neighboring communities across Kentucky, Ohio and surrounding states wanted to be part of it, eventually expanding the route into the six-state corridor it is today.

“Over the following years, Ohio was added to it, Georgia down into Alabama, and eventually the last portion that was added was into the southern portion of Michigan,” Randall said. Next year, he added, marks the sale’s 40th anniversary.

Spanning nearly 700 miles, the event is so vast that even those who run it struggle to capture its magnitude. With no single entry point or gate count to rely on, organizers estimate that participation climbs into the hundreds of thousands, driven by more than 10,000 vendors spread across all six states.

open image in gallery A roadside sign propped inside an open casket promises a ‘killer deal’ along a 700-mile stretch of rural back roads ( 127 Yard Sale )

open image in gallery A replica dinosaur at the 127 Yard Sale ( 127 Yard Sale )

Navigating the sale requires patience and a willingness to abandon strict schedules. Because traffic slows to a crawl through the heavy vendor clusters, driving Highway 127 means surrendering to the pace of the road.

“You might show up somewhere and think you're going to be there for ten minutes,” Randall said, "and the next thing you know, you're talking to a vendor and you're there for two hours.”

For Randall, that unhurried pace is precisely what gives the sale its staying power. Having traveled the entire 700-mile corridor multiple times, he sees the event as a rare reprieve from an increasingly digital world.

“Today, so much of our lives is digital — we’re on social media, we’re doing email,” he said. “Actually being in person and talking to other human beings face-to-face is becoming more of a unique thing. People spend a lot of time talking, and there’s a real community aspect to it.”

open image in gallery Beyond typical household clutter, the route features massive specialty collections, including extensive sets of vintage toy cars ( 127 Yard Sale )

open image in gallery A collection of salt-and-pepper shakers at the 127 Yard Sale ( 127 Yard Sale )

That desire to talk to actual people mirrors a broader trend in the explosion of second-hand shopping and secondhand culture. In recent years, thrifting and vintage hunting have transformed what used to be a weekend hobby into a massive secondary economy, fueled in large part by social media creators, digital resellers and content creators looking for unique pieces.

The 127 Yard Sale Facebook community alone has grown to more than 199,000 members, serving as a year-round online home base where shoppers post wish lists, vendors share photos of incoming merchandise and property owners rent out booth spaces for about $25 per day.

Yet while platforms like TikTok, Instagram and online marketplaces have introduced a younger generation to the thrill of second-hand treasure hunting, Randall notes that digital hype can only take you so far.

open image in gallery Driven by viral social media trends, a younger generation of content creators is heading to Highway 127 for old-fashioned, face-to-face dealmaking ( 127 Yard Sale )

open image in gallery Property owners along the route turn front yards and empty pastures into bustling outdoor markets charging around $25 a day per booth ( 127 Yard Sale )

The online space helps build anticipation, but it ultimately serves to feed the real-world experience.

Influencers and content creators now travel the route to document their journeys in real time, drawing viewers into a culture centered on tactile discovery — sifting through physical crates, bargaining over old tools or vintage fashion and connecting directly with the seller.

Beyond individual sellers clearing out attics, the event provides an essential economic lift to small towns along the route. One indoor antique mall in Chattanooga, Tennessee, recorded four-day sales totals during the event that eclipsed its entire previous month’s revenue.

Revenue aside, most people come for the simple joy of the drive.

“You get to experience something you wouldn't normally,” Randall said.

Keely Hodgkinson expects her hotly-anticipated European title showdown with new nemesis Audrey Werro will make the women’s 800 metres the “race of the championships” in Birmingham.

The British Olympic gold medallist was beaten by the Swiss athlete in Stockholm in June, where Werro went third on the all-time list before running even faster three weeks later in Paris to enter this week’s European Athletics Championships with a world-leading one minute, 53.80 seconds.

Both women have declared their intent to take down Jarmila Kratochvilova’s 43-year-old world record, while the Netherlands’ Femke Broeders-Bol, one of the greatest 400m hurdlers, has also splashed into the 800m waters and holds the third-fastest time this season.

“We’ve spoken about (what they might do) a little bit,” said Hodgkinson. “Obviously I need to get through the rounds and just be in that final, but ultimately I’ll just focus on what I can do best and control my race.

“I don’t know what anyone else is going to do, but I think it’s going to be the race of the championships. I think it’s going to be really fun, so I’m excited.”

All four of the world’s top women at 800m this year are European. French record-holder Anais Bourgoin rounds out the quartet of Birmingham competitors who have dipped below one minute, 56 seconds.

The only other woman to do so this year, Hodgkinson’s training partner Georgia Hunter Bell, is focusing on the 1500m, the same distance at which she is an Olympic bronze medallist.

open image in gallery Hodgkinson expects the 800m to be the race of the European championships (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Wire )

Hodgkinson insists defending her European title for a second time would mean “just as much to me, almost, as winning in Paris (at the Olympics)”, because it would be a first on home soil.

She “hasn’t spent too much time” with Werro, though Hodgkinson admits the 22-year-old took her by surprise in Stockholm.

“I don’t really think I did anything wrong in that race,” the 24-year-old insisted.

“I didn’t know what she was capable of at that point. I think that just shows you like you can’t underestimate anybody. If you look at all our other head-to-heads, you wouldn’t have thought she was going to hang on.

open image in gallery Audrey Werro is set to be one of Hodgkinson’s main rivals in Birmingham (Miek Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“I think that’s where I was at that point in the season. It was my opening race. I think people are trying to make me feel like it was a failure and it really wasn’t. That was a British record. It was my fastest time ever and I’m going to remind myself of that because I’m proud of that.”

Hodgkinson, who has worked through a few fitness concerns already this season, still has her fair share of online critics.

They can be cruel, wrong, and sometimes downright bizarre.

It was never in Hodgkinson’s plans to compete at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, where Hunter Bell claimed the 800m title.

Yet Hodgkinson revealed: “Me and Georgia were laughing the other day because we saw a TikTok, and it was like ‘Georgia Bell pays Keely £200k to not do the Commonwealth Games.

“I thought, ‘well, I didn’t get that money so where the f***’s it going’. People make up stuff. We just laugh about it. But it’s a strange world we live in sometimes.”

Keely Hodgkinson returns to competition at the European Athletics Championships in an unusual position. After breaking the world indoor record over 800m in March, it looked as though the world was at her feet. But the Paris Olympic champion has had a distinctly stop-start outdoor season, troubled by a “freak” injury and dogged by bad luck, and has been beaten resoundingly, twice, by Switzerland’s breakout star Audrey Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year.

With that in mind, does she still believe she is the best in the world, going into a major championships on home soil? On a video call with The Independent and other outlets, she smiles confidently as she says: “Yes, I still believe I’m very much capable of that.

“This is what I trained for, this is the exciting moment. I’ve been doing this for a couple of years now, had lots of people come around and challenge me, and I’ve always been there. I’m proud to have always been in that top segment, I’ve medalled at every single championships. So it’s really great to have the women’s 800 in the spotlight and everyone getting behind us and wanting us to run fast, it’s really exciting.”

The 24-year-old’s outdoor woes began when she fell in training onto a metal grate that left her with cuts to her knees before the Prefontaine Classic in Oregon, where she lost to world champion Lilian Odira. She suffered surprise back-to-back defeats and withdrew in tears from the British national championships earlier this summer, moments before the 400m final, after tweaking her hamstring.

Now she is relaxed about the fall; her knees have healed – “I’ve got some fat scars, but they’re all fine” – and the incident didn’t cause her to miss any training. “It was like, how much pain can I manage? Against these girls, if you’re limping and your back’s out, all these little fine margins can affect your performance.

open image in gallery Hodgkinson returned to winning ways at the London Diamond League last month ( Getty )

“I just fell over, it’s a freak accident, who cares? I think people are very quick to judge and don’t really fully know what has happened. I wanted to run, I was there, I flew all the way out. Maybe in hindsight I probably shouldn’t have, but, I was there, I just thought, why not?”

She returned to winning ways on home soil at the London Diamond League last month, but cannot be considered the out-and-out favourite – although she remains a major force – in a glittering field.

Switzerland’s Werro has been the surprise package of the season and is the outright favourite after running the fastest times in the world this year. She won the Diamond League in Stockholm in one minute 53.98 seconds – the third fastest women’s 800m ever and the quickest this year – to leave Hodgkinson a distant second, even with a new personal best and British record time of 1:54.33.

Hodgkinson reflected on that race, saying: “I didn’t know what she was capable of at that point, and I think that just shows you that you can’t underestimate anybody. If you look at all our other head-to-heads, you wouldn’t have thought she was going to hang on. I don’t think I did anything wrong – I think people were trying to make me feel like it was a failure and it really wasn’t. That was a British record, it was my fastest time ever, and I’m going to remind myself of that because I’m proud of that.”

open image in gallery It has been a stop-start season for the Brit who withdrew from the national championships in tears ( PA Wire )

Hodgkinson has become used to being the athlete to beat throughout her young career, a generational talent who wins with ease. This year she has been on the back foot. With Femke Broeders-Bol – having converted her brilliance in her normal discipline of 400m hurdles to the 800m – also a potent force, the 800 is set to be the race of the championships, but it may not go all Hodgkinson’s way.

She is taking a relaxed approach to that. “I’ve obviously got a lot of experience, and experience can be both a positive and a negative thing. Sometimes you overthink more because it’s like, I’ve done it this way, I’ve done it this way. So I just like to go back to basics, like when I was young, upcoming, I didn’t care. I had nothing to lose and I think it’s important for me that I hold on to that and I just race with courage and fearlessness and I think that’s how I’ll get the best out of myself.”

Of the strength of her competition, she says: “I think it definitely just helps motivation-wise. This is what I love about championships. I’ve gone into them ranked eighth in the Olympics in Tokyo, came out with a silver; I’ve gone in as favourite and not won. I think it’s like a bit of a clean slate.

“The standard now in Europe has gone up [over the last few years], so I think the heats, the semis are going to be a lot faster than what we’ve seen in the last couple of years. It does mean you’ve got to bring your A game a bit sooner. But I think that’s a bit better for me because I like to line up and feel like, you know, this matters, I’m gonna have to run fast, I’ve got these girls to run against. I think it’s really exciting, the levels that we have.”

open image in gallery She was part of a trio of British success stories at the world indoor championships in Poland ( Getty )

She had initially pencilled in the London Diamond League for an attempt at breaking the infamous world outdoor record, having smashed the world indoor record in March. But it now looks as though Werro, who became the first woman since the controversial Jarmila Kratochvilova to run under 1:54 – twice – in Paris and Stockholm this year, is the best placed to finally topple the Czech’s mark of 1:53.28, which has stood since 1983.

The stage is set for a hugely entertaining race – the only drawback is that newly crowned Commonwealth 800m champion Georgia Hunter Bell is opting not to compete over the distance in Birmingham, focusing on the 1,500m instead.

Hunter Bell and Hodgkinson are training partners and close friends, but the 32-year-old has spoken openly about her desire to double up, racing both the 800m and 1,500m, in future championships, adding yet another rivalry to the 800m field and another dynamic to negotiate for coaches Trevor Painter and Jenny Meadows.

open image in gallery Training partners and rivals Hodgkinson and Georgia Hunter Bell will not compete over the same distance in Birmingham ( PA Wire )

Asked whether she would relish the challenge of having another rival over 800m, Hodgkinson says: “If Georgia wants to do that, that doesn’t really affect me. I think it’d be great. Obviously we train together, we push each other really hard, we’re both in really good shape. When we plan our races, I sit down with Trevor and plan mine, she does hers and whatever she feels like she wants to do.

“I think with there being three championships [UK nationals, Commonwealths and Europeans] and her being decisive between the two events, she’s just done what is best for her. But I’m sure there’ll be a time this season that we do match up and it’ll be a good race.”

One Night Only director Will Gluck has revealed that he decided to scale back the amount of nudity in the romcom because he believes audiences are too uncomfortable with sex on screen.

The movie, starring Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner, is set in a bizarre world in which the U.S. has outlawed premarital sex for 364 days a year — leaving single people just 12 hours annually to hook up.

It has been widely compared to the horror franchise The Purge, in which violent crimes are legalised for one day per year.

In a new interview for Variety, Gluck, whose credits include Easy A and Anyone But You, said he studied empirical data about how Gen Z and Gen Alpha don’t want to see sex on screen, which informed how much intimacy was shown in the final cut of the movie.

“I cut out so much,” he said. “There was so much nudity in this movie that we shot on the streets.”

open image in gallery ‘One Night Only’ is set in a bizarre world in which the U.S. has outlawed premarital sex for 364 days a year — leaving single people just 12 hours annually to hook up ( Universal Pictures )

He decided to cut back on intimate scenes based on the audience’s reaction at test screenings for the movie.

“As we started to show it to audiences, we felt it takes you out of the movie. You’re engaged in the characters and what’s going on, and then you pan over and there’s two naked people having sex, and you watch the audience … it’s a physical thing,” he explained.

“So we just kept editing it out until we got a balance, and those comments went away.”

Gluck suggested that because people are constantly exposed to nudity and intimate scenes on their phones, it’s become “more of a private, intimate thing that people don’t want to see when they’re in a shared experience.”

“Whenever people now see nudity or very adult situations in a big theater, they get uncomfortable,” he reckoned.

open image in gallery Director Will Gluck said he ‘cut out so much’ nudity and intimate scenes from the final cut of the movie ( Universal Pictures )

The director added that he used an intimacy coordinator for romance scenes, and also cast real-life couples already familiar with each other to act in them.

“It was never like we met an extra and were like, ‘you guys are kissing.’ It was fun because there were married couples, people who broke up during the movie and people who became couples so they could do that,” he said.

Reviews for the movie have been polarized, with some critics describing the message of the film as being “strangely conservative” and even “fascist”.

In The Guardian, critic Benjamin Lee wrote that the film’s premise ought to be “the set-up for a grim Handmaid’s Tale-adjacent horror of a totalitarian state insisting extreme control over the body, but instead it’s used as the backdrop for a sunny meet-cute, screams of protest drowned out by a zippy Top 40 soundtrack”.

“If it sounds like far too much for a breezy summer romp to take on, then that’s because it most definitely is, an overstuffed yet undercooked soufflé that can’t quite, ahem, rise to the occasion…”

Others have been kinder to the film, with several outlets singling out the chemistry between the two leads for particular praise.

Variety’s Guy Lodge praised them as “two attractive, pleasingly grown-up leads whom you wouldn’t mind seeing get together; it’s set in New York City at its most invitingly balmy.”

You’ve probably heard the news. Rome is hot this summer, and not in a good way. Roman summers are typically hot and humid, but this season has been one for the record books, with daily temperatures routinely topping 39C. It's beastly — bestiale, as we say in Italian. Yet it hasn't kept visitors away. In July, Rome averaged 60,000-80,000 visitors a day in its centro storico. That's a lot of sweaty people crowding into the Colosseum.

Every guidebook will tell you to duck into a church for a break from the heat, and that’s good advice: marble floors, high ceilings and thick walls do their job. But if you really want to escape the Roman summer, you need to go underground. Below the churches, below the streets, below 2,000 years of layered history, there’s a level of Rome that’s always cool: its underground archaeological sites where the temperatures are pleasant — sometimes even chilly — year-round, with temperatures as low as 10C, no matter how sweltering it is up on street level.

The cool air, though, is really just an excuse. The five sites listed below are among some of the most fascinating in Rome, offering, in many cases, a real glimpse of what the city looked like when it reigned as caput mundi — capital of the ancient world.

Domus Aurea – the Golden House of Nero

open image in gallery The Domus Aurea are the excavated remains of Emperor Nero’s palace ( Elizabeth Heath )



It was already hot by mid-June as my guests and I huddled in a small patch of shade, waiting for our timed entry to the Domus Aurea. When our guide appeared, dressed in a puffer jacket, scarf and beanie cap, I thought she was exaggerating. About 40 minutes into our tour, I understood her cold weather attire and was grateful that I'd at least worn long sleeves.

The partially excavated remains of notorious Emperor Nero’s vast pleasure palace are entirely underground, thanks to the Roman practice of damnatio memoriae, erasing all traces of undesirables from history and memory. After Nero's death in 68CE by noble suicide, the palace, which once covered as many as 300 acres, was entirely filled with millions of tonnes of rubble and lay forgotten for 14 centuries. Today, guided tours reveal a maze of connected rooms, many with fragments of frescoes, marble and mosaics. A virtual reality experience is breathtakingly vivid. The downside is that it’s only open Friday-Sunday, and tickets get snatched up as soon as they go on sale, so act fast.

Basilica di San Clemente excavations

A few minutes' walk from the crowds baking outside the Colosseum, San Clemente illustrates, perhaps better than any site in Rome, how the city’s many layers were stacked atop one another, reused, and in some cases, remarkably well-preserved. Beneath the (not to be skipped over) 12th-century basilica lies a 4th-century Paleo-Christian church and, below that, a 1st-century CE apartment and a Mithraeum — a cave-like temple dedicated to the Eastern god Mithras. Water still courses through an ancient underground channel here and provides the soundtrack to a dark and mysterious ambience. The upper basilica is free to enter, while the excavation area is ticketed.



Domus Romane at Palazzo Valentini

open image in gallery Via Fori Imperiali with the archaeological ruins of the Imperial Forums and the Trajan's Forum ( Getty Images )

I'm such a fan of this underground archaeological site that I almost hesitate to recommend it, because I'm not sure I want people to find out about it. The Domus Romane lie seven metres below 19th-century Palazzo Valentini and are reached by an entrance near Trajan’s Column. This is one of the best-interpreted sites in Rome — visitors walk across a glass floor, and peer down into the ruins, where light projections illustrate what these patrician houses looked like at their peak — mosaicked and marbled floors, frescoed walls, and even a swimming pool. Because the site is not as well-known as its famous neighbours (the Colosseum and Forum are right nearby), it’s still easy — for now — to book a timed-entry tour here. If it’s available, book a tour that includes the presentation about Trajan’s Column.

The Catacombs on the Appian Way

Outside the Aurelian Walls along the Via Appia Antica (the Old Appian Way), lie several early Christian tomb complexes, dug several storeys deep into the volcanic tuff stone. Among them are the catacombs of San Callisto, San Sebastiano, and Domitilla. It’s hard to say which one is the “best” of the bunch; San Callisto is the largest, but often the most crowded by tour buses. The San Sebastiano tour goes deeper underground, and Domitilla contains well-preserved frescoes. All maintain a steady temperature of about 15C. The three catacombs rotate their closing dates during the week so be sure to check online before you make your plans.

The Vatican Grottoes

Beneath the main floor of St Peter’s Basilica, these vaulted chambers house the tombs of dozens of popes, dating from the 10th to 16th centuries — making them practically modern by Rome’s standards. Still, it’s neat to descend under the main basilica and ponder the age and gravitas of these spaces, which include a gilded monument over the burial place of St. Peter. The other sarcophagi range from austere to elaborate. The Grottoes are accessed from the interior of the basilica, at the pier to the right of Bernini’s Baldacchino — look for signs marked or "Tombe dei Papi”. Like the basilica, entrance to the Grottoes is free of charge.

News.title: Liverpool’s lack of depth bites as they squander two-goal lead again
News.content:
For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans joke ‘don’t let Mikel Arteta see this’ as star assists goal with incredible SOMERSAULT throw-in routine
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans were left stunned after seeing an incredible somersault throw-in go viral on social media.

And many joked that set piece enthusiast Mikel Arteta would be taking note.



The somersault throw-in came in a Russian second-tier match between SKA-Khabarovsk and Spartak Kostroma.

Spartak’s Iranian defender Nader Mohammadi went over to take a throw on the right side, with his side 2-1 up late on.



The 29-year-old proceeded to somersault during his run-up as he launched the ball deep into the box.

Mohammadi’s remarkable throw was headed straight in by Amur Kalmykov, making Spartak’s three points safe.



And fans on social media were left flabbergasted by the incredible throw.

One joked: “Don’t let Arteta see this, I’m begging you”.

And a second similarly quipped: “Don’t let Arsenal see this”.

A third begged: “Keep arsenal far away from him”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another added: “When Arteta catches wind of this strategy on his evening scroll tonight, the Premier League is finished”.

This was not the first time that Mohammadi’s throw has gone viral.

In 2021, the defender won his side a corner with a throw from his own half during an Iranian top flight match.

Despite its prowess, his monster throw has so far not been enough to earn an international call-up.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘set for bumper pay-day windfall thanks to secret Romelu Lukaku clause as striker nears Fenerbahce transfer’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are set to significantly benefit from Napoli star Romelu Lukaku’s imminent move to Fenerbahce with a massive windfall.

Lukaku, 33, joined the Partenopei from the Blues in 2024 after three years in his second stint at Stamford Bridge that also saw him being loaned out to Inter Milan and Roma.



According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Fener and the Serie A giants are closing in on a deal for the striker.

The same source claims the Belgium international has agreed in principle to join the Turkish giants.



The ex-Manchester United star has agreed a two-year contract worth £8.6million, including bonuses.

Negotiations between the two clubs are now in their final stages and the transfer is expected to be completed within the next 24 hours.

It is said the deal could cost at least £9-10m, which is what Napoli are demanding to let Lukaku go.

And that is very good new for Chelsea, who added a resale value on the Belgian after selling him to Naples two years ago.

Napoli agreed to pay the West Londoners a 40 per cent sell-on share of any future transfer.

The deal would work as a massive boost for Massimiliano Allegri’s side as that would remove the ex-Everton star’s £9m annual salary from the wage bill.

Lukaku would be joining a star-studded Fenerbahce side that also signed Nathan Ake and Vedat Muriqi this summer.

The ex-West Brom star will also be linking up with the likes of Ederson, Milan Skriniar, Caglar Soyuncu, Mert Muldur, Nelson Semedo, N’Golo Kante, Matteo Guendouzi, Fred, Marco Asensio and Kerem Arkturkoglu.

Lukaku amassed a total of 15 goals and two assists in 59 appearances across both stints at Chelsea.

Sports.title: ‘Let another gem down’ – Chelsea fans fume as academy hero Trevoh Chalobah completes shock transfer exit to Como
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans have fumed at the club for letting academy hero Trevoh Chalobah complete a move to Como.

Chalobah joined the club at the age of eight and worked hard to become a key first team player.



The 27-year-old ended up making 151 appearances for the Blues but the England star clearly wasn’t in Xabi Alonso‘s plans.

The club accepted a £31million bid from Serie A club Como and he has now left in a permanent move.



Some Chelsea supporters aren’t happy that another club prospect has been axed and said Chalobah “doesn’t deserve” to be sold.

The club have already cashed in on Tyrique George this summer, while the likes of Alfie Gilchrist and Carney Chukwuemeka left last year.



One wrote on X: “Chalobah doesn’t deserve to leave Chelsea, man loved the club with his whole heart, even when they sent him on loan and wanted him back, he never hesitated to come back. You let another gem down again.”

Another said the exit was “hard to take” and questioned why he had been sold before Benoit Badiashille and Axel Disasi.

A third added: “Two decades at the club just to get forced out to Como so the board can balance the books. Modern football is completely soulless.”

And a fourth wrote: “He wasn’t treated as he should. This young lad loved this club. You guys just wanted him out. I am not happy with that decision.”



And one commented: “If Chelsea cared about players who have team cultural values they would never sell him. Sad.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chalobah has already broken his silence on the move as he prepares to link up with boss Cesc Fabregas, an ex-Chelsea Premier League winner.

In an emotional post, he wrote: “After 18 years, it’s time to say goodbye to Chelsea. I arrived as a nine-year-old with a dream, and I leave as a man who’s lived that dream in ways I never imagined.

“This journey tested me, lifted me, and strengthened me. To every teammate, coach, staff member, and supporter, thank you for shaping me.



“I gave everything I had, and I’m proud of the person this club helped me become.

“To the young players: the path won’t always be smooth. But stay ready, stay positive, and keep your faith. God’s timing is always right. Thank you all, truly, with love and gratitude.”

Chelsea added: “Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Trev for his years of loyal service and wish him the very best in his next chapter in Italy.”

It will be the second time Chalobah has played abroad after previously going on loan to Lorient in France for the 2020-21 season.

He also spent the 2024-25 campaign with Crystal Palace before returning to Chelsea and playing 47 times in all competitions last season.



Chalobah helped Chelsea win the Uefa Conference League in 2025 and the Club World Cup last summer.

Sports.title: Rodrigo de Paul shows support for Lionel Messi with emotional goal tribute following death of Argentina legend’s dad
Sports.content:
RODRIGO DE PAUL showed solidarity with Lionel Messi by paying an emotional tribute to his late father.

Messi‘s dad and agent, Jorge, sadly passed away at the age of 86 in the early hours of Saturday morning.



He had been battling a long illness and died in a hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina.

Following the tragic news, Messi missed Inter Miami‘s Leagues Cup defeat by Monterrey.



The David Beckham-owned club paid tribute with a minute’s silence before kick-off, while players also wore black armbands and Jorge’s name was shown on screens at Nu Stadium.

But international and Inter team-mate De Paul added his own heartfelt homage to his close friend.

After scoring the game’s opening goal from range, the 32-year-old took off his shirt and revealed a second Inter Miami shirt with Messi’s name on the back.

He pointed towards it on his back and swivelled to show it to fans around the ground.

Luis Suarez was missing the game through suspension, but paid his own tribute to his former Barcelona team-mate by saying Jorge would continue to watch over his son “with pride, as he always did”.

Fans also displayed banners with poignant messages to the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner.



The club added: “Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family,” while also adding a black ribbon to their social media pages.

Jorge played a huge role in convincing Barcelona to sign Messi during a trip to Spain when the would-be football great was just 13 years old.

Messi signed for Barcelona at the age of 14, and went on to become the most decorated player of all time.

His list of trophies with the club include 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues, seven Copa del Reys and three Club World Cups, as well as winning six of his eight Ballon d’Or trophies there.

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘hand Marcus Rashford brand new squad number and England World Cup star could STAY under Michael Carrick’
Sports.content:
MARCUS RASHFORD has reportedly been handed the No 14 shirt at Manchester United and could be handed a second chance under Michael Carrick.

Rashford‘s future remains up in the air after returning from his loan at Barcelona with a lack of suitors in the market.



The England star, 28, was previously frozen out of the team by old boss Ruben Amorim.

But United boss Carrick could now be willing to re-integrate him back into the squad after giving him his new number, according to Fabrizio Romano.



The move sends out a message that Rashford is trusted at United, the report adds.

And unless a big comes in from a top European club, the forward will stay at Old Trafford this summer.

Rashford was previously the No 10 at United, before that digit was taken by Mateus Cunha at the start of last season.

He looked almost certain to leave the club after an impressive season on loan at Barca that saw him score 14 goals and assist 10 in all competitions.

Rashford was a key part of the squad that won La Liga under Hansi Flick last season.

But the Spanish giants opted to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle in a £70million deal, leaving Rashford with no clear path.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He then jetted off to the USA with England for the World Cup before the Three Lions were knocked out in the semi-finals by Argentina.

Rashford joined up with United at Carrington this week after his month off and flew with the team to Dublin for their training camp.

It’s understood the player is keen to resurrect his career at United despite a turbulent three years.

The last time he featured for the Red Devils was on December 12, 2024 before he rowed with Amorim over his attitude.



And ironically he could make his return for United in their friendly against Amorim’s AC Milan in Poland on Saturday.

Carrick and Rashford have worked together before after Carrick spent six years with him as a coach.

He was also club captain when Rashford made his debut in February 2016.

Rashford is United’s highest earner on £325,000 a week and has two years remaining on his contract.

Sports.title: England World Cup hero Jude Bellingham watches from stands as brother Jobe takes on Arsenal in pre-season battle
Sports.content:
ENGLAND superstar Jude Bellingham was spotted watching his brother Jobe Bellingham and former club Borussia Dortmund take on Arsenal.

Dortmund defeated Arsenal 3-2 in a blockbuster pre-season friendly at the Emirates.



And Jude, 23, made his presence known in the VIP section of the Gunners’ stadium keeping an eye on the action.

The versatile midfielder got to see Jobe, 20, starting for BVB and playing the entirety of the game against the Premier League champions.



The Real Madrid superstar also witnessed his former club dominate the first half in north London.

Niko Kovac’s side broke the deadlock after just seven minutes thanks to Samuele Inacio’s opener.



And star signing Konstantinos Karetsas doubled the visitors’ lead just before the half-hour mark with a stunning solo finish.

Arsenal responded in the second half with Ethan Nwaneri on 54 minutes after yet another assist by summer signing Christos Tzolis.

But Jude’s former club kept up the pressure and made it three just four minutes later with Joane Gadou.

Viktor Gyokeres put Mikel Arteta’s side back in the game from the penalty spot in the 69th minute but never managed to equalise.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Jude appeared to be in good spirits following the performance of Dortmund, where he spent three years and amassed a total of 24 goals and 16 assists in 132 appearances until his move to Real in 2023.

Jobe, on the other hand, counts five goals in 49 appearances across all competitions since joining the Bundesliga giants last year.

Jude is expected to join Real’s pre-season on Monday after an extended summer break following England’s third-place finish in the 2026 World Cup.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify new left-back target as Red Devils and Arsenal submit transfer enquiries
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED and Arsenal are among several clubs chasing Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys.

And Seys is also capturing attention from the likes of Aston Villa and Newcastle, as well as Portuguese giants Benfica and Porto.



Seys, 21, is a regular for Club Brugge and even forced his way into Belgium‘s World Cup squad, featuring in his country’s quarter-final defeat to eventual winners Spain last month.

SunSport understands that Man Utd, Arsenal and Aston Villa have all submitted enquiries as to Seys’ availability following extensive scouting.



Club Brugge are not in a hurry to sell, with three years remaining on Seys’ contract.

And the Belgian side are set to demand €35million (£30m) for their rising star.



This fee is unlikely to deter United, who want to find a long-term solution in the left-back position.

But it remains to be seen whether club chiefs will pull the trigger on a deal this summer, or wait as they prioritise other business.

Arsenal scouts, meanwhile, have provided boss Mikel Arteta with a detailed report on Seys.

They believe that the 5ft 10in star would suit their system as someone solid defensively who also provides creativity on the flank.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Villa, meanwhile, believe that Seys can provide extra Champions League quality for their squad ahead of the upcoming season.

The Europa League winners, who are set to sell left-back Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain, are particularity impressed with Seys’ technical quality and physical attributes.

Newcastle hold an interest but are currently behind Man Utd, Arsenal and Villa in the race.

Benfica and Porto both feel that they can provide a perfect platform for Seys’ further development, but could find themselves gazumped by the financial might of the Premier League sides.



Seys has made 97 appearances for Club Brugge to date and has already begun the new season with his boyhood club.

But movement around his future could accelerate quickly in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Wing wizard Christos Tzolis continues fine start but Cristhian Mosquera flat-footed in defence
Sports.content:
ARSENAL suffered another pre-season defeat as they missed out on the chance to lift the Emirates Cup.

The Gunners lost 3-2 at their home stadium to Borussia Dortmund.



Samuele Inacio and Konstantinos Karetsas gave the Germans a 2-0 lead at half-time.

Ethan Nwaneri tucked home nine minutes after the break but Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage four minutes later through Joane Gadou.



Viktor Gyokeres fired home a penalty on 69 minutes but Mikel Arteta’s side could not find the equaliser.

Arsenal then won a practice penalty shootout after full-time, with Nwaneri grabbing the decisive effort.



Here’s how SunSport’s Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rated the Arsenal players…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 5

The Spaniard looked shaky against Real Betis in midweek and has been fighting to remain Arteta’s No2 after the arrival of Illan Meslier this summer.

This performance did nothing to try and claim that place as his own.

BEN WHITE – 6

White will have to play a big part of the start of Arsenal’s season, given Jurrien Timber’s ongoing groin issue.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A solid showing from the right-back, but nothing to write home about.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA – 4

Given William Saliba’s injury issues are expected to see him out for a significant period, Mosquera can expect to be called upon a fair bit if Arsenal don’t bring in a new centre-back before the end of the window.

There were some positive moments, but the Spaniard switched off to allow Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind and open the scoring for Dortmund.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

A first pre-season start for the Brazilian after he got just 30 minutes of action off the bench against Real Betis last time out.



A decent enough performance, but he will have been disappointed with his role in Dortmund’s opener.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 4

The Italian had little to no impact on the game and was replaced after 60 minutes.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 6

Arteta is persisting with Lewis-Skelly in midfield, especially with Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi yet to return to training after the World Cup.

However, the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes means the 19-year-old has another top-class midfielder to fight for his place in the squad against.

This performance showed he can do well on the ball, but he will welcome the return of some experienced midfielders alongside him.



KAI HAVERTZ – 6

Started in midfield alongside Martin Odegaard in a technically sound attack-minded lineup.

The German found himself in some threatening positions down the channels but lacked the final ball at times.

Perhaps most noticeably when he tried to square a golden chance to Viktor Gyokeres and played it straight into Alexander Meyer’s grasp.



MARTIN ODEGAARD – 7

The first we have seen of the Gunners captain since the World Cup, where he shone as Norway exceeded the expectations of the masses.

He was only given 30 minutes of action, but looked strong on the ball and keen to pull the strings from midfield.

MAX DOWMAN – 7

It has been no surprise to anyone, but Dowman has been one of the brightest sparks in Arsenal’s pre-season preparations this summer.

He was always trying to make things happen and had some bright moments down the right flank. With Bukayo Saka yet to return, Dowman could be a big part of Arsenal’s start to the season.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 8

The £34m summer arrival might have a bigger part to play on the left wing this season now that Arsenal’s pursuit of Vinicius Junior has come to a crashing halt.



But that might not be a bad thing, as Tzolis has impressed every time he has taken to the pitch during pre-season.

This was another good performance, with some more promising set-piece deliveries and an assist to boot.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 7

The striker finally got his pre-season goal with a second-half penalty.

His first half was less than ideal, as he smashed a free kick miles over, clattered the crossbar from close range and flopped to the floor instead of taking a shot in the box.

However, his second half was much improved as he drove the team forward in search of a comeback.



SUBSTITIUTES

ETHAN NWANERI (for Odegaard, 32min) – 8

Nwaneri is effectively playing for his Arsenal career this summer.

Last season’s failed loan to Marseille showed where Mikel Arteta views him in the pecking order at the club, and the youngster needs to impress if he wants first-team action this term.

His second-half performance might go some way to giving Arteta something to think about, including a well-taken goal and some dangerous play.



ILLAN MESLIER (for Kepa, 45 mins) – 5

Meslier had a chance to stake a claim as the No2, but struggled with a routine corner at the first sign of danger.

Arsenal need David Raya back as quickly as possible.

PIERO HINCAPIE (for Gabriel, 60 mins) – 6

A solid substitute cameo from the versatile defender.

MARLI SALMON (for Calafiori, 60 mins) – 7

The youngster made a brilliant last-ditch tackle to prevent Dortmund from running away with the game.

Salmon is rated very highly at Arsenal and you can see why every time he plays.



FABIO VIEIRA – N/A

JOSH OGUNNAIKE – N/A

CEADACH O’NEILL – N/A

GABRIEL MARTINELLI – N/A

GABRIEL JESUS – N/A

Sports.title: Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'
Sports.content:
Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'

Mikel Arteta has been asked if fans can expect more signings before the transfer window closes with Arsenal still in the market for a new defender

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal are in the market for more signings (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta has admitted that Arsenal are pushing to sign more players before the end of the transfer window.

The Gunners have spent more than £100million on new players this summer. Piero Hincapie's loan move from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent in a £34.5m deal, Christos Tzolis made the £34m switch from Club Brugge, Illan Meslier has signed after his Leeds contract expired, and Bruno Guimaraes has joined for £75m from Newcastle.

But Arsenal, who go into the season as the reigning Premier League champions, are not expected to stop there and want to bolster their squad with more additions in the coming weeks. Indeed, following the Gunners' 3-2 pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, Arteta revealed the club remain active in the summer window.

"Well, that's what we're trying to do [sign more players]," Arteta said. "If we have the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal have conceded six goals in their last two pre-season matches; three against Dortmund and then three in the 3-1 defeat to Real Betis last Wednesday. In both matches, the Gunners looked open at the back and in truth Dortmund and Betis could have scored more than three each.

View 2 Images Jurrien Timber and William Saliba are still out (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Although it is just pre-season, concerns have been raised about Arsenal's capabilities in defence without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, with Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White both struggling in the Betis and Dortmund matches. Ezri Konsa has been listed as a top target as the Gunners look to strengthen at the back, though Aston Villa are determined to keep the £35million-rated England international.

When asked if a defender is a position the Gunners are trying to sign, Arteta added: "I wouldn't go there just to put an isolated there. We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today.

Arsenal go up against Como in their fourth pre-season fixture on Wednesday. They then face Manchester City in the Community Shield next Sunday before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry City.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star and current transfer target both sent off in pre-season brawl
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star and current transfer target both sent off in pre-season brawl

The pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Batis saw three red cards shown just before half time.

View 2 Images Both Antony and Alex Scott were sent off during the pre-season friendly. (Image: Fran Santiago/Getty Images))

AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott was one of three people sent off during the pre-season friendly against Real Betis on Saturday. The England international was involved in an argument with former Manchester United man Antony, who was also shown a red card.

‌



The two teams met in Spain as they prepare for the new season. But an incident just before the half time whistle means that both teams would play the rest of the game with 10 men.

‌



It unfolded with Real Betis' Nelson Edossa reacting to a foul from Bournemouth defender Bafode Diakate. The Real Betis man kicked the ball at the Cherries' player from close range, which prompted a response from other Bournemouth players. That's when Antony got involved.

‌

It emerged at the interval that new Bournemouth manager Marco Rose had also been shown a red card during half time, forcing him to observe the second half from the press box.

Alongside Scott, the club have been linked with potential moves for Aurelien Tchouameni, Manu Kone and Carlos Baleba.

Antony, meanwhile, struggled to leave his mark during his three years at United. He arrived from Ajax in 2022, netting 12 goals in 96 appearances, before heading to Real Betis on loan in January 2025.

Sports.title: Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links
Sports.content:
Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links

Former Manchester United striker Michael Owen has cast doubt on whether Benjamin Sesko is the right long-term centre forward for the club

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has been linked with a Manchester United exit this summer (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Michael Owen has explained why he has “doubts” that Benjamin Sesko could be a long-term option for Manchester United. Sesko signed for the Red Devils last summer from RB Leipzig in a deal believed to be worth around £74million.

‌



There have been reports in recent weeks providing speculation around Sesko’s future at United, with the striker scoring 12 goals during his first season at Old Trafford.

‌



Sesko was granted more minutes for United after Michael Carrick took charge at the start of the year, but did not feature in any of the final four matches of the campaign with a shin injury.

‌



Sesko's future has been a subject of discussion over the summer, with reports in recent days suggesting that Bayern Munich are considering making an approach for the United striker. Sesko is said to be viewed by Bayern as a possible long-term replacement for Harry Kane.

The Mirror's sister-title football.london report that the 25-year-old is currently in Mikel Arteta's plans but the ambitious move for Vinicius Junior indicated a desire to strengthen out wide with other clubs taking note of Martinelli's potential availability.

Christos Tzolis has already joined this summer and has been Arteta's chosen left winger throughout pre-season. The former Norwich City man scored in the win over Girona and assisted Piero Hincapie's headed goal in the defeat to Real Betis.

‌



He produced an impressive Champions League campaign during the league phase, but failed to find the net in any knockout fixture en route to the final.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That impact when it matters seems to be what Arsenal are looking for. Should they identify a suitable option, it would likely trigger a change in approach regarding Martinelli's situation.

The player is thought to be content in north London and retains aspirations of competing at the highest level, but the guarantee of consistent game time and the prospect of being displaced by another new signing could alter that outlook.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is looking at more Arsenal new signings

Arteta addressed the media following the clash in Girona, hinting that further transfer activity could be on the horizon over the coming weeks. Bruno Guimaraes has already been confirmed as an Arsenal signing, though additional deals are still anticipated.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously," the Spaniard added, speaking after a 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona.

"We want to get better like anybody else, and you just can see the transfer market and our opponents, what ‌we are doing. We won't sit still, and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‌



"The margins are very small. Because we want to get better, and the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we ‌don't have in the team."
