Sports.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas says ‘Infantino era is over’ at Fifa
Sports.content:
Javier Tebas says Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is untenable, claiming he is “destroying the very essence of football” while calling for reform at the highest levels of the game.

The La Liga president, who is a longstanding and vociferous critic of the current Fifa regime, said “the Infantino era is over” and called for control of the game to be expanded beyond the current “elite”.

While Tebas’s remarks will surprise no one within the game, they maintain the drumbeat of criticism directed against Infantino following his determination to continue in post despite his secret and subsequently quashed plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

In an interview with French newspaper Le Monde, Tebas repeated his call for Infantino to resign, an appeal first made after the World Cup but before the sell-off scandal. “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed,” he said.

“I’m not saying this because of recent events; I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over. What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold. I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino has received the backing of Fifa in spite of Uefa’s threat to boycott all its tournaments. Photograph: Sam Corum/PA

Infantino is battling to stay in post despite an increasingly coordinated attempt by European football officials and others to unseat the 56-year-old Swiss. Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable, the Norwegian FA has called for the president to stand down and a number of European associations have withdrawn letters endorsing Infantino for another term at the head of Fifa.

Uefa confirmed on Saturday that a “departure payment” had been made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary more than a decade ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum after the alleged relationship, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

On Saturday night, Fifa published a statement accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before the presidential election next March. “Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes,” the statement read.

Infantino has also garnered support from prominent nations outside Europe, including the World Cup co-host Mexico and the finalists Argentina. Uefa say a proposed boycott of all Fifa tournaments remains in prospect, with the women’s Under-20 World Cup due to start in Poland on 5 September.

Sports.title: Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costly
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola told his Liverpool team they have work to do after squandering a 2-0 lead against Monaco to lose a second successive pre-season friendly.

The former Bournemouth coach last managed a game at Anfield almost exactly a year ago in the memorable opener to the 2025-26 Premier League season, a game the Cherries were unfortunate to lose 4-2. Now on his debut in the home dugout, Iraola saw his team produce a similarly open display and lose again. It became clear Liverpool’s longstanding defensive frailties are still to be eliminated.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored in the first half as the hosts exhibited some free-flowing football, but Monaco dominated a second half that became fragmented as Iraola and Monaco’s Filipe Luís made wholesale changes.

“As soon as we have made some changes they start to get tired, we cannot sustain that level, so we have work to do,” Iraola told LFCTV on Liverpool’s “frustrating” regression after a bright start. “They were much better in the second half, in the same way we were better in the first half.”

After Liverpool beat Wrexham and Sunderland during a pre-season tour to the US, a 4-2 defeat against Leeds brought back memories of the struggles of last season. This result will cause some concerns with transfer activity dragging its heels.

Ronald Araújo is at least due to arrive on loan from Barcelona. Although that deal is not yet complete, and Alexis Mac Allister is still to return from World Cup duty, Iraola’s team to face Monaco was strong, with Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Lewis Koumas, 20, the only fringe players to start if you exclude Kostas Tsimikas, back from a loan at Roma. Jérémy Jacquet and Curtis Jones were not considered because of fitness doubts, with Iraola at pains not to “rush” the £50m signing from Rennes into action after a chequered time with injury.

Iraola said: “Jérémy, we were in doubt whether to pick him today, should be fine for the next one. Curtis [there is] something wrong with his hip, [it] didn’t make sense to risk [him].”

Wirtz was sharp, testing Lukas Hradecky with an early shot. Isak’s opener on 16 minutes was met with a hearty cheer from the home faithful, perhaps not surprising given it was just the fourth time the Anfield crowd have been able to celebrate an Isak goal, competitive or otherwise.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola was disappointed after watching Liverpool slip to a second successive friendly defeat. Photograph: Lewis Storey/Danehouse/Getty Images

The strike came after Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai’s slick midfield exchange, the former then finding the Swede, who rifled low into the corner. Koumas and Wirtz both squandered presentable chances, but it was soon 2-0 when the German forced home after a goalmouth scramble.

Iraola cut a relaxed figure on the touchline throughout and was content with his side’s attacking fluidity. The Spaniard’s preference for a high defensive line was evident throughout, though Alisson Becker was tested far less often than Hradecky until he had to face a 44th-minute penalty after Virgil van Dijk’s trip on Aleksandr Golovin. The Russian stroked home the spot-kick himself to make it 2-1 at the break, giving Alisson no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wataru Endo for Ndukwe and Giorgi Mamardashvili for Alisson were the only half-time substitutions from Iraola, who made more sweeping changes just before the hour, with Rio Ngumoha, Milos Kerkez and the summer signing Víctor Muñoz among those introduced.

By that stage it was 2-2, after Mamardashvili had saved from Mika Biereth only to see the striker tap in the rebound. Monaco’s goals were greeted with eerie silence given there were almost no away fans. There were some groans from home supporters frustrated at seeing their side fritter away a two-goal lead and Ngumoha’s name was sung when he came on.

That Ngumoha was selected on the right wing – Mohamed Salah’s old stomping ground – was lost on nobody, nor was the fact that both the youngster and Muñoz were brought on ahead of Federico Chiesa. The Italian did appear after 74 minutes along with Harvey Elliott, who was welcomed warmly back to Anfield after his nightmare on loan at Aston Villa.

Monaco carved out the better chances in the search for the next goal, with Flávio Nazinho firing wide, and Oumar Konaté failing to seize on a good through ball, before their 88th-minute winner stemmed from a corner swung in from the left, which Paris Brunner met with a sweet header.

There was no Anfield roar to push the hosts on to equalise as there would have been in a competitive match, and Liverpool’s side resembled a reserves squad by the end, but it was still a tame finish nonetheless. Only a double-header against Como – the first of which will be played behind closed doors – now remains before Iraola’s competitive debut away at Newcastle on 23 August, with his home league debut coming against Nottingham Forest a week later. The new manager will demand an improvement in the next fortnight.

Sports.title: Arteta expects Guimarães to ‘ignite’ Arsenal and help take team to new level
Sports.content:
The Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta, has backed “warrior” Bruno Guimarães, who to “ignite something different” in the Premier League champions. The Brazil midfielder was introduced to fans ahead of Sunday’s 3-2 defeat by Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup after completing his £75m move from Newcastle.

The 28-year-old, who has signed a four-year deal, bolsters a midfield which already includes Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and Eberechi Eze.

“You can see the immediate reaction,” Arteta told the club website after Guimarães was given a warm reception by supporters. “I think he describes himself as a warrior. I think he’s a warrior with a tremendous quality as well, and intuition and leadership and charisma that is going to help us. That is going to really ignite something different in the team. I think he’s going to push everybody inside the team as well and that’s the type of player that we need.”

After finishing runners-up for three successive seasons, Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for the Premier League title last term, in addition to reaching the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals. Guimaraes watched on against Dortmund as an Ethan Nwaneri strike and Viktor Gyökeres’ penalty were not enough to prevent defeat.

Samuele Inácio, Konstantinos Karetsas and Joane Gadou scored for the Bundesliga side at the Emirates Stadium, before Arsenal won a pre-arranged penalty shootout 5-4.

“Well, (I’m) disappointed that we lost the game,” said Arteta, who gave Ødegaard his first minutes of pre-season following the World Cup and will welcome back his full squad on Monday. I think there were some poor moments where we were not very recognisable, especially in set-pieces and defending actions and timings that we are normally very efficient (in).

“Some other very, very positive attacking combinations, big chances that some of them didn’t finish in anything because of the final pass because they were completely open. But, overall, disappointed because you want to win the games in any context and today, we haven’t managed to do that.”

View image in fullscreen TOPSHOT - Manchester City's Phil Foden falls in a collision with Atletico Madrid's Morten Hjulmand. Photograph: Greg Baker/AFP/Getty Images

The Manchester City manager, Enzo Maresca, praised the impact of his wide players after Antoine Semenyo supplied ⁠assists for Omar Marmoush in a 3-1 victory over Atlético Madrid to wrap up their preseason tour ⁠of Asia.

Marmoush scored ⁠twice in ​the space of three minutes early in the second half before substitute Rayan Aït-Nouri added a third in stoppage ⁠time, helping City overturn a half-time deficit in front of more than 50,000 fans at Seoul World Cup Stadium.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Overall, it was a ⁠very good test against one of the best teams in Europe,” Maresca said. “Credit ​to the players for the effort ‌they have done. From ‌tomorrow pre-season is finished and the real business starts.“

Semenyo finished the Asia tour with four assists in ​three matches, while Savinho also impressed on the opposite flank. Ait-Nouri completed the scoring late on, but Maresca said City still needed greater efficiency in front of goal.

“We need to be clinical. It’s something we need to improve,” he said. “Slowly we ⁠are getting there and with Erling (Haaland) we can be even more ​dangerous. Today Omar ​scored twice. This is a ​boost.“

Maresca also said he was encouraged by the progress made during ​his first three ‌matches in charge ​after succeeding Pep ​Guardiola, with City ending their Asia tour with a draw against Inter, before a penalty-shootout defeat, and victories over a K League All-Stars side and Atlético.

Sports.title: Hibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic win
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes suffered a damaging home debut as Rangers manager with a 2-1 Premiership defeat to Hibernian compounded by striker Youssef Chermiti being carried off the pitch on a stretcher.

David Gray’s side took the lead in the 12th minute with a Josh Campbell penalty after the video assistant referee (VAR) had flagged up that Vanja Dragojevic, making his first Rangers start after signing from Partizan Belgrade, had fouled Jason Kerr in the area.

There was more woe before the break when Chermiti, subject to a failed bid by Galatasaray for a reported club record fee of £22million, having to go off after picking up an injury.

Rangers pushed forward relentlessly and were rewarded in the 85th minute when the Hibs defender Miguel Chaiwa turned the ball past the goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

However, in the third minute of added time, the substitute Callum Wright guided a shot into the far corner for a stunning win.

With Celtic and St Mirren both on six points from two games, Rangers are five behind with McInnes looking for his first win after three matches in the Ibrox hot seat.

Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win at Kilmarnock. O’Neill missed the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend. “He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Kasper Høgh scores the first of his three goals against Kilmarnock. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Three Hearts summer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with a 4-0 win over Dundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.

Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Cláudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.

Hearts made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.

View image in fullscreen Josh McPake turns away after scoring Hearts’ fourth goal against Dundee United. Photograph: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty Images

The home side were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.

Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for Hearts with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.

In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off, Motherwell drew 0-0 at home to Falkirk.

On Saturday, Dundee beat Aberdeen 2-0 thanks to goals from Joe Westley and Joe Bevan while St Mirren edged St Johnstone 1-0 courtesy of Killian Phillips’ penalty.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas: ‘I’m hungry to win, to fight with my teammates for victory’
Sports.content:
Momentarily, Alexia Putellas appears somewhat nervous, stepping inside the cramped conference room in a Kent hotel to see 23 reporters squeezed inside, all eager to hear from the Women’s Super League’s newest global superstar, but she quickly composes herself. Within minutes, she is into her stride, asking for tips about roast dinners and drawing laughs from the room as she jokes that her friends who play for other English clubs have told her they are going to kick her. Welcome to the WSL.

Speaking in English throughout the 20-minute session with ever-increasing proficiency, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner and four-time Champions League winner explains why she has swapped the prestige of Barcelona – where she has been idolised over a trophy-laden 14-year spell – for a team that finished 22 points adrift of the European qualification places last term.

Backed by the ambitious businesswoman Michele Kang, the independently run London City Lionesses have made eye-catching, world-class signings this summer, including the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes – who are also majority-owned by Kang – Putellas’s Barcelona teammate Mapi León and the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps from PSG.

Undoubtedly, though, Putellas is the biggest of them all and the signing that will have made all of women’s football take notice. As a serial winner will Putellas have to be patient for trophies here?

“Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed,” the 2023 World Cup winner says. “I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory. I’m going to try to give my best to the team and let’s see at the end of the season how good we were.”

View image in fullscreen Barcelona made Putellas a parting gift of a photo of herself surrounded by every trophy she’d won while at the club. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

London City Lionesses were promoted to the WSL in 2025, finished sixth last season in their top-flight debut and are yet to win a major trophy. Asked what her expectations are, Putellas says: “I don’t have expectations. I just want the hard work we are doing to speak for itself. It’s a hard competition. Of course, I have a competitive mind and I want to win every game. But I don’t have expectations in this sport. In my opinion, you shouldn’t. Just work in the back[ground] and give everything.”

Putellas was named as the Women’s Champions League’s player of the season after helping fire Barcelona to a fourth European title in six seasons, yet at the age of 32, she still feels she can improve – “Of course, always, day after day, I want to learn things [and] just keep going, I never stop [trying to] be as good as I can,” – but specifically she thinks the WSL can add elements to her skillset.

“It will be different, but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving myself,” she says. “It’s being a more complete player, as much as I can. It’s about learning new things, playing with and against other players and just trying to find where my limits are. It will take time because it’s a new beginning and a big change for me.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas will be hoping to stamp her name on more than just her contract and the camera after joining London City Lionesses. Photograph: London City Lionesses

“[In the WSL] you never know what will be the result of the game; it’s a very competitive league, week after week. I imagine all the games will push you to your limits. It’s a very entertaining league.

“The first conversation [I had with London City] was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete. I made the move for that and just being in other positions that I’ve never been in. In my opinion, this league can give me that.”

When asked if she had sought advice from her former Barcelona teammates, such as the England duo Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze, about what to expect in England, she says: “Well, some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re going to kick me. No, I’m just joking.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

She also chuckled when asked about London’s traffic and expensive property prices, even if she was slightly hesitant reflecting on her first taste of an English fry-up: “Erm, yes. It was quite different. Not the beans, but the sausages and eggs. It was fine.”

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas scored twice when Spain thrashed England 4-0 in June, ending the Lionesses’ chances of automatic World Cup qualification. Photograph: Francisco Ubilla/Reuters

She will have plenty of help when it comes to settling into the London City, with six Spanish teammates and a head coach, Eder Maestre, who she says did a “really good job with Tenerife”. Maestre, yet another coaching export of the Basque Country, was at Tenerife for a year and a half, finishing sixth in his only full season and taking them to fifth by the time he left for England.

Putellas knows there will be differences tactically in the English game and thinks that can help her add even more strings to her bow.

“I really believe that moving to England can give me something more,” she says. “Like, I can control the low blocks and all this stuff; I am used to it playing in Spain. I have already controlled that, so [I want] different kind of games or box-to-box and all this stuff.”

She then apologises for her English – not that any apology was needed – and explains she is still learning the language and working hard to improve it all the time. If her footballing ability continues to enhance too, then WSL defenders had better beware.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a true art form’: Nigeria goalkeeper Maduka Okoye on high fashion and life at Udinese
Sports.content:
When Maduka Okoye visited Paris fashion week for the Jean Paul Gaultier show, taking his seat in the front row alongside rapper Cardi B, the online reaction was swift. Within hours, footage of the Udinese and Nigeria goalkeeper was all over TikTok and Instagram – where his audience now stretches to nearly two million followers – transforming the appearance into a viral cultural moment that crossed beyond the boundaries of football.

Yet ask Okoye to reflect on his sudden explosion into the fashion ecosystem, and he frames it not as a pursuit of celebrity or status, but as a genuine interest in art. “Being at the Paris fashion week was really impressive,” Okoye says. “It was my first time really coming into contact with high fashion, and it was fascinating. It’s a true art form. I enjoyed it immensely and since that moment I’ve become a much bigger fan of fashion than I was before.”

In an era where elite footballers are expected to be multi-dimensional figures – balancing performance on the pitch, personal branding, digital presence, and commercial partnerships – Okoye embodies a generation navigating this global landscape with ease. Crucially, he knows exactly where to steer the ship.

While some athletes run the danger of losing their bearings when the off-pitch spotlight intensifies, the goalkeeper draws a sharp, impenetrable line between his two realms.

“What happens off the pitch is one thing, what happens on the pitch is another,” he says. “You have to separate the two. I never let these two worlds collide. Even though marketing and personal branding are part of the business today, at the end of the day I am a goalkeeper, and my main job is to protect my team’s goal. Outside football, I pursue things that matter to me but my priority and my work remain between the posts. These two worlds don’t overlap. What I do off the pitch has zero impact on what I do on it, and those two spheres will never cross.”

Reinforcing that boundary is the daily environment in which Okoye operates. Playing for Udinese, nestled in the calm, industrious region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, creates a vivid contrast with the flashing cameras of Paris or the hyper-fast churn of social media trends. For Okoye, who grew up in Düsseldorf, Udine offers an essential sanctuary.

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye arrived at Udinese after spells at Sparta Rotterdam and Watford. Photograph: Foto Petrussi/Udinese FC

“I grew up in a big city, so in my heart I am and always will be a city boy, used to the metropolitan rhythm,” he smiles. “However, as you grow older, you learn to appreciate the peaceful side of life. I really like Udine. It’s a human, quiet city. You have your peace there and you can focus 100% on your work. I’m genuinely happy to live here. The serenity in Udine is good for you as a person and makes you feel very comfortable.”

That quiet focus away from the noise is paying dividends on the pitch. Having arrived after spells with Sparta Rotterdam and Watford – where he only made two senior appearances – he has established himself as a cornerstone between the posts for Udinese. In a footballing landscape often obsessed with highlight-reel saves, Okoye is staying focused.

“I believe there is always room for improvement in every direction,” he says. “I’m very happy working here with a great goalkeeping staff. I’m on a good path, learning every day, and I can’t wait to show it on the pitch during the season.”

When asked which goalkeeper impressed him most during the recent World Cup, Okoye says: “I found Spain’s Unai Simón very impressive, especially towards the final stages. Not so much for making hundreds of saves, but for the way he remained inside the game, defending deep balls against France. For me, that was goalkeeping of the highest level.

“As I said, it’s not just about spectacular saves; it’s about managing those details. Overall it was a great World Cup, and for us young goalkeepers it was a fantastic learning opportunity.”

Okoye’s drive to absorb lessons from top-tier athletes extends beyond football. During a recent visit to the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, he met rising Italian Formula One driver Kimi Antonelli, taking the opportunity to study the mechanics of another high-level sport.

“It was fantastic. The whole Formula One experience was extraordinary,” Okoye says. “I think there’s so much an athlete can learn from other sports. Meeting the drivers, especially Kimi, was great. From the outside you only see the race on TV, but behind it there’s an immense amount of work going on. It was impressive to see how much effort and preparation go into competing at that level.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye enjoyed his visit to the British Grand Prix where he presented Kimi Antonelli with his pole position award after qualifying. Photograph: David Davies/PA

Udinese enter the Serie A season with stability and ambition and, in Friuli, that means looking towards Europe. “Everything is possible,” Okoye says. “But I think we should talk about that again in February or March. First we have to get the basics right and take it game by game. Then we’ll see where we are. We certainly have the quality, the players, an excellent staff, and a solid club behind us. Udinese is a club where a player can really grow and make that leap in quality.

“For me, Serie A remains one of the best leagues in the world and I’m grateful to be part of it. The higher the level of the league, the happier and prouder I am to play in it. We’re working hard and can’t wait to compete against the best.”

There is also unfinished business with Nigeria. Watching the World Cup from his living room was far from ideal. “Obviously it would have been better to be part of it, but unfortunately we didn’t qualify,” Okoye acknowledges. “We’ll try again for the next World Cup. I still enjoyed watching it from the outside; I supported Germany, hoping they’d go a bit further. Now we look to the future, and I really hope to be there at the next edition.”

As football continues to evolve into a convergence of sport, entertainment and global culture, figures such as Okoye offer a compelling blueprint for the modern athlete. He is a player capable of sitting in the front row in Paris on Monday, studying a rival on screen on Wednesday, and commanding his penalty box on Sunday – all without losing his sporting identity.

“On a personal level, it hasn’t changed me at all. I’m still the exact same person,” Okoye says. “Of course, when it comes to business and my personal image, a lot of things have changed. Fortunately, I have a great team around me and we try to make the most of these opportunities. But I repeat: who I am hasn’t changed. It’s simply part of my professional journey.”

And what advice would Okoye offer a young footballer dreaming of putting on the gloves and following in his footsteps? The Udinese goalkeeper does not hesitate: “To work hard, believe in yourself, and have faith.”

Sports.title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour
Sports.content:
It began with a text sent during the World Cup. Ertugrul Dogan, the president of Trabzonspor, was watching Egypt when he picked up his phone and messaged his manager, Fatih Tekke. “Coach,” it read. “Do you want Mohamed Salah?”

Tekke’s response was immediate enthusiasm, though Trabzonspor’s initial push for Salah went under the radar with Besiktas looking most likely to land the former Liverpool striker. In Turkish football, Istanbul’s Big Three – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Besiktas – have long held monopoly on the Super Lig’s marquee signings.

Istanbul is not the capital but it is the undisputed financial, cultural and commercial heartbeat of the country and wider region. It came as a shock, then, when Salah opted for Trabzonspor.

The club are by no means minnows. They form part of the traditional Big Four alongside their Istanbul rivals. Yet the football-crazy port city on the eastern Black Sea coast lacks the cosmopolitan lifestyle Istanbul offers. What it possesses instead is devotion. Most Turkish cities do not have a strong local football identity, with residents supporting one of the major Istanbul sides from afar. Trabzon is one of the few exceptions. The entire region eats, sleeps and breathes for its team.

Trabzon is like the Newcastle of Turkey: a proud, working-class city in the north-east with an industrial maritime past, deeply tied to its football club and trying to forge a new identity to adapt to the modern world.

Salah’s arrival has thrust a city that often feels politically and geographically sidelined onto the global stage. This transfer is bigger than football. Trabzon wants to revitalise the city as a maritime trade, tourism and logistics hub. The arrival of the Egyptian superstar ensures an even bigger spotlight on the city.

View image in fullscreen An excited Trabzonspor fan decked in traditional claret and sky blue colours sports sunglasses decorated with new signing Mohamed Salah. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The chaotic scenes at Trabzon airport on Wednesday – when supporters turned the terminal into a sea of red flares, followed by tens of thousands packing Papara Park for Salah’s signing ceremony – demonstrated their fervour.

Salah could easily have accepted lucrative proposals in the Saudi Pro League or Major League Soccer, but their fan culture pales by comparison. Crucially, the 34-year-old remains in a highly competitive league in the Uefa zone; Trabzonspor need only navigate the playoff rounds for a place in the Europa League group stage.

“I am seeing a reception like this for the first time in my life,” Salah told the roaring crowd during his unveiling. “I came here to win trophies. I am here to bring titles to this club.”

Trabzonspor have played the role of disruptors in Turkish football – the Black Sea rebels who broke Istanbul’s stranglehold in the 1970s and most recently won the league title in 2021–22. But never before has a player of this magnitude rejected Istanbul for Trabzon.

View image in fullscreen Salah takes a photo as the fans offer a hearty welcome. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The Turkish top flight is experiencing a renaissance. Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas after a title-winning campaign with Arsenal; Victor Osimhen continues to spearhead Galatasaray’s attack; while Nathan Aké and Mason Greenwood now line up for Fenerbahce. The league is also developing world-class homegrown talent, with Arda Güler at Real Madrid and Ferdi Kadioglu at Brighton serving as prime examples.

Trabzonspor’s pursuit of Salah was executed in the shadows. The club deployed their former winger Mahmoud Hassan – known as Trézéguet – as their secret operative. Salah’s international teammate spoke with the Egyptian captain daily, to help convince him to consider the move.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a cultural element, too: moving to a welcoming, Muslim-majority nation where Salah and his family could feel immediately at home. Trabzonspor locked him into a two-year contract through to June 2028 and disclosed the financial details on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP). Salah will earn a base annual salary of €10m (£8.5m) alongside a guaranteed €7m annual signing bonus, netting him €17m per season (€34m net over two years).

Because wages in Turkey are paid net, with the club covering all tax liabilities, Salah in effect takes home 50% more than his final Liverpool contract. The deal also includes performance add-ons, a 5% agent’s fee on gross wages and an extraordinary image-rights agreement granting Salah a 20% royalty on all personal merchandise sold through the club’s official TS Club retail network.

The commercial return was immediate. Within 24 hours of Salah landing, Trabzonspor sold more than 17,000 season tickets, generating £11m. Dogan confirmed that total projected revenue from tickets, sponsorships and merchandise during the Salah era is expected to approach £22m, in effect self-funding the transfer.

View image in fullscreen Trabzonspor supporters unveil a banner celebrating Salah. Photograph: Nurgul Gunaydin/AFP/Getty Images

Crucially, Trabzonspor did not overextend themselves. Balanced by roughly €95m raised in player sales since last season, the transfer is manageable financially. Salah joins a side on an upward trajectory under Tekke. Languishing in 13th when Tekke took over in March 2025, the team recovered to finish eight points behind the champions, Galatasaray, in third and won the Turkish Cup.

Tekke added the Valencia defender Cenk Özkacar and the Manchester United loanee André Onana in goal and Trabzonspor are in talks with Darwin Núñez.

Taking his favoured No 10 shirt, Salah steps into a side in the ascendant. Yet the challenge remains steep. Galatasaray have won four consecutive league titles, while Besiktas and Fenerbahce have spent lavishly this summer. Trabzonspor will be hoping his arrival serves as a catalyst for a change in fortunes.

For Trabzon and the eastern region, however, Salah’s arrival is far more than a transfer story. The tide could be turning back in the favour of the Black Sea Storm.

Sports.title: Mason Mount injury overshadows Manchester United’s draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Manchester United managed a creditable 1-1 draw with the European champions, Paris Saint-Germain, in a Gothenburg friendly on Saturday but the result was overshadowed by an injury to Mason Mount.

The England midfielder, who joined United from Chelsea in 2023, has been hampered by injury problems since arriving at Old Trafford and he lasted fewer than 20 minutes after starting against PSG.

Mount, 27, appeared to suffer a foot injury in Sweden and, after discussions with coaches on the touchline, left the field to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher. Mount has been restricted to 54 league appearances – many of them as a substitute – during his first three seasons with United.

“He got kicked,” ⁠Carrick told reporters of Mount. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him. ‌We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.“

His side were 1-0 down to PSG at the time of his injury, having gone behind in the second minute through an Ibrahim Mbaye goal even though the French giants were missing many of their star players.

But Bryan Mbeumo equalised in the 32nd minute when Amad Diallo played him in after winning the ball back.

There were more injury concerns for United early in the second half when their 40-year-old goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a right hamstring problem while rushing out to make a clearance.

Mbeumo might have doubled his tally but for the fine form of PSG’s Matvey Safonov but the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering into Joshua Zirkzee way outside his area – an incident that may well have led to him being punished in a competitive match.

There were late chances for Fletcher, Shea Lacey and the captain, Bruno Fernandes, who linked up well with new arrival Youri Tielemans in an encouraging sign for the United manager, Michael Carrick.

View image in fullscreen Mason Mount (back right) started the friendly in Gothenburg but had to be removed with an apparent injury. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

“I enjoyed it,” Carrick told MUTV, United’s in-house television station. “Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should’ve scored more goals.

“It’s good for the boys sometimes to have to problem-solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don’t always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there.”

United have two more friendly fixtures, against bitter rivals Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday and AC Milan in Wroclaw three days later, before launching their Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull on 22 August.

Sports.title: Manchester United interested in signing Leicester star, 18, who is already on radars of Arsenal and Aston Villa - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Digne returns to PSG

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus' World Cup matches, had two years left on his contract with the midlands club, with PSG triggering a release clause.

Digne, who started his professional career with Lille, made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona.

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa

He told PSG's website: 'I am very honoured to be returning to Paris St Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.

'I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years. The working conditions at the Campus are exceptional and reflect the club's ambitions.

'I can't wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team. Once again, I will give my very best to defend the colours of Paris St Germain.'

JAMES DUTTON

Chalobah's Italian Job

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million.

England defender Chalobah departs Stamford Bridge for an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons, as revealed by Window Watch last week.

The 27-year-old has signed a contract until 2031 with the Serie A club, who are managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and are preparing for their first season in the Champions League.

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million

Chalobah made 151 appearances for the Blues, including 47 last term, after joining the club's academy at under-nine level.

He said: 'I'm thrilled and honoured to be here at Como. It's an ambitious, rising project and working with manager Cesc Fabregas again is truly special.

'I can't wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans. I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together'.

JAMES DUTTON

Sunderland target Ipswich keeper

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich Town goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side as Wrexham continue to push for Sunderland keeper Anthony Patterson who is valued at £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Ipswich face Sunderland in the first game of the season.

As well as Palmer, Ipswich have Christian Walton returning from injury and have signed two new Dutch keepers in Kjell Scherpen and Kayne van Oevelen.

The latter may yet go out on loan and Ipswich are among the clubs that have held interest in Newcastle United keeper Nick Pope.

Man City striker in talks with Southampton

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama is in talks to join Southampton on loan for the season.

The former West Ham forward did well on loan at Stoke City last season up until he suffered an ankle ligament injury in January, incurred by a hefty challenge against QPR.

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama is in talks to join Southampton on loan for the season

He has bounced back to full fitness though and has impressed on City's pre-season tour scoring two goals, including a composed finish against Inter Milan, and weighing in with an assist.

The 21-year-old has had interest from a number of Championship clubs including Preston North End, Middlesbrough and Derby County.

Swedish international heads to Hull

Hull City have signed Sweden international Elliot Stroud from Swedish side Mjallby for around £3.5million.

The wing-back has joined on a four-year contract, which includes an option for a an extra year.

The 24-year-old played in all four of Sweden's matches at the World Cup.

West Ham make opening Parrott bid

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and are exploring a deal for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson.

Parrott, their leading goalscorer last season, started on the bench for Alkmaar's opening league game against Den Haag on Saturday.

The Hammers are prepared to break the Championship record of over £17.5million to get Parrott amid competition from Porto.

Nelson has been on the Hammers' radar before and has attracted interest from Fulham and Benfica in this window.

The 26-year-old had an indifferent campaign on loan at Brentford last season.

The Hammers had been pursuing a loan for Sunderland's Simon Adingra but he picked up an injury and has been wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

United keen on Page

Manchester United are interested in signing Leicester prospect Louis Page.

The 18-year-old midfielder has made 21 appearances for the Foxes and won EFL Apprentice of the Year last season.

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also expressed interest in the England Under-20 international but it is understood he wants to join United.

Louis Page has impressed for Leicester and is on the radar of some top sides

Charles closes on Fulham move

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

Read the full story here.

Willock on Besiktas radar

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock remains a target for Besiktas.

The Turkish side are working on an offer for the 26-year-old but believe Newcastle's current asking price is too high.

Joe Willock is a target of Turkish side Besiktas this month

Newcastle are continuing to work on a £13m deal for Marseille's Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

They want an experienced midfielder to work alongside new signings Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba.

Read the latest on Newcastle's summer transfer business here.

Race to sign Tuanzebe heats up

Free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe is attracting interest from Saudi Pro league and Premier League sides.

The 28-year-old centre back had an impressive World Cup on the back of a challenging season with Burnley in the top flight and is ready for a new challenge.

Axel Tuanzebe is drawing a lot of interest from both English sides and abroad

Everton and Brentford have looked at the former Manchester United academy graduate and he has drawn attention from abroad also.

He made 16 appearances and scored one goal last season and spent the two previous seasons with Ipswich Town.

Hamer closes on Cov return

Gus Hamer is due to undergo a medical after Coventry and Sheffield United agreed a £6million deal for the midfielder.

The package for the 29-year-old is worth £6m plus add-ons.

Hamer spent three years at Coventry between 2020 and 2023, becoming a real fans favourite scoring 19 goals in 132 appearances.

Blades manager Chris Wilder hinted last week that Hamer had asked to join Coventry and had already spoken to Frank Lampard. His medical is scheduled for today.

Sports.title: Skydiver narrowly avoids serious injury as he crashes into advertising boards after stunt went wrong before football match
Sports.content:
Skydiver narrowly avoids serious injury as he crashes into advertising boards after stunt went wrong before football match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A skydiver had a lucky escape after colliding with advertising hoardings before a football match in the Netherlands.

Dutch side Go Ahead Eagles had planned to make a spectacular start to the new domestic football season by having the match ball delivered by skydivers for their opening match.

A team of parachutists landed at De Adelaarshorst stadium ahead of kick off against Willem II.

While the majority landed without incident, one parachutist came dangerously close to suffering injury.

Having dropped into the stadium at speed, the man proved unable to slow himself to a halt on the playing surface.

Instead, the skydiver was captured on television drifting towards one of the goals.

Oei, dat ging even niet zoals gepland 🪂🫣#gaewil pic.twitter.com/SoOH3J3HOl — ESPN NL (@ESPNnl) August 8, 2026

A parachutist avoided injury after crashing into advertising hoardings before a football match

The man had been part of a team of parachutists who entered the pitch before Go Ahead Eagles first match of the new season

The Dutch side had been looking to have the matchball delivered in spectacular fashion

Fortunately the man avoided colliding with the goalframe as he quickly pulled their parachute in an attempt to reduce his speed.

The man still struck a stanchion behind the goal and the advertising hoardings, although fortunately their speed had reduced at the time he collided.

Fans cheered after the parachutist got back to their feet and signalled to the crowd that they had avoided injury from the incident.

'Ooh, that didn't land very well,' ESPN's commentator reacted.

'The first injury of the season is a fact. Not of a player, but a parachutist.'

After the pre-match scare, Go Ahead Eagles made a dominant start to the new Eredivisie season.

Despite falling behind in the early stages, the hosts stormed back to earn a 4-1 victory over newly promoted Willem II.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola was 'writing line-ups down' but rejected the Italy job because of 'EXHAUSTION', reveals Paolo Maldini
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola was 'writing line-ups down' but rejected the Italy job because of 'EXHAUSTION', reveals Paolo Maldini

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Pep Guardiola came so close to being appointed Italy manager that he was 'writing down line-ups' before ultimately deciding not to take the role on.

The former Manchester City boss brought an end to his 10-year tenure at the Etihad a matter of months ago, but was touted to take over an under-performing Italian national team.

That fell through, though, and Italian Football Federation technical director and defensive legend Paolo Maldini resigned after a move to appoint Andrea Pirlo also collapsed due to his commercial links with a Russian betting company.

Maldini has now though opened up on how close Guardiola came to taking over the team, revealing that the Spaniard was seemingly on board for a pretty long time.

'(Guardiola) is the coach who best embodies technical, attacking football,' Maldini told Corriere della Sera. 'He had expressed the idea of wanting to coach a national team to some friends.

'We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day.

Pep Guardiola was 'writing down line-ups' ahead of potentially becoming Italy manager

Paolo Maldini met the former Manchester City boss in Barcelona to try and convince him to take over the side

'He was very tempted. He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper.'

The move, though, fell through and left Maldini having to look elsewhere for a new Italy boss.

Fellow former City manager Roberto Mancini was instead appointed, replacing Gennaro Gattuso after the Italians failed to qualify for the World Cup for a third successive tournament.

'Because of exhaustion,' Maldini said, speaking of why Guardiola ultimately turned down the opportunity. 'Guardiola is coming off 10 gruelling years in the Premier League. He had back surgery. He wants to rest.

'But it was a very serious discussion. We studied the squads from the Under-17s upwards.'

This was all despite Guardiola – who spent two seasons in Italy during his playing days with Brescia and Roma and can speak the language – being offered a comprehensive project where he would have significant control over Italian football.

The 55-year-old was understood to be concerned about the commitment required by jumping straight back into management having promised his family that he would live in Barcelona now his time in England has come to an end.

Sports.title: William Saliba-shaped hole grows ever larger for Mikel Arteta after 3-2 defeat by Borussia Dortmund - but Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz are proving they CAN play together, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
William Saliba-shaped hole grows ever larger for Mikel Arteta after 3-2 defeat by Borussia Dortmund - but Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz are proving they CAN play together, writes ISAAN KHAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

For all the focus on Arsenal’s gaping hole at left wing, the leaky backline needs addressing – and fast.

The absence of William Saliba due to a back injury is problematic for the Gunners, highlighted further after this pre-season friendly against Borussia Dortmund.

The north London club have conceded six goals in two matches, not helped by a lack of cohesion at the back.

Riccardo Calafiori’s adventurous runs forward and a midfield with a desire to attack left spaces for the Borussia Dortmund frontline to exploit – and they did.

Take their two first-half goals. Samuele Inacio was easily played through in the area, to poke the ball past Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Then on 29 minutes, Konstantinos Karetsas navigated his way into the area before curling the ball high into the net.

Arsenal have conceded six goals in two pre-season matches and must address their leaky backline fast

Mikel Arteta's side are set to start the season without the influential William Saliba through injury

The Gunners are in the market for a centre back to strengthen their options alongside Gabriel

The ease by which Dortmund were able to breach the defence stood out because of how strong this team typically are defensively. It certainly will have incensed Saliba from where the Frenchman was watching.

His absence for the coming months shifts the team’s balance, which the north London club are keenly trying to address.

It’s understood Arsenal are in the market for a centre-back, with Cristian Romero an option that has been assessed.

The connection between the Argentine and assistant coach Gabriel Heinze is an influencing factor. Though Tottenham, as expected, are staunchly against the prospect.

Saliba’s positioning and ease on the ball may not be replicated, but a defender mirroring those traits would help plug the gap for now.

On Saliba, Mikel Arteta said: ‘When he's been available, he's hit form. And the stats are incredible. So we know that we lost a massive player. The same with Jurrien (Timber). Some of these seven or eight players weren't here today with us.’

At the other end of the pitch, Christos Tzolis clearly fancies his chances as Arsenal still hunt a shiny new forward after losing out on Vinicius Junior.

Tzolis is viewed internally as a winger with a high ceiling, one who can and should push for a first-team slot in the coming seasons.

New signing Christos Tzolis looks eager to take his chance on the left wing after Arsenal missed out on Vinicius Jr

Yet, aware of the circumstances, the Greek is pushing hard to stake a claim right now. After a mixed first half, Tzolis kept trying to get on the ball and make things happen.

His ability to target the byline or cut inside makes him a tough proposition to face, the opposition at times stuck on which way to shield him towards.

The winger’s assist for Ethan Nwaneri, driving towards the byline to put the ball on a plate for his team-mate, pressed home his attributes.

It’s now four goal contributions in four games, including an assist against MK Dons behind closed doors.

The opportunity is there with Gabriel Martinelli, who has not reached the heights of his breakthrough 2022-23 where he struck 21 goal contributions, a possible outgoing this summer.

That was reinforced by Arteta’s substitutions, bringing on Martinelli after 78 minutes, along with Gabriel Jesus and Fabio Vieira who are already at the exit door.

Arsenal are open to Martinelli leaving if the right money is offered, with Galatasaray interested.

Fans excited as Guimaraes adds to formidable midfield

Trotting up the Emirates tunnel with a cluster of club videographers encircling, Bruno Guimaraes emerged. Wearing baggy jeans and an Arsenal jersey, he raised his arms aloft to cheers.

It wasn’t quite the unveiling of say Eberechi Eze last season ahead of Arsenal’s first home league game against Leeds. The circumstances were different, that game a match with ramifications rather than a friendly.

The Gunners also had the added bragging rights of beating Tottenham to the signing of Eze.

So the noise and reaction was understandably different, yet very clear: the Gunners faithful are excited about the Brazilian’s arrival. He’s the club’s first marquee signing of the summer, ending a long saga.

The midfield is already a formidable concoction featuring Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and Martin Zubimendi.

Adding the aggressive edge and propensity to play ambitious passes provides a layer which the Gunners can lack at times.

Add a new attacker and centre-back to the mix, Arsenal will take some stopping.

Bruno Guimaraes was unveiled in front of the Arsenal fans after his £75m move from Newcastle

Gyokeres and Havertz offer Arteta another option

It’s starting to come together, finally. The pair who initially were viewed as separate commodities are slowly becoming an option of being in the same line-up.

Arteta planned to have Kai Havertz as his No1 striker last season before the German’s knee issues paved the way for Gyokeres.

With Havertz now fully fit, Arteta has started the pair together for three consecutive pre-season matches, testing whether they can complement each other for the new season.

There is more work to be done in understanding each other’s positioning and runs. But there were enough signs here to suggest it can be an option.

On 20 minutes, a sublime Odegaard through ball released Havertz down field. He tried squaring it to Gyokeres, before goalkeeper Alexander Meyer snuffed the attack out.

Viktor Gyokeres linked up with Kai Havertz in attack with the pair showing enough to give Arteta another option ahead of the new season

The pass should’ve been better. But the thought was there.

Minutes later, another Odegaard pass reached Havertz, his cross headed wide by Gyokeres. Across the match the pair kept trying to look out for one another to link up.

They are friends off the pitch and there is a willingness to work in unison, rather than a stubbornness to be the main man.

It will be interesting to see how Arteta utilises the pairing once the season officially starts.

Sports.title: England star Jude Bellingham joins his mum to watch his brother, Jobe, play for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal
Sports.content:
England star Jude Bellingham joins his mum to watch his brother, Jobe, play for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England World Cup hero Jude Bellingham's post-season break took him to the Emirates on Sunday afternoon as he watched his brother line up against Arsenal.

Jude is on a three-week sabbatical after helping the Three Lions finish third in North America at the World Cup, with England's players due back training at their clubs this week.

But, before he heads back to Spain to start the new season with Real Madrid, he has found time to pop to Arsenal's stadium to watch Jobe Bellingham line up for Borussia Dortmund in a pre-season friendly.

Jude was seen sat in the stands at the Premier League champions' ground next to his mother Denise as Jobe, 20, played the full 90 minutes.

Jobe has been tipped to follow in the footsteps of Jude, 23, having followed him from Birmingham City to Dortmund – though via Sunderland.

The younger Bellingham brother signed for Dortmund for £32million last summer, making 45 appearances in all competitions though without a goal.

Jude Bellingham joined his mother Denise to watch brother Jobe play for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal

Jobe (left) has been tipped to follow in his brother's footsteps and is currently playing for his former club - the pair posed for a snap after the game

He is a regular at England Under-21 level, and has been tipped to make his senior debut alongside his brother in the near future.

Both players came from humble beginnings at Birmingham, with the Championship side retiring Jude's shirt number – 22 – when he left for Dortmund when he had just turned 17 in 2020.

He travelled over to St Andrew's for a pre-season friendly against Madrid's arch rivals Barcelona last week, giving Blues fans plenty to cheer about as they were given a rare opportunity to see the LaLiga champions in action.

Before kick-off, Birmingham City's official social media account showed Bellingham taking his seat and waving to fans in a touching video captioned: 'Jude. He's home.'

As he raised his arms aloft to greet the adoring fans, Blues supporters loudly bellowed 'Jude' to honour their former starlet and fervently chanted 'he's one of our own' in a special moment for the England midfielder at St Andrew's.

The £113million midfielder cheered jubilantly as he watched his boyhood club triumph over Madrid's rivals, winning on penalties after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Bellingham is expected to play a key role at Madrid again this season, with Jose Mourinho taking over as manager again after the club opted to move on from interim manager Alvaro Arbeloa.

He will rejoin the England camp towards the end of next month for the next international break, which is three weeks long.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta provides gloomy injury update on William Saliba and Jurrien Timber just two weeks before Arsenal's title defence starts
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta provides gloomy injury update on William Saliba and Jurrien Timber just two weeks before Arsenal's title defence starts

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal will be without half of their first-choice back four for the start of the Premier League season, Mikel Arteta has confirmed in a disappointing injury update.

The Gunners knew they would be going into the new campaign without centre back William Saliba, who sustained a back injury while on World Cup duty with France.

The club had already confirmed that his issue would require 'a period of rehabilitation', splitting last season's star central duo of Saliba and Gabriel.

But there had been hope that Timber, who missed the World Cup with the Netherlands, would be fit, but it appears he is still some way away from returning to action.

'I cannot be very precise with that,' Arteta said after Arsenal's pre-season defeat by Borussia Dortmund on Sunday. 'Jurrien is progressing really well, he's on the pitch, he's doing quite a lot right now, but is still weeks away. I cannot say how much.

'William is in rest mode at the moment. For two weeks he had to do almost nothing, don't aggravate the injury. It's going to take some time to heal, we know that.

Arsenal are set for a period of time without William Saliba (left) and Jurrien Timber (right)

'As quick as we have more news we can inform.'

Ben White and Cristhian Mosquera are currently set to deputise for the duo, but Arsenal could go into the market to buy replacements too.

Saliba was captured saying 'my back is gone, my back is gone' after being withdrawn in the second-half of Les Bleus' defeat by Spain at the World Cup, with reports in his home country suggesting that he could be sidelined for an extended period of time.

Arsenal and Saliba are believed to have opted against surgery to heal the issue.

Timber, meanwhile, played briefly at the end of last season but missed the World Cup with a persistent groin issue.

Arteta said: 'We have experienced that in the past, unfortunately. When he's been available, his stats are incredible.

'We know that we have lost an incredible player. Same with Jurrien.'

He added: 'We need to improve with the players that we have.'

Sports.title: Formula One star George Russell reveals he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt as he shares snaps of stunning candlelit proposal - weeks after hinting at marriage plans
Sports.content:
Formula One star George Russell has revealed he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt.

The Mercedes racer shared he proposed to the Spanish businesswoman in a heartfelt social media post.

George shared adorable snaps of the proposal, including one of Carmen showing off her beautiful engagement ring, after he popped the question during a romantic candle-lit dinner.

The official F1 account was among the first congratulate the happy couple, after they got engaged while on a sunny island getaway.

The couple have been together since 2020, with George sharing back in June he was ready to pop the question.

Carmen was born in Spain, and moved to London when she was 18 to study business management and finance from the University of Westminster.

Formula One star George Russell has revealed he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt after six years together

The Mercedes racer shared he proposed to the Spanish businesswoman in a heartfelt social media post, as they enjoyed a romantic candlelit dinner

George had previously credited Carmen with helping him to stay grounded as an F1 driver, and described her as his 'future.'

He told The Times: 'Carmen brings me stability when it comes to racing and also a way to disconnect.

'Without doubt she's my future. So [I hope we'll be married] in due course. It won't be next week, but it won't be longer than five years. So somewhere in that timeframe.'

George also said in March: 'I have a really great group of people around me. Carmen is a huge part of that. She supports me in every way possible.

'When I was in Melbourne and preparing to race she got on the time zone, going to bed at six at night and waking up at three in the morning.

'I'm sure some people prefer going out for dinner with their friends instead. But not only does she support me mentally, she's invested in what we're trying to achieve. And that helps a lot. I feel very fortunate.'

The pair met by chance over a meal six years ago, when she did not know he was a Formula One driver.

Now, having quit her high-flying financial job in London to live with Russell in Monaco, she regularly supports him at races.

George shared adorable snaps of the proposal, including one of Carmen showing off her beautiful engagement ring

George first came across fashion influencer Carmen, when the Spaniard had been set to meet a friend of his for a date in 2020.

'My mate couldn't make it, so I thought I'll swing along to see how it goes,' Russell told The Sun.

'She told me she's from the south of Spain and she wouldn't ever expect someone to know the small place she's from.

'I knew exactly where she was from, so it was quite coincidental.'

The pair quickly bonded, with George having spent a significant amount of time in the city of Jerez in southern Spain where Carmen hails from during his karting days.

When the pair celebrated five years together, Carmen detailed her pride in her partner in a post on social media.

She wrote: 'Five years with the most wonderful person I could ever ask for. Forever proud of who you are and what you do.'

Russell sits third in the F1 standings this season, 59 points behind teenage team-mate Kimi Antonelli and nine behind seven-time world champion and Ferrari ace Lewis Hamilton.

Sports.title: Newcastle add former Tottenham midfielder Joao Palhinha to transfer shortlist as move for Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg ramps up - plus fitness update on Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley
Sports.content:
Newcastle have identified Joao Palhinha as an option in their search for an experienced midfielder to fill the void left by Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

Talks continue over a move for Marseille’s Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and a deal in the region of £13million could accelerate over the next 48 hours.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 31-year-old has indicated he is keen on the switch and new head coach Matthias Jaissle sees the Dane as the potential organiser at the base of his young midfield.

However, there is still work to do on that transfer and alternatives have been identified, including Palhinha. Aston Villa are also interested in the Bayern Munich midfielder, 31, and he looks set to return to the Premier League this summer after spending last season on loan at Tottenham.

Newcastle like the Portugal international and he fits the profile of older head they want to complement new arrivals such as Sean Steur, 18, and Aladji Bamba, 20.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

Joao Palhinha is another experienced midfielder Newcastle are considering to fill the void left by the departures of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali

Tino Livramento is not expected to be fit for Newcastle's season opener as he recovers from the injury he picked up on England duty at the World Cup

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
