World.title: Iraq arrests senior Trade Ministry official Hashem Al-Sudani
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi prosecutors detained Hashem Al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company (GAMCO), on Sunday for suspected embezzlement in a contract with the Ministry of Defense.

The contract’s specifics, including its value and the particular alleged infractions under investigation, have not been released. Al-Sudani’s arrest is part of Iraq’s growing anti-corruption effort, which targets prominent government officials, legislators, and business leaders.

The new arrest comes as Baghdad ramps up the “Dawn Crackdown,” an anti-corruption operation that began on June 28 by Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to probe big crimes involving public contracts and state finances.

The initiative has gained traction among senior and politically connected individuals.

Recently, police arrested former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court as part of a separate inquiry.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and reclaiming public monies, with authorities attempting to show that probes would extend to officials regardless of party or institutional affiliation.

Corruption has long been a major impediment to Iraq’s growth, depleting state resources, degrading public services, and deterring private and international investment.

The ongoing arrests imply Baghdad’s new effort is spreading to official institutions, but anyone arrested or interrogated has not been convicted and is still subject to due process.

World.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region.

The World Health Organization denounced a strike that destroyed a warehouse in Ukraine holding medical supplies.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, both countries are ramping up long-range strikes. The resulting civilian casualties led the United Nations to condemn both sides last week.

Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at Ukraine this week.

“More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he added.

The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, said Zelensky.

Twenty-three people were also wounded, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov, sharing images of a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.

Zelensky said eight people had also been wounded overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.

He condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region that wounded nine people, including four children.

– WHO condemns warehouse strike –

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro had been destroyed in strikes on Friday.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros in a post on X Sunday.

“Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!”

In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.

Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also wounded, he added.

Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, said Shuvaev.

A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.

On the front line, the Russian army said Sunday they had captured two small villages in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. The claim has not yet been independently verified.

One of them, Vasiutynske, is about 10 kilometres (six miles) from the city of Kramatorsk, a Ukrainian urban and logistical hub.

– Zelensky defends strikes –

Zelensky, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s responses to Russia’s attacks — including strikes on oil refineries, air-defence systems and radar stations — as “truly just responses”.

“The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said.

On Thursday, United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned both sides for their repeated attacks on civilian areas.

“Attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are a clear violation of international humanitarian law, and must stop immediately,” he said.

The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

World.title: Como sign England defender Chalobah from Chelsea
World.content:
Milan – Como have completed the signing of England centre-back Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for a reported fee of 30 million euros ($34.5 million), the Serie A club announced Sunday.

The 27-year-old has penned a five-year deal with Cesc Fabregas’s ambitious side, who will play in the Champions League for the first time this season.

“I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans,” said Chalobah, who made 151 appearances for Chelsea.

“I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together.”

Como pipped AC Milan and Juventus to Italy’s fourth and final Champions League place last season.

Scudetto holders Inter Milan had also been heavily linked with a move for Chalobah, before reportedly deciding the asking price was too high.

“Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club,” said Como coach Fabregas, a former Chelsea midfielder.

“He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Chalobah was part of the England squad which finished third at the World Cup last month, after receiving a late call-up as a replacement for the injured Tino Livramento.

He could make his Como debut when they visit Udinese in their Serie A opener on August 22.

World.title: Iraq steps up digital transformation of banking and customs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is speeding up preparations to digitize its financial and customs systems, with Finance Minister Falih Sari and Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasser Hussein considering tighter integration of electronic payments, customs processes, and government financial data.

The conference, which included members from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), aimed to accelerate electronic linkages between Iraq’s customs and payment systems.

Sari urged authorities to speed up implementation as part of measures to modernize financial management, streamline trade processes, and create a more efficient environment for companies and investors.

The talks also focused on increasing cooperation between fiscal and monetary agencies, including digital data interchange and upgrading Iraq’s banking infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability and meeting government financial responsibilities.

The revisions are part of Iraq’s larger transition from cash-heavy and paper-based institutions to a more integrated digital financial infrastructure.

Baghdad sees modernization of banking, payments, and customs as more crucial as the government strives to bring its financial system closer to international norms, increase transparency, and make it simpler for Iraqi and foreign enterprises to do business.

The drive also supports broader banking changes in Iraq, as the government seeks deeper connectivity with the international financial system and encourages private sector development.

World.title: PSG sign France full-back Digne from Villa
World.content:
Paris – Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne has joined Paris Saint-Germain on a three-year deal, the European champions announced Sunday.

The 33-year-old French international, who grew up in the Paris region, returns to PSG, where he played for two seasons between 2013 and 2015.

“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain,” Digne said in a statement on the Ligue 1 champions’ website.

“I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.

“I can’t wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team.”

After PSG, Digne spent time on loan in Serie A with Roma before signing for Spanish giants Barcelona, who were then coached by current PSG boss Luis Enrique.

He moved to the Premier League in 2018, firstly with Everton, then four years later joining Aston Villa.

At Villa Park, he won the Europa League under Unai Emery last season.

Capped 64 times by his country, Digne became France’s first-choice left-back over the course of the 2026 World Cup.

Digne is PSG’s second major signing of the summer transfer window after fellow French international Maghnes Akliouche arrived from Monaco.

He could make his debut for his new club against his former employers Aston Villa on Wednesday in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg.

However, long term it is likely his principal role will be to provide cover for PSG’s starting left-back, Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Former Iraq finance minister Taif Sami summoned in widening corruption probe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami has been officially summoned by a court and put on a judicial wanted list as authorities broaden a corruption probe that has reached high political and government officials, according to sources.

Sami is thought to be outside Iraq and has not been captured.

The alleged court action is part of an inquiry and does not prove misconduct or lead to a conviction.

The revelation comes as Iraq’s new administration steps up its anti-corruption effort, which has already resulted in the detention of important political personalities and bureaucrats.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, often known as Abu Mazen, was detained in Baghdad recently on suspicions of misusing public contract funds.

A close acquaintance was also arrested as part of the inquiry.

The new charges stem from a big operation in Baghdad’s highly protected Green Zone in late June, when Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service detained numerous officials as part of a larger corruption probe.

According to reports at the time, authorities were looking into claims involving government contracts and huge sums of public money.

Sami, the previous administration’s finance minister under former Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammad Shia Al-Sudani, was one of Iraq’s most significant economic leaders, responsible for handling the federal budget, government expenditures, and financial ties between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

The purported summons therefore implies a potentially major extension of the probe against individuals who formerly held top positions inside the Iraqi state.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and improving state institutions as part of its domestic agenda to boost public trust and reassure international investors.

With the arrest of Abu Mazen and the rumored legal proceedings against Sami, Iraq’s anti-corruption campaign is gaining traction among established political players.

However, the claims are still being examined, and individuals who are being arrested have the right to due process.

World.title: Lionel Messi bids farewell to father who guided his glittering career
World.content:
Rosario – Argentina football icon Lionel Messi bid farewell Sunday to his father Jorge, the global star’s emotional anchor and agent since childhood who passed away following a battle with cancer aged 68.

The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner touched down on a private flight from Miami late on Saturday with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo and their children.

A private ceremony with close family and a few Argentina teammates took place at a cemetery in the town of Perez, adjacent to Rosario, later Sunday.

The gates of the town’s El Prado cemetery displayed handwritten messages from fans — “Stay strong, Leo, we love you” and “Stay strong, Messi family” — alongside a large floral wreath.

Messi’s teammates rallied around their captain following the announcement that Jorge Messi had passed away late Friday at a clinic in Rosario.

“It will surely do him good for us to be there,” Boca Juniors midfielder Leandro Paredes told journalists after his team’s match on Saturday.

“I need to speak with a few of my teammates to see if we go now or sometime tomorrow.”

According to media reports midfielder Rodrigo de Paul — a close friend of Messi and his Inter Miami teammate — travelled to Argentina.

After scoring a goal in a 2-1 defeat to Monterrey in Miami on Saturday, De Paul paid tribute by taking off his shirt to reveal Messi’s number 10 jersey.

There was a handful of fans outside the cemetery, including 15-year-old Lucas Blanco, who hung a sign reading “Stay strong, Messi” on the gate.

“He has brought so much joy to this country, now it’s our turn to give a little back and offer him some comfort,” he said.

“We drove 700 kilometres to be here. We wanted to stand by Leo during this time,” said Carlos and Ana, a couple who travelled from Tres Arroyos, a town south of Buenos Aires.

The cause of death was not disclosed, but local media reported that Jorge Messi had been suffering from cancer.

His unusual absence from the World Cup in June had already attracted attention.

Messi’s family asked the media for “humanity” during the tournament amid persistent rumours over Jorge’s health.

After bursting into tears after scoring against Algeria, 39-year-old Messi had admitted to dealing with “a situation outside of sports”.

“I went through a few difficult, complicated days,” he later acknowledged. “But I am grateful to the entire delegation and my teammates, because they stood by me, as always.”

Immediately after the World Cup final defeat against Spain, Messi returned to spend a few days with his family in Rosario.

– Humble beginnings –

A guiding figure throughout his son’s career, Jorge Messi was his first coach who left everything behind to accompany his son to Spain.

A metalworker in Rosario, 340 km north of Buenos Aires, Jorge managed youth teams at the small local club Grandoli.

He was the one who introduced Argentina’s future captain to the game aged four on vacant lots where local kids played.

His life changed course in 2000 when Barcelona invited the young prodigy, then aged 13, to Catalonia to continue treatment for a growth hormone deficiency while playing for the club’s youth teams.

Jorge left behind his job in Argentina, his wife, and his three other children to settle in Spain with Lionel.

“When we arrived in Barcelona, I used to lock myself in my room to cry alone, and my father did the same — either without me seeing him or thinking I didn’t see him. We pretended we were both fine, but we were struggling,” Messi later said.

His father was later the agent who negotiated contracts on his behalf, from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami.

Messages of sympathy have poured in since Saturday from the football world, including from the clubs Messi played for and the Spanish Football Federation.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) ordered a minute’s silence before matches and that black armbands be worn at games across all age groups for the week.

World.title: Iran Guards say won’t reopen Hormuz without US meeting Tehran’s demands
World.content:
Tehran – Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that they would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States complied with a list of demands, including paying compensation for war damage.

Iran has effectively blockaded the crucial energy conduit since the United States and Israel attacked it in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage, striking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route.

Attacks in the waterway, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire, and mediators have urged both sides to return to the terms of a subsequent June memorandum that set out a path for peace talks.

Iran’s security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr had laid out on Saturday a list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the “war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq”.

He also demanded the lifting of a US counterblockade of Iranian ports, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, the Tasnim news agency reported.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Sunday said their strategy was to maintain the closure “until the enemy accepts all our conditions… the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway”.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who had also said the reopening of Hormuz was subject to conditions, denied on Sunday that Iran was negotiating with the US, saying they were merely “exchanging messages” via intermediaries.

– Hormuz strikes –

Traffic through Hormuz has dropped significantly amid the ongoing attacks.

The United Arab Emirates on Saturday accused Iran of striking a tanker belonging to its national oil company as it transited the strait.

And later on Saturday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a ship was hit by a projectile off Oman, though it was unclear whether they were referring to the same ship.

Oman’s foreign ministry on Saturday condemned “repeated attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz”, without naming Iran.

It also said “ongoing negotiations regarding navigation arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz are proceeding”, and warned against any actions that might jeopardise the progress.

The June Iran-US deal had said Tehran and Muscat would hash out future arrangements for the strait in discussion with other Gulf countries and “in line with the applicable international law”, which generally forbids tolling in such waterways.

Araghchi had said that discussions with Oman over management of the strait were “approaching the final stages”.

– Houthi attacks –

As Iran throttles traffic in Hormuz, its Houthi allies in Yemen have declared a parallel maritime blockade on Saudi ports in the Red Sea, the oil-exporting giant’s only other maritime route.

The Houthis announced on Sunday that they had struck a Saudi oil facility on the country’s Red Sea coast, after the Gulf kingdom said it had extinguished a fire at the site.

Saudi Arabia has long propped up Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war against the Houthis, which was paused by a UN-backed 2022 accord that has appeared to break down since the rebels declared their blockade last month.

A medical source in government-held Mokha said three civilians and eight military personnel were killed and a further 32 people wounded on Sunday, with all the civilian casualties resulting from Houthi strikes on the Yemeni city’s port.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted “Saudi enemy” troops and equipment in the area with missiles and drones.

– Security agreement –

The Middle East war has proven an unprecedented challenge to Saudi Arabia’s carefully cultivated reputation for stability and security, as well as its ambitious plans to diversify its economy away from reliance on petroleum.

On Friday, the kingdom signed a joint defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan, including a NATO-style clause that considers any attack on one country as an attack on all.

Turkey’s foreign minister said on Saturday he expected Egypt to also join the pact, calling the country a “natural partner on all issues”.

“We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members,” Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said in an interview.

A drone struck US assets at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean last month, marking the first such attack on Egyptian territory since the outbreak of the Iran war.

Fidan said the agreement was not aimed at a specific country, while Pakistan’s foreign ministry said Friday that it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

World.title: Police search 26 locations tied to banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Police searched 26 locations across Sopore in north Kashmir on Sunday in a coordinated crackdown on banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K, seizing documents, literature and electronic devices as part of a probe into its alleged links to terrorist outfits and youth radicalisation.

The search targeted residential and other premises linked to Jamaat-e-Islami J&K members and activists. No arrest was reported till filing of this report. âThe operation was conducted in accordance with due legal procedure and prescribed protocols,â police said.

Police said the seized material was being examined to establish further linkages and activities connected with the proscribed organisation. The operation was part of efforts to dismantle networks linked to banned organisations, separatist activities and terrorist funding.

Distinct from Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Jamaat-e-Islami J&K has a history tied to regional separatism and has long had a support base in Sopore. Union government first declared it an âunlawful associationâ in Feb 2019 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. In Feb 2024, the ban was extended for five years, with the government saying the organisation continued activities against Indiaâs security, integrity and sovereignty.

Sundayâs search followed a sweeping crackdown in Kashmir after the fatal shooting of a J&K police head constable on duty in Anantnag town on July 22 â the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre in April 2025. World.title: 'Ranchi police fully prepared': Jharkhand braces for students' protest march to Assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Sunday said it was prepared for the planned Assembly march by JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi, assuring protesters that they would not face action if the demonstration remained peaceful.

The assurance came hours after a second round of talks between student representatives and the state government, with the administration agreeing to consider some of their key demands but failing to resolve the issue of a CBI probe into the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination.

Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said adequate security arrangements were being made as a large number of students are expected to participate in Mondayâs âVidhan Sabha gheraoâ.

âPrecautionary force deployment will be carried out effectively; the Ranchi Police is fully prepared. There will be a large number of students. Instructions have been issued to all Ranchi Police personnel that if the protesters conduct themselves peacefully, no inconvenience will be caused to anyone,â Rana said.

âHowever, if anyone attempts to resort to violence, appropriate legal action will be taken against them,â he added.





Rana also clarified a controversy surrounding a viral video that appeared to show security personnel carrying a pellet gun.

âIf a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video - what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, coloured balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun,â he said.

The police officer said any pellet gun, if deployed, would be kept strictly for emergency situations.

Meanwhile, student leader Ravindra Paswan said the government had agreed to consider cancelling three examinations - the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, JPSC Backlog 2023 and JPSC Backlog 2025.

Student are set march towards the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha on Monday after government agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC, JPSC Backlog 2023, and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams but rejected the demand to scrap the CGL examination, saying it was conducted under court orders and selected candidates are already employed.

Student leader Kunal said the âVidhan Sabha gheraoâ would be held peacefully but maintained that the demand for a CBI inquiry into the CGL examination remained non-negotiable.

âLet me clarify that our Vidhan Sabha gherao will continue peacefully. Our demand is for a CBI inquiry; we will not compromise on that,â Kunal said.

The students have been protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations and are demanding accountability and reforms in the examination process.

World.title: 'Reflection of public anger': Suvendu Adhikari after Mamata Banerjee faces protests, called 'chor'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday described the protests against his predecessor,

, at Hailsahar in North 24 Parganas as a reflection of âstrong public anger.â

Mamata Banerjee faced protests earlier in the day when a group of protesters allegedly surrounded her vehicle, raised âchor-chorâ (thief, thief) slogans and hurled mud and slippers at her car. She had gone to meet the family of a

(TMC) worker who allegedly died in police custody.

Denying any involvement of the ruling BJP in the incident, Adhikari said, âYou (Mamata Banerjee) have committed so much theft, you will have to hear people call you a thief.â

He further claimed that the TMC supremo went to Halisahar without being invited by the deceasedâs family and that the TMC worker's family was "satisfied" with the police and administration.

âDo not do this when the family is shutting the door. You are saying you will enter by force. Do it when people seek your help or intervention. This is the time for development. Do not go anywhere and do anything that disrupts normal life,â he added.





The chief minister also questioned why his predecessor had not visited the family of âAbhayaâ (fearless), the moniker given to the RG Kar rape and murder victim, on the second anniversary of her death.

âYou could have gone to Abhayaâs house today. You could have gone to Ratna Debnath with a towel around your neck and apologised, saying you had made a mistake and asking for forgiveness. I believe she would have forgiven you,â Adhikari remarked.

Ratna Debnath, Abhayaâs mother, is now a BJP MLA. She had previously said she contested the recent West Bengal assembly elections to fight for justice and accused Mamata Banerjee, who was the chief minister at the time of the RG Kar incident, of failing to save "Abhaya."

Meanwhile, Adhkari accused Mamata Banerjee of trying to sabotage probe into the RG Kar incident, and questioned why would people not be angry with her.

He asked: âYou (Banerjee) killed Abhaya, went to destroy evidence and tried to buy her family with Rs 10 lakh. If people threw mud at your car, what else would they throw? Flowers?â

Earlier, Mamata Banerjee was forced to pass through a police cordon as the demonstration briefly turned the road into a charged political theatre, with rival sides trading allegations of conspiracy, provocation and administrative failure.

âMy car has been attacked with stones, shoes and mud. This is nothing but a conspiracy. I had informed the police that I would be coming, but despite that, no security measures were taken,â she told reporters after reaching the area.

The former chief minister also alleged that "large bricks" had been thrown at her vehicle.

Mamata Banerjee also trained her guns on CM Adhikari, saying she had "no particular anger" against the police but alleging that the force was being used at the behest of the state government.

âThe police are protecting the lumpens. Bengal has fallen into the hands of lumpens,â she added, saying her party would pursue the matter.

World.title: ED director Rahul Navin gets 1-year extension
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rahul Navin gets one year extension as ED director. His 2-yr fixed tenure was coming to an end this month, now extended till 13 Aug 2027.

According to a notification issued by the DoPT on Saturday, âAppointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved extension in tenure of Rahul Navin, IRS, as Director of Enforcement in the Directorate of Enforcement for a period of one year beyond 13.08.2026 i.e.

up to 13.08.2027, including extension in service beyond the date of his superannuation i.e. 31.07.2027, or until further orders, whichever is earlier.â

After three years as director ED, Navin, a 1993 batch officer of the Indian Revenue Service (Income Tax), stands a chance of getting two more extensions and serve till Aug 2029, all through the present tenure of the Modi govt with next general elections due in April-May 2029.

As per service age Navinâs retirement is due on 31 July 2027, but tenure of ED director can continue beyond that as in the case of his predecessor Sanjay Mishra.

Rahul Navin hails from Bihar and had an outstanding academic distinction with a degree in BTech and MTech from IIT Kanpurand an MBA from Swinburne University of Technology, Melbourne.

On 15th September 2023, he assumed charge as Director (In-Charge) and was appointed as Director of ED on 14th August 2024.





He has also written a book on "Information Exchange and Tax Transparency: Tackling Global Tax Evasion and Avoidance" while being in the tax policy division of the finance ministry.

As ED director, Navin has laid down a new roadmap for his officers of completing all investigations within two years and ensuring attached properties are auctioned and restituted to the rightful claimant and victims of frauds â whether it be banks or individuals â within a specific timeframe.

World.title: DGCA to conduct preliminary probe into Baramati aircraft runway excursion: Centre
World.content:
No injuries as training aircraft veers off runway at Baramati airport

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The ministry of civil aviation (MoCA) said on Sunday that a team from aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), is being sent to Maharashtraâs Baramati airfield, where a Cessna training aircraft was involved in a runway excursion earlier in the day.âThe air safety team from the DGCA is going to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident,â the ministry statement read.MoCA further noted that the plane appeared to have sustained damage to its propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear, while no fatalities or injuries were reported.âThere were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities,â the statement added.According to the ministry, the incident occurred around 12:25 pm when the Cessna C172, bearing registration VT-SEX and operated by flying training school Academy of Carver Aviation, veered off the runway at Baramati airfield.The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise.It was under the command of flight instructor Captain Chirag Shashikant Doifode, with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.The plane had taxied out at around 12:09 pm for the scheduled training exercise.âDuring the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out.âSubsequently, the aircraft lined up at the threshold of runway 11 and another rejected take-off exercise was carried out,â the statement noted.During the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion, according to the ministry.

World.title: 'Attempt to murder': TMC MPs blame BJP for attack on Mamata Banerjee's car, claim CM Suvendu link
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(TMC) MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee on Sunday accused the

of being behind an alleged attack on former West Bengal chief minister

's vehicle, after stones and other objects were reportedly hurled at her car in North 24 Parganas.

Mamata Banerjee was travelling to meet the family of a TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody when the incident took place. TMC MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Dola Sen were accompanying her.

Kalyan Banerjee described the incident as an "attempt to murder" and alleged that the attack was targeted at Mamata Banerjee. He also accused the police of remaining silent spectators while the incident took place.

"The entire car, there was not a single second when stones were not thrown.

Stones were thrown every moment, targeting Mamata Banerjee to assault her," Kalyan Banerjee said, as cited by news agency ANI.

He alleged that hundreds of BJP workers were present at the spot and claimed that the incident took place in the presence of police personnel.

"Hundreds and hundreds of BJP workers were there, and police were remaining silent spectators, absolutely silent spectators," he said.

Kalyan Banerjee also alleged that there was a direction from West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari behind the incident.





"Of course there was a direction given by the CM Suvendu Adhikari," he said.

Abhishek Banerjee alleges ' political violence '

TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee also accused the BJP of unleashing political violence in West Bengal and alleged that Mamata Banerjee was "brutally attacked" while travelling to meet the family of the deceased party worker.

In a post on social media, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that the incident reflected a wider law-and-order failure in the state.

"And now, a former Chief Minister of the state, who was on her way to meet the grieving family, is brutally attacked by goons planted by BJP," he said, as reported by ANI.

He questioned the police response and said the incident represented a "failure of governance".

"This is not merely a failure of the state police. This is a failure of governance," Abhishek Banerjee said.

He also alleged that the police had failed to protect TMC workers and the grieving family, and questioned whether political violence had become a tool of governance in the state.

Dola Sen questions law and order

Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said Mamata Banerjee had gone to meet the family of the TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody and questioned whether she should have been prevented from making the visit.

"Our worker died in police custody, an incident akin to a lockup death. His wife is a councillor. You tell me, as a matter of simple, natural justice, should our leader, Mamata Banerjee, not go to meet that family?" Sen said.

She alleged that stones and half-bricks were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle and claimed that BJP workers and police personnel were present at the spot.

"They attacked her in a targeted manner... BJP goons and police stood in front, throwing half-bricks and stones, cracking the glass of Didi's car," she alleged.

Sen also said Mamata Banerjee's visit was not a political programme but an attempt to meet the family of the deceased worker.

Mamata alleges attack could have caused serious injuries

Mamata Banerjee herself alleged that large stones were hurled at her car in front of police personnel and said the attack could have resulted in serious injuries or death.

"Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements, right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open. We could have all been killed," she said.

She also alleged that the police were providing protection to the BJP and said she had never witnessed such an incident before.

"This happened right in front of the police. I have never seen anything like this. What is going on?" she said.

"Chor bhagao" slogans were also heard from the crowd, according to ANI.

BJP denies involvement, condemns incident

West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya denied any BJP involvement in the alleged attack and condemned the throwing of stones or other objects at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle.

World.title: Punjab: AAP's youth wing holds marathon in Mohali
World.content:
The youth wing of the Punjab AAP on Sunday held the 'Punjab Youth Run 2026' marathon under the state government's anti-drug campaign, with party leaders urging participants to make fitness a regular part of their lives.

AAP's youth wing president and MLA Manjinder Singh Lalpura said that the marathon started from Gurdwara Sri Amb Sahib and witnessed enthusiastic participation from youngsters, sportspersons, women, senior citizens and people from different parts of Punjab.

Thanking the participants for turning up in large numbers, Lalpura said, "The response showed that the people of Punjab wanted to see a healthy, vibrant and drug-free Punjab.

The event was not merely a political programme but an initiative for Punjab and its people."

The youth wing will organise similar marathon events under its 'Yudh Nashian Virudh,' campaign in other parts of Punjab, including Amritsar, Patiala, Bathinda and Ludhiana, so that the message of fitness, sports and a drug-free Punjab can reach every corner of the state, Lalpura further said.

Highlighting the AAP government's focus on sports, AAP MP Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer said, "The state's sports budget has increased from around Rs 150 crore when I took charge of the sports department to approximately Rs 1,800 crore now."





This major increase reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that Punjab's youth have greater opportunities to participate in sports, he said.

Urging the participants to make fitness a regular part of their lives, Hayer said Do not treat the marathon as a one-day activity.

World.title: People of 'Devbhoomi' always stand firm on national duty, says CM Dhami; commends 'Tiranga Yatra' response
World.content:
Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday praised the people of Devbhoomi for their overwhelming response to the ongoing 'Tiranga Yatras' across the state, stating that the citizens of the state have always stood firm when it comes to national duty.

Speaking to the reporters, the chief minister said that the resolve to serve and protect the country remains deeply embedded in the hearts of the common people.

"This serves as proof that the common people of Devbhoomi Uttarakhand have never lagged behind when it comes to the nation, and this resolve remains strong in everyone's hearts today. We will always remain committed to the country's security, unity, and integrity, and this campaign will continue across the entire state right up to August 15th.

Tiranga Yatras will be organised in various places, further strengthening our collective resolve of patriotism," he said.

Earlier, CM Dhami participated in the 'Har Ghar Tiranga Yatra' organised in Dehradun ahead of the 80th

on August 15.

Speaking at the event, he emphasised that the nation is currently traversing through the pivotal phase of 'Amrit Kaal', establishing a robust and distinct identity on the global stage as a superpower.





"Today our country is passing through the Amrit Kaal. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the nation is establishing a new identity for itself on the global stage as a superpower. The India of today does not bow down to anyone; instead, it looks the world in the eye and speaks its mind. While India's economy is growing rapidly, the country is also scripting a new narrative of a self-reliant India, be it in the digital revolution, infrastructure development, or indigenous technology through the 'Make in India' initiative.

Today, we are not merely keeping pace with the world; we are leading it in numerous sectors and guiding the global community," Dhami said.

World.title: Mediating Telangana’s inter-State issues
World.content:
The Telangana Government is gearing up to present its views against the unauthorised projects taken up by the neighbouring State of Karnataka across the river Krishna to the Central Government.

The State is focussing on raising the disputes under Section 3 of the Inter State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 which allows it to complain to the Union Government in the event of river water disputes arising with neighbouring States. Telangana is firming up plans to furnish its views at the 31st Southern Zonal Council (SZC) meeting scheduled to be held at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu on August 20.

The Union Government has invited Telangana to attend the SZC meeting, claiming that it provides an excellent forum for deliberating upon and amicably resolving issues of mutual interest between the Centre and the States as well as among the States themselves. According to the agenda approved tentatively by the Union Home Ministry, the State Government will insist on its demand for conferment of national project status to the Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Projects. Interestingly, the agenda of the meeting indicates that the Karnataka Government is also planning to complain to the Centre about the new projects being taken up by Telangana.

The Karnataka Government has maintained that the liberty to use the remaining water in the Krishna river mentioned in the final order of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-II is not devolved upon Telangana and that the State could not take up any permanent construction to utilise the surplus waters.

Given the firm stances adopted by the two neighbouring States, the zonal council meeting is likely to witness heated arguments between the two sides if river water sharing forms part of the final agenda.

Slow progress

The Telangana Government is preparing detailed notes to present a strong case in support of its stand on major projects at the SZC meeting, which will be chaired by the Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Union Home Secretary. The planning department of the State has been directed to identify key inter-State and regional issues that require deliberations at the SZC meeting while the other departments have been instructed to prepare a list of pending issues so that inter-State issues can be put on fast track mode.

The departments are accordingly finalising Telangana’s agenda; the recommendations to be made at the council; and the State’s submissions regarding pending matters that require the Union Home Ministry’s approval.

Senior officials are however sceptical about the outcome of the SZC meetings as the resolution of pending issues has been relatively slow. Officials say that the focus of the previous meetings was on resolving the issues connected to the Central Government rather than issues pertaining to individual States. While the issues raised by Telangana in the past have been deliberated in the meetings of the standing committee, they were subsequently dropped.

For instance, the issue over a subsidy from the Centre between Telangana and Andhra Pradesh remains unresolved till date. The subsidy amount, which was due to both the States, was credited to the account of Andhra Pradesh. Telangana has been claiming a refund of its share which was considered positively by the SZC which directed Andhra Pradesh to credit the amount to Telangana. The latter is yet to release the amount along with the applicable interest to Telangana.

A similar conundrum is seen with the division of assets pertaining to institutions not listed anywhere in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014. Telangana is firm that only cash balances should be shared between the two States while institutions should be apportioned on a location basis. However, Andhra Pradesh, referring to Section 66 of the Act, is insisting that some of these institutions be included in Schedule IX or X.

It is better for the Union Home Ministry to take a serious view on addressing the issues raised by States so that they will be motivated to raise their issues at the national level rather than prolonging them. The Centre’s intervention for the speedy resolution of pending issues will go a long way in helping the States focus on issues which need immediate attention.

World.title: CPI(M) accuses UDF govt. of ‘surrendering’ to BJP over Vande Mataram order
World.content:
The CPI(M) on Sunday accused the UDF government of “surrendering to the BJP” after General Education Minister Shamsudheen defended the State government’s decision to implement Governor Rajendra Arlekar’s directive to sing the full version of Vande Mataram during Independence Day celebrations.

In a statement, K.V. Abdul Khader, secretary, CPI(M) Thrissur district committee, said the Minister’s reported remark that the State could not ignore the Raj Bhavan’s directive amounted to an admission that the UDF government was prepared to accept the Governor’s positions unquestioningly. “The Minister’s statement is proof that the UDF government has surrendered to the BJP,” the CPI(M) alleged.

Mr. Khader argued that the Governor, as the political nominee of the BJP-led Union government, was advancing the Centre’s agenda and that the State government’s decision to issue an official order based on his directive reflected a shift in its political stance.

The CPI(M) also targeted the government’s approach towards the Governor, alleging that the Chief Minister and his Cabinet had chosen not to confront Lok Bhavan and were instead implementing every directive issued by the Governor.

Drawing a comparison with the previous LDF administration led by Pinarayi Vijayan, Mr Khader claimed that it had consistently resisted what it described as the Governor’s “pro-BJP positions”, whereas the present government had taken the stand that the Governor’s directions could not be disregarded.

“If the government believes it cannot refuse the Governor’s directives, it would be better to hand over the administration to the Governor,” the CPI(M) said, describing the Minister’s remarks as “deceptive” and a betrayal of the government’s stated position.

World.title: Amit Shah’s helicopter diverted to IAF station due to heavy rain
World.content:
Due to heavy rain that lashed the city on Sunday afternoon, Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s helicopter, which was to land at the Chennai airport, was diverted to the Air Force Station at Tambaram.

Mr. Shah was scheduled to arrive from Puducherry at Chennai airport by an Indian Air Force (IAF) helicopter at 3.26 p.m., according to a statement from Airports Authority of India (AAI). However, the helicopter could not land at the airport due to adverse weather, and the helicopter with Mr. Shah on board and another were diverted to the Air Force Station.

The police informed AAI that Mr. Shah would reach Chennai airport by road. He departed for New Delhi from the airport by an IAF aircraft at 4.54 p.m.

“Despite the diversion of the helicopters, subsequent road movement and departure from Chennai Airport were carried out smoothly,” a statement said.

World.title: Orthodox, Jacobite priests and members clash at church
World.content:
Priests and members of the Orthodox and Jacobite factions of the Malankara Church clashed at St. John’s Bethlehem Church in Piramadom, near Muvattupuzha, on Sunday (August 9).

The clash erupted after members and priests of the Orthodox faction allegedly arrived at the church, claiming to have obtained a favourable court order regarding its ownership. The church was under the control of the Jacobite faction, the police said.

The Holy Mass led by a Jacobite priest was reportedly under way when members of the rival faction arrived with the court order. The police dispersed members of both factions to de-escalate the situation and temporarily locked the church as a preventive measure. Visuals showing priests from both factions pushing and shoving each other near the altar, while members of the factions intervened, were widely shared on social media.

Meanwhile, the district administration is expected to hold discussions with representatives of both factions on Monday (August 10).

World.title: India, U.S. navies to hold EOD exercise in Kochi from August 10
World.content:
The Indian Navy–U.S. Navy Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Exercise 2026 will be held at the Southern Naval Command here from August 10 to 14.

The bilateral exercise aims to enhance interoperability and strengthen professional cooperation between the specialist diving and EOD teams of the two navies, according to a communication.

The exercise is designed to promote collaborative learning and operational synergy, enabling personnel from both navies to refine procedures, improve mutual understanding and strengthen their ability to respond effectively to complex and evolving challenges, says an official press release.

The Indian Navy and the U.S. Navy have been conducting joint salvage and EOD exercises since 2005. The forthcoming engagement marks the eighth edition of the specialised bilateral training exercise. It underscores the enduring commitment of the two navies towards enhancing interoperability, sharing operational expertise and strengthening cooperation in specialised maritime operations, it says.

World.title: T.N. police arrest 837 cyber criminals in two days
World.content:
In a crackdown on cybercrime network, the Cyber Crime Wing (CCW) of the Tamil Nadu Police launched a 48-hour “State-wide Special Drive against Mule Account Holders” commencing on August 6, and arrested 837 cyber criminals across the State.

The operation was focused on identifying persons involved in opening, operating, and facilitating the misuse of bank accounts for receiving and withdrawing proceeds from cyber fraud.

Acting on the instructions of the Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, special teams of the CCW conducted the operation in all the districts and cities.

It was based on accused profiling through the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP) and the Pratibimb portal of the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

Financial data analysis done

The profiling was further strengthened through bank fund-trail linkages established by financial data analysis of cybercrime networks.

“Mule accounts are bank accounts used by cybercriminals to receive, transfer, layer, or withdraw money obtained through fraudulent and illegal activities. Individuals who allow their bank accounts to be used for such transactions facilitate the movement of illicit funds,” Dr. Aggarwal said.

Investigators targeted individuals linked to 9,804 complaints involving fraudulent transactions amounting to more than ₹545 crore, and arrested 837 cyber criminals involved in 601 cases. Also, 157 new FIRs were registered across the State to curb the operation of mule bank accounts for facilitating cyber fraud.

The police said 204 mobile phones and other storage devices, some cash, and bank documents were seized from the premises of the accused.

Dr. Aggarwal said the arrests marked a significant achievement in disrupting and dismantling the organised cybercrime network operating in Tamil Nadu.

The operation was directly supervised from the police headquarters by the Additional Director-General of Police, CCW, Bala Naga Devi, to ensure seamless coordination and real-time monitoring throughout the drive.

The police were analysing the digital evidence seized and interrogating the arrested persons to uncover layers of the criminal network and identify their associates operating in other States. Efforts were on to trace and apprehend other members of the network, recover defrauded funds, and establish wider linkages with nationwide cybercrime operations, the police said in a statement.

World.title: City hospital organises movie screening for Thalassemia warriors
World.content: Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Teynampet, organised a special screening of Spider-Man: Brand New Day at Kamala Cinemas for around 100 young “Thalassemia warriors” and their families and caregivers. A release from the hospital said, the choice of the movie was fitting as its story reflects courage, hope and the strength to overcome challenges. Revathi Raj, Senior Consultant – Paediatrics & Haematology Oncology, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Teynampet, said: “We wanted to give them a moment to forget the hospital, laugh freely and simply be children.” Ramya U., Consultant – Paediatric Haematology, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Teynampet, said: “Our Thalassemia Warriors show remarkable courage, and today is about celebrating their childhood, dreams and happiness.”

World.title: Singapenn marathon held in Chennai for awareness of cervical cancer
World.content:
Singappen Special Force chief K. Bhavaneeswari flagged off the Singappen marathon for creating awareness about cervical cancer and promoting the women safety helpline in the Marina Beach on Sunday. The marathon was held from Island Grounds to Light House.

The marathon, organised by the Rotary Club of Madras Central, InnerWheel Clubs of District 323 and the Singappen Special Force (SSF), saw the participation of more than 3,000 people.

Inaugurating the marathon, Ms. Bhavaneeswari emphasised the need for creating awareness among women for eradicating cervical cancer and also the need to strengthen women safety through the national women helpline no. 1091.

Nallammai Ramanathan, chairman of the Singappen Marathon, citing that the country accounts for 25% of the global cervical cancer deaths, said there is an urgent need for creating awareness and action against cervical cancer.

Sridhar Krishnaswamy, president of the Rotary Club of Madras Central, also participated.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact open to any other country in region, 'purely defensive': DPM Dar
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister said on Sunday that the defence pact signed between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

He also clarified that the agreement was “purely defensive” in nature.

The indication that an expansion of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi city on Friday, was possible came a day after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact.

The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Dar further elaborated on the pact, which he referred to as the Makkah Accord, in a post on X.

“The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement […] reflects the depth of the brotherly relations between the leadership and peoples of the three countries.

“The Makkah Accord is the culmination of years of discussions and coordination, with a common desire to strengthen strategic cooperation in addressing multifarious peace and security challenges and advancing regional peace, stability and prosperity,” he said.

He clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations.

Reiterating that any external armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all under the pact, he said it was consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

Moreover, he said, the accord was “purely defensive” in nature.

“It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.”

“The Makkah Accord remains open to any country in the region willing to uphold its fundamental principles and resolve differences through mutual respect, cooperation and peaceful means,” he said, adding that the pact was consistent with the fundamental pillars of Islamabad’s foreign policy.

“Pakistan looks forward to continuing to work closely with all brotherly countries in the region towards lasting peace and stability. We remain committed to advancing the cause of peaceful resolution of all conflicts and building a more secure, stable and prosperous future for our peoples,” he concluded.

Later in the day, Dar and Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand exchanged views on the regional situation, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Dar informed Anand of the “essence of the agreement and the joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

Egypt likely to join: Turkish FM

Earlier, on Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan also said he believed Egypt could join the pact once several technical issues were resolved.

“Egypt is already our natural partner on all issues. I believe that at the next stage, Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members. There are a few technical issues. Once these are implemented, there is no reason for Egypt not to be part of it,” he told Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu news agency.

Other countries had expressed interest in joining the agreement, but the founding members had debated how the expansion should be handled, he further stated.

Some countries that wanted to join asked not to be named, he said, adding that the preferred model was for Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to remain the three core founding countries, responsible for establishing the principles, standards and long-term structure of the alliance, while other countries could join with the approval of the core members.

“Under our president’s vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow,” Fidan said.

Fidan also said the initiative was broader than the traditional definition of the Middle East because of Pakistan’s participation.

Pakistan’s geographical position meant the initiative went beyond the conventional definition of the Middle East and represented a broader regional perspective.

‘Same as Nato’s Article 5’

Fidan further elaborated on this, saying the pact was technically the same as Nato’s Article 5 mutual defence agreement.

Article 5 of the North Atlantic alliance specifies that an attack on one ​of its members is an attack on all of them. It obliges allies to take action they deem necessary to assist the country under attack, including potentially the use of military force.

While the Makkah defence pact stipulates the same, Fidan explained that its text contained general commitments whose practical implementation would depend on discussions and decisions by relevant bodies.

A country would need to make a request for assistance and would determine the type of support it needs, he said, adding that the requests could be of different kinds, ranging from intelligence and logistics to ammunition or, if necessary, military units, depending on the scale of the threat.

The signatories, he said, would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of ​support they would ask for in the event of an attack, but that no country would be considered a ​threat as long as a member state is not attacked.

Fidan also said that the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support the three signatories’ security.

He further told Anadolu that discussions on the initiative began before the current war environment, when there was no US-Israel war on Iran and other regional countries had also been involved in the talks leading to the agreement.

Fidan said its signatories were countries that did not have expansionist policies. “They are countries concerned with their own borders, their own problems and their development, and, if possible, they want to contribute positively to their environment through good relations and good neighbourliness.“

The three countries, he said, had different styles and capacities, but when brought together, they naturally formed a defence-oriented organisation rather than an offensive one.

“It is not an approach of going on the offensive and saying, ‘Let’s do this or that together.’ Therefore, unless it is attacked by a country, whether from inside or outside the region, this alliance cannot have any dispute with any country. But, of course, the power composition we have put forward will make a constructive contribution to regional stability,” he said.

He termed the pact the “most important step” toward bringing lasting stability to this region.

How will the alliance function?

According to Fidan, the pact would be operational under a political and military committee comprising foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of general staff, similar to Nato structures.

The committee would translate the vision set by the leaders into decisions and carry out related work, while a secretariat would be established to implement those decisions, he explained.

“At the first committee meeting, ministers would likely present proposals to the leaders on the establishment, structure and functioning of the secretariat, as well as its initial tasks,” he said, adding that the pact would cover a broad range of military issues, including interoperability, or the ability of countries with different military structures to operate together. Other areas would include joint training, mutual support, logistics, threat assessments, intelligence sharing and, most importantly, defence industry cooperation.

He said the committee would meet at certain intervals during the year and that a permanent secretariat would be established in Saudi Arabia. The structure, functioning and additional units of the secretariat would be determined in discussions among the members.

Fidan added that joint exercises and training would be necessary to establish the ability of the countries to operate together.

“Because after a while you will see that when you find yourselves in a common combat scenario, how your weapons systems and communications systems will communicate with one another and how they will be compatible are important issues. These are the things that will be done after the secretariat is established,” he said.

He said standards would need to be developed and that analyses and assessments would also be carried out.

‘Support in the Muslim world and the West’

Fidan said the defence agreement had received strong support from countries in the Muslim world, including those that were not members but were nevertheless very pleased with the agreement.

He said there were also supporters in the West who understood the substance of the initiative.

“Especially in the Islamic world, there are many who strongly support this issue. There are also supporters in the West, among those who understand the essence of the matter. The way for the Middle East to cease being a place that produces problems for humanity and the international community and instead become a place that creates added value with everything it possesses is through implementing constructive alliances of this kind,” Fidan said.

Fidan said the leadership of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had created significant regional and global expectations and that officials now had the responsibility to fill those expectations professionally.

“Our responsibility, in the positions we hold, is to recognise that the political will put forward by the leadership of the three countries has created a very significant regional and global expectation. We need to fill that expectation very professionally, move forward step by step and make it work. We have begun doing this, and God willing, we will continue,” he said.

The signing of the accord comes at a time of heightened regional tensions, with Pakistan seeking to balance ties with Middle Eastern and Western partners.

Analysts say many in the region view the development as a step toward Gulf states taking greater responsibility for their own security.

Israel’s increasingly aggressive military posture in recent years has also emerged as an important factor shaping how Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye perceive the regional security environment, they added.

For decades, Saudi Arabia has relied heavily on its strategic relationship with the United States for its security. Experts note the new agreement does not replace Washington, but it does create an additional security pillar.

“The regional states are not seeking to sever ties with Washington, but neither do they want to entrust their security exclusively to American guarantees,” one analyst said.

Additional input from Syed Irfan Raza

World.title: Sindh govt decides judicial commission to probe Mir Raza Ali murder case
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to seek a judicial commission to probe the killing of 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali, Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Sunday.

Ali’s body was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

However, after injury details from a second postmortem ruled out the possibility of suicide, a murder charge was added to the case on Sunday.

“A decision has been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry into the murder case of Mir Raza Ali Khan,” the Sindh home minister said in a statement issued by his office.

According to the statement, Lanjar, along with Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, visited Ali’s residence to meet his parents. They assured the family that they would be provided complete justice.

Lanjar said the judicial commission would be constituted under the leadership of a Sindh High Court judge on the recommendation of the Sindh chief minister.

During the meeting, Lanjar briefed Ali’s parents in detail about the progress of the case and the investigation, the statement said.

“The investigation team will maintain full contact and cooperation with the deceased’s parents,” the minister was quoted as saying. “A transparent and impartial investigation into the case will be ensured.”

He affirmed that all requirements of justice would be fulfilled and no leniency would be shown to anyone responsible.

Meanwhile, the Karachi mayor noted that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah chaired a four-hour-long meeting during which “all aspects of the incident and the investigation were reviewed in detail”.

The decision of a judicial inquiry comes after Faryal Talpur, the chairperson of Sindh Assembly’s Standing Committee on Home, recommended that CM Murad constitute a judicial commission for a “transparent, impartial and comprehensive investigation” into the case.

Taking notice of Ali’s murder, she said the proposed commission should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

“Legal and disciplinary action should be taken without discrimination against those found responsible in light of the commission’s findings,” Talpur added.

She further stressed that justice for the victim’s family must be ensured at all costs and that the public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case.

“No negligence or bias will be tolerated in meeting the requirements of justice,” she said, adding that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system were fundamental responsibilities of the government and relevant institutions.

2 officers suspended

Separately, Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan ordered the immediate suspension of Sharea Faisal sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi.

They were suspended over “failure to preserve the crime scene and carry out proper crime scene investigation”, AIG Khan told Dawn.

According to a statement released by his office, the additional IG also ordered SHO Qureshi’s reversion to a lower rank.

“The full implementation of rules, regulations and accountability principles in departmental affairs would be ensured,” the statement said.

“Action will be taken in accordance with the law and rules in case of any violation of discipline by an officer.”

New police team for probe

Earlier on Sunday, an order released by the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death.

It also showed that the murder charge had been added to the first information report (FIR) on his father’s complaint.

The order, seen by Dawn, said the new investigating team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem, to “supervise the investigation of FIR no. 795/2026 u/s 365/ 302/ 201 of the PPC”.

Initially, the FIR was registered only under Section 365 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), which pertains to kidnapping.

Of the newly added provisions, Section 302 pertains to murder and Section 201 to hiding the evidence of an offence or giving false information to screen the offender.

The case would now be probed by a five-member team led by Sindh Deputy IG (Crime and Investigation) Amir Farooqui and comprising Rapid Response Force Al-Falah SSP Syed Muhammad Ali Raza, Korangi SP (Investigation) Qais Khan, Central SP (Investigation) Anam Tajjamul and Zaman Town SIO Ch. Ghazanfar, the police order said.

It added: “The team shall undertake a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the case from all relevant angles. The team shall identify, collect, preserve and examine any new or additional evidence and shall thoroughly examine and analyse all physical, technical, circumstantial and forensic evidence collected during the investigation.

“The team shall make all out efforts to work out the case and submit a report to the court concerned within the stipulated period. The team may co-opt any officer to assist in the investigation. Progress shall be reported on a day-to-day basis.”

On Saturday, the lawyer for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, had demanded that the first investigation probing the case be replaced, after a fresh post-mortem examination conducted following the exhumation of Ali’s body found that he had been shot in the back — evidence that ruled out the possibility of suicide.

Speaking to the media, he reiterated the allegation that Ali had been tortured before being murdered.

“This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged.

The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”.

Advocate Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed.

Controversy over autopsy

Ali, an Institute of Business Administration graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

The latest developments in his case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board.

However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

On Friday morning, Ali’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was deferred after they objected ti the new board. Standing alongside Ali’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board on Friday, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday.

After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn, “We have collected samples for identification, chemical analysis and gunshot residue. The cause of death is reserved for laboratory reports.”

Regarding the autopsy, she said that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said.

She said the body bore “injuries in right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in mouth and throat”.

World.title: Pakistan to partner with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar on oil storage scheme
World.content:
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Sunday said plans were underway to launch a scheme with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar for oil storage to strengthen energy security.

Pakistan has been planning to boost domestic storage for crude oil and refined products to increase its energy security, it emerged in May. With no strategic petroleum reserves, the country has been left exposed to oil supply shocks resulting from the US-Iran war that has choked supplies through the Strait of Hormuz .

Addressing a press conference in Lahore today, Malik said: “I am grateful to the governments of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar that we will have a bonded scheme with them, under which these countries will store their oil on the secure territories of Pakistan at their own cost, and supply to the entire world from here.”

He added that Pakistan will have the right that in the case of a conflict, it could “buy those resources from them by paying for them and fulfil our needs”.

The minister said the “commercial bonded scheme drafted with the help of Aramco and other major companies” has been forwarded to the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) upon the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

“When, God-willing, a decision is made on it next week, you will see the progress,” he added, asserting that Pakistan’s energy needs will be fulfilled “without spending money and despite a lack of resources”.

The US-Israel war on Iran has caused oil supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively blockaded, leading to unprecedented hikes in petroleum prices.

The minister said the government was committed to strengthening energy security. He noted that $500 million were required for storing crude oil reserves for one month, in addition to $300-400m needed for an underground storage system.

He said the government would later debate whether the country could invest this amount, adding that the leadership would work on it in the upcoming months.

Highlighting Pakistan’s energy challenges, Malik said the country imported around 90 per cent of its energy requirements, while domestic oil production stood at approximately 70,000 barrels per day against a daily demand of around 500,000 barrels.

He stressed the need to accelerate indigenous oil and gas exploration to reduce reliance on imports.

He said the prime minister and the field marshal had tasked a leading international company with preparing a comprehensive roadmap for the country’s energy sector, which would be presented to the national leadership in the coming months.

Malik also said Turkiye’s Turkish Petroleum would soon commence offshore drilling operations in Pakistan’s territorial waters, paving the way for significant foreign investment in the energy sector.

He announced that tenders for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) would open on Monday and said the government had made arrangements to issue new gas connections to facilitate consumers.

Speaking on international developments, Malik said that despite economic pressures from the US-Iran war, the government ensured uninterrupted fuel supplies across the country and made “every effort” to protect consumers from the full impact of rising global prices.

The minister said the government remained committed to providing maximum relief to the public despite limited financial resources.

He added that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had introduced a transparent petroleum pricing mechanism, with all pricing calculations available on the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority’s (Ogra) website.

Since mid-July, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices as hostilities between the US and Iran renewed. Before that, petroleum prices were revised weekly since the war began, alongside measures for conserving fuel.

Recalling that the federal cabinet had approved a refinery policy last month, Malik affirmed that the government was resolving long-standing financial issues facing the petroleum sector.

He added that the flow of circular debt had been halted and efforts were underway to clear outstanding liabilities inherited from previous administrations.

World.title: Movement restricted under Section 144 in some areas of South Waziristan, Tank on Monday
World.content:
